$comment: READ THIS BEFORE YOU CHANGE A `value`. This file is read at RUNTIME by all four
repos: the compiled engine carries a copy, and it REFUSES TO CONSTRUCT when the two
disagree. So a value edit and `maturin develop --release` are ONE STEP. Between them,
every other session's engine is down -- not slow, down, with `RustEngine()` raising.
That happened twice in twenty minutes on 2026-09-22, and the second time was twenty
minutes after the rule was written into a log, which is why it is written here instead:
nobody reads history before editing a file. `tests/test_ledger_build_step.py` fails the
moment the two disagree, so run the suite and you will trip over it before anyone else
does. Adding a KEY counts: an engine built without it refuses just as loudly.
THE CALIBRATION REGISTRY. Every physics constant in the engine lives here, and
every one of them carries how well it is known. Nothing in the Rust core or the
Python layer may hardcode a number that appears in this file.
WHY: this project's predecessor stalled for weeks trying to make pathfinding
match the real game. The cause was not difficulty -- it was that plausible
numbers and measured numbers were stored the same way, so a wrong guess was
indistinguishable from a fact and later tuning absorbed the error instead of
revealing it. A constant fitted to the one case anybody checked makes a wrong
LAW read as right, on every board at once.
STATUS VALUES, in increasing order of trust:
guess        nobody has evidence; a placeholder so the engine runs
disputed_existence  the key names something no shipped data or recording shows
exists; ranked with guess, because nobody has evidence either way
hypothesis   an argument from data shape, not an observation
community    multiple independent third parties agree, no primary source
third_party_measured  one outside measurement, its source, method and sample named,
not reproduced by this project's own instruments. Ranked WITH community
and never overwrite-protected, so this project's own measurement replaces
it without --supersede. Added 2026-09-24: two outside readings had been
filed as measured, which protected them against the very correction
that should replace them.
datamined    taken from shipped game data (state the file and the vintage)
measured     observed in the real game in this project's own recorded traces
owner_ruling a first-hand observation of the live game by a maintainer,
quoted verbatim and dated. Ranked WITH measured, never below it:
a direct observation of the live 2026 game, which is the target,
is a primary source. Added 2026-09-17, because
filing the Log ruling as 'community' would have made it
indistinguishable from the fandom prose it overturned -- exactly
the confusion this registry exists to prevent. Like measured, it
cannot be overwritten with a different value without --supersede.
A ruling may settle only PART of a key (the Log's sign, not its
off-axis vector); say which part in confidence, and keep a
promotion_rule for the rest.
PROMOTION RULE: a constant may only be promoted by adding evidence, never by
an engine result looking right. If the sim matches reality with a 'guess' in
it, that is a coincidence until measured, and saying so costs nothing.

meta.target_note: The LIVE 2026 game was chosen over a frozen 2023 build. Consequence: every datamined constant below is from 2016-2018 or 2023 game data and is therefore EVIDENCE, NOT SPEC. Supercell rewrote ground pathfinding on 2025-03-31; anything tagged pre-2025 about movement is archaeology until re-measured.

SUBTILE_PER_TILE.provenance: Design choice, following cr-sim. NOT a game constant.
rationale: This number is chosen so that it cannot bake in the answer to the two
biggest open questions (tick rate, speed divisor). Under EVERY candidate
hypothesis, a unit's per-tick displacement is an exact integer:
Speed is tiles/min, 20 TPS -> Speed * 15 subtiles/tick
Speed is tiles/min, 30 TPS -> Speed * 10 subtiles/tick
Speed is tiles/min, 60 TPS -> Speed *  5 subtiles/tick
18000 = 1000 * 18, so one millitile (the unit ALL shipped distances use)
is exactly 18 subtiles and no game data value ever needs rounding.
Consequence: we can run at 20 TPS and re-run at 60 TPS and any divergence
is a real signal rather than a rounding artefact.
SUBTILE_PER_TILE.promotion_rules: Not promotable -- it is ours, not Supercell's. Revisit only if a measured per-tick displacement is not an integer multiple of 1/18000 tile.

MILLITILE_PER_TILE.provenance: All distance columns in characters.csv/buildings.csv are millitiles. Cross-checked against community tile values across dozens of cards: Knight SightRange 5500 = 5.5 tiles, CollisionRadius 500 = 0.5, Mini P.E.K.K.A 450 = 0.45, Mortar/X-Bow Range 11500 = 11.5.
MILLITILE_PER_TILE.promotion_rules: Already as good as it gets from data and traces.

POSITION_TYPE.provenance: Community projects report entity positions as raw i32. The internal SCALE is unknown; we choose our own (above) and do not claim it matches.
POSITION_TYPE.note: Arena max is 32 tiles * 18000 = 576000, far inside i32. Squared distances reach 3.3e11 and MUST use i64 -- an i32 squared-distance is a silent overflow bug.
POSITION_TYPE.promotion_rules: Not observable in a trace; out of scope.

TICK_MS.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. The free per-unit speed fit (no card table, S in 1..5000, synth_adjudicate B2) has exactly one survivor per card and every unit of a card fits the same integer, which only happens when one trace frame is one logic tick; at 2-5 sub-steps per tick no integer speed survives at all. The stomp pause schedule ((k+1)*TICK_MS) mod (Stop+Wait) > Stop reproduces Giant 308/308 and Golem 306/306 moving ticks with TICK_MS = 50 and no phase offset.

disagreement.30_TPS_33ms: the old engine in legacy/ used dt=0.033 (and not even exactly 1/30).

TICK_MS.why_it_matters: Every interaction is a function of this: body-block timing, whether a Fireball lands before a unit crosses, how many tower hits a Hog gets. A 3x error here is absorbed into fitted card constants and never shows up as itself.
TICK_MS.promotion_rules: SETTLED by the 15.535.29 measurements. Re-open only against a second independent trace capture, never against an argument from data shape.
TICK_MS.engine_contract: Read from here. Never write `50` in engine code.

history.provenance: No primary source exists. This is the single most load-bearing unknown in the engine.
history.overturned_by: the 15.535.29 traces advance the battle by one logic tick per 50 ms of shipped DeployTime/HitSpeed: every measured per-tick speed is an integer number of millitiles and the stomp phase (Giant 308/308, Golem 306/306) only closes at TICK_MS = 50.

struck.60_TPS_16.67ms: STRUCK. Its arithmetic is wrong: PhoenixNoRespawn DeployTime 733 ms is 733/16.667 = 43.98 ticks at 60 Hz, not 44 -- the argument needs 733.33. Lightning HitSpeed = 460 is a whole number of ticks at none of 50, 33.3 or 16.67 ms, so 'shipped durations are whole ticks' is void in either direction. Overturned by the 15.535.29 measurement above in any case.

SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.units: multiplier applied to the Speed column
SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. Free integer per-unit fit over every moving tick of every unit (synth_adjudicate B2, no card table, S in 1..5000): exactly one survivor per card and every unit of a card fits it -- Knight 60 (131 units), Giant 52 (12), Golem 54, Skeletons 90 (3), MiniPekka 90, HogRider 120. Those are the raw Speed column values themselves (Giant 45 and Golem 45 after the StopMovementAfterMS/WaitMS rule, movement.STOMP_SPEED_RULE), i.e. Speed is millitiles per tick exactly. 1 millitile = 18 subtiles, so subtiles_per_tick = Speed * 18.
SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.why_it_matters: A flat 20% error on the movement speed of every unit in the game.
SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.promotion_rules: SETTLED. The former value is in `history` and the two former hypotheses are in `struck` with their original arguments, the same way time.TICK_MS archives its refuted entry -- a promotion adds evidence, it never deletes it. A buffed speed (SpeedMultiplier) follows the SAME law with a larger integer S: data/oracle-native/rage/Knight_rage_seed2.jsonl.gz fits S = 60 on t121..155, S = 78 on t156..217 (the Rage) and S = 60 again on t218..340, and 78 = 60 x 1.3 exactly. Its ROUNDING is still unmeasured, because 60 x 1.3 is a whole number and floor/round/truncate/ceil all give 78 -- see movement.STOMP_SPEED_RULE.
SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.engine_contract: subtiles_per_tick = Speed * SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK. Set to 10 for 30 TPS, 5 for 60 TPS, 18 for the millitile-per-tick reading.

history.provenance: Derived: assumes Speed is tiles/minute AND TICK_MS=50. Speed 60 (Medium) -> 1.0 tiles/s.
history.overturned_by: the 15.535.29 measurements: Speed is millitiles per 50 ms tick (divide_by_50), so one Speed unit is 18 subtiles per tick, not 15.

SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.resolves: divide_by_50 vs divide_by_60: divide_by_50 is correct. Medium (Speed 60) is 1.20 tiles/s, not 1.00.

struck.divide_by_60: STRUCK 2026-09-18 by the 15.535.29 measurements. Its argument was: 'Speed is tiles/minute. Medium (60) = 1.00 tiles/s. Supported by cr-sim's exact-at-60TPS derivation and by the highest-sample community VOD medians (skeletons 1.56 at Speed 90, hog 1.45 at Speed 120).' Overturned because the free per-unit integer fit's survivors ARE the raw Speed column (Knight 60, Giant 52, Golem 54, Skeletons 90, MiniPekka 90, HogRider 120) at TICK_MS = 50, i.e. one Speed unit is one millitile per 50 ms tick; at 60 TPS the same fit has no integer survivor.
struck.divide_by_50: UPHELD 2026-09-18, and now measured rather than argued. Its argument was: 'Speed is millitiles per 50ms tick. Medium (60) = 1.20 tiles/s. Architecturally cleaner. Matches lower-sample VOD medians (musketeer 1.20, knight 1.12 at Speed 60).' Kept here because the entry it lived in was deleted on promotion; the evidence that settled it is in `provenance`.

PROJECTILE_SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.provenance: MEASURED on the live 16.402 effects stream (every projectile object on every frame of the captures): the princess tower's arrow (TowerPrincessProjectile Speed 600) advances 599-600 native per tick on 293 consecutive steps of capture 20260920-003751-B and 688 of 20260920-081819-B, the king tower's (Speed 1000) 999-1000, the Musketeer's (Speed 1000) 1000, the Bomber's (Speed 400) 399-400, the Cannon's (Speed 500) 499-500 -- one projectile Speed unit is one native millitile per 50 ms tick, the troop unit (18 subtiles), not 15. History: hypothesis 15 (2026-09-13) mirrored a 'tiles/min at 20 TPS' reading; the AesDragon wiki blog's assertion and the Darknighture frame test (x1.2 for both a Musketeer projectile and a Giant) were right.

history.provenance: Mirrors time.SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK (Speed = tiles/min at 20 TPS). Community: the AesDragon wiki blog ASSERTS (unmeasured) that projectile Speed uses the troop unit; a Darknighture frame test (2023) measured x1.2 (Speed/50) for BOTH a Musketeer projectile and a Giant. No source was found for a 'troops /50, projectiles /60' split. crforge and legacy/ use /60 for both. Kept as its own key so a recording can split projectiles from troops without a code change (docs/spell-spec.md, projectile and rolling families).

PROJECTILE_SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.units: subtiles per tick per raw projectile Speed unit
PROJECTILE_SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.applies_to: EVERY projectile: troop and tower projectiles (combat.rs fire) and spell projectiles (spell.rs), including The Log's airborne and rolling phases
PROJECTILE_SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.promotion_rules: Time a Goblin Barrel from release to landing, Blue king centre to enemy princess centre (23.16 tiles: 3.474 s at 15, 2.895 s at 18), or a live Log roll from first contact to despawn (3.03 s vs 2.525 s). Split from the troop key only if the projectile measurement disagrees with the troop measurement beyond frame error.

arena.$comment: NOT stored here. Derived from the shipped tilemap by tools/extract_arena.py into data/derived/arena.json, and gated there. Hardcoding arena geometry is what made the old engine wrong about the river, the bridges and the king footprint all at once.

ARENA_SOURCE_VINTAGE.caveat: The modern client no longer ships a Map section -- the battlefield moved out of data and into code. The 2016-era per-arena data sets show TWO geometries (2-tile bridges in most arenas, 3-tile in Legendary/Royal), so bridge width is arena-dependent and possibly changed since. An 0.5-tile error in bridge span is about one Knight hitbox and decides every bridge body-block.
ARENA_SOURCE_VINTAGE.promotion_rules: Re-measure against a screenshot of the live arena with a calibrated tile overlay.

TERRITORY_MODEL.provenance: data/raw/retroroyale-2018/csv_logic/buildings.csv NoDeploySizeW / NoDeploySizeH, ~2018 client data (PRE-2025; evidence, not spec). The columns are set on exactly three rows: KingTower (18, 16), PrincessTower (11, 21) and NOTINUSE21, a disused copy of the king (18, 16). Carried into data/derived/cards.json towers[].no_deploy_size_tiles by tools/extract_cards.py.
TERRITORY_MODEL.rule: A TROOP may not be placed at a point inside the closed axis-aligned rectangle, centred on the tower centre with half-extents NoDeploySizeW/2 and NoDeploySizeH/2 tiles, of any ALIVE ENEMY crown tower; plus the tilemap WATER and NO_DEPLOY bits, arena bounds, building footprints, and the river band (never troop territory, see open_question). Buildings stay own half only (unsourced, unchanged). Spells anywhere.
TERRITORY_MODEL.unit_inference: TILES, inferred from 4 of 4 landmarks that come out exact under that reading and 0 of 4 under the half-tile reading, against the independently derived data/derived/arena.json and the princess tower centre (3.5, 6.5): (1) the king rect spans x = [0, 18], exactly the arena width; (2) the left and right princess rects (x = 3.5 +- 5.5 and 14.5 +- 5.5) meet exactly at x = 9, the centre line; (3) and (4) each princess rect's far edge (y = 6.5 + 10.5 = 17) is exactly the far river bank. tools/check_data.py gates all four.
TERRITORY_MODEL.consequence: With every enemy tower up, the rects forbid everything from the near river bank onward. When one enemy princess falls, the ground that opens on that side is between the far river bank (y = 17) and the enemy king rect (y = 21): 8 half-rows (4 tiles), x from the side wall to the centre line.
TERRITORY_MODEL.open_question: The four dry bridge half-columns (rows 15-17) are marked neither WATER nor NO_DEPLOY in the tilemap, so the rects alone would open them once that lane's princess falls. The engine keeps the river band closed to troops, carried from the previous rule WITHOUT a source. A recording of a troop placement attempt on the bridge after a princess tower falls settles it.

history.provenance: NONE. A pocket-depth constant in crates/royalesim/src/arena.rs: after a princess tower fell, troop territory reached 12 half-rows (6 tiles) past the far river bank on that engine-column side. Not in globals.csv, locations.csv, arenas.csv, game_modes.csv or the tilemap; chosen only to equal protocol.py MOCK_POCKET_DEPTH_HALF_ROWS. Before it, the engine used the far bank up to the destroyed tower's centre row (8.5 tiles), equally unsourced.
history.overturned_by: buildings.csv NoDeploySizeW/H on the crown towers, read as tiles: 4 of 4 arena landmarks exact (see unit_inference). The shipped mechanic replaces the depth; the depth was not tuned to 8.

TERRITORY_MODEL.promotion_rules: Record the DEEPEST legal troop placement on one lane after that lane's enemy princess tower falls (drag a troop card forward until the placement indicator refuses). This model predicts the limit at the enemy king rect edge, 4 tiles past the far river bank; the old 12-half-row model predicts 6 tiles, 2 tiles deeper. Also record whether the bridge accepts a troop then (open_question).

ADD_CHARACTER_RANGE_TO_RADIUS.provenance: globals.csv, present in both 1.3.2 and modern data sets.
ADD_CHARACTER_RANGE_TO_RADIUS.meaning: Range is measured EDGE to EDGE, not centre to centre: in_range = centre_distance <= range + target.collision_radius. The old engine used centre-to-centre only, so every melee unit under-reached.
ADD_CHARACTER_RANGE_TO_RADIUS.open: Whether the ATTACKER's own collision radius is also added: SETTLED by targeting.ATTACK_RANGE_RULE -- it is (measured: the live Prince, Range 1600 and CollisionRadius 600, stops 3135 native from a princess tower's centre, CollisionRadius 1000, the first step inside 3200; under Range + the target's radius alone it would walk on to 2600).

ATTACK_RANGE_RULE.confidence: HIGH -- three independent stop distances and a tower acquisition tick of the live corpus, each one walking step wide, all inside the both-radii sum and all outside the target-radius-only sum
ATTACK_RANGE_RULE.provenance: MEASURED on the live 16.402 corpus (the reach gap of the corpus report): the Prince (Range 1600, CollisionRadius 600) of capture 20260920-003751 stops 3135 native from the princess tower's centre (CollisionRadius 1000) and the one of 20260920-002736 at 3133, never inside 3126 -- the first step inside 3200 = Range + own R + the tower's R, 600 short of the 2600 the target-radius-only sum gives; the Dark Prince (Range 1200) stops at 2776, inside 2800, not 2200; the princess tower (Range 7500, R 1000) acquires the Prince on the tick after it steps inside 9100 (t279 at 9009 -> attacking at t280), not at 8500. THE RULE (target.rs in_attack_range): a target is in range when the centre distance is <= Range + the ATTACKER's CollisionRadius + the TARGET's CollisionRadius; the sight scan sums SightRange the same way (with EXTRA_SIGHT_RANGE_TO_CROWN_TOWERS / _TO_BUILDING by the candidate's kind); MinimumRange adds the lower bound (R + minRange). The goal cell of the walk stays Range + own R to the target's CENTRE (pathfinding.PATH_SEARCH), so a unit stops walking EARLIER than its goal cell: its attack sees the target in range at Range + own R + target R.
ATTACK_RANGE_RULE.meaning: range_plus_both_radii: a target is in range when the centre distance is <= Range + the ATTACKER's CollisionRadius + the TARGET's CollisionRadius (the same sum, with SightRange, for the sight scan and the keep-target / cancel-hit extensions). range_plus_target_radius: the earlier engine -- Range + the target's radius only, so every unit walked its own radius too far (a Prince 600 native past where the game stops it) and every tower acquired a unit its radius too late.
ATTACK_RANGE_RULE.promotion_rules: Measured; re-open only against a live capture whose stop distance parts from Range + both radii by more than one walking step.
ATTACK_RANGE_RULE.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json -> attack_range_rule); target.rs in_attack_range takes the attacker's radius and adds it under the shipped arm (every caller: combat.rs attack_step, the Path phase's attacking test, the sight scan, keep-target, the lock hold, the wake trigger); the goal reach was already Range + own R. The old arm stays runnable as range_plus_target_radius (the regression plant reach_without_own_radius forces it). tests/reach.rs pins the stop distances from the card data.

EXTRA_SIGHT_RANGE_TO_CROWN_TOWERS.open: Direction is ambiguous: extra range for TOWERS acquiring units, or for units acquiring TOWERS? Nobody established which.

LOGIC_RANGE_EXTENSION_TO_KEEP_TARGET.provenance: globals.csv of an UNVENDORED 2023 data, per recon. NOT PRESENT in the vendored 2018 globals.csv (data/raw/retroroyale-2018). Reported during 2026-09-12 recon as read from a newer globals.csv (a 2023 data) that this repo does not vendor, so nothing in the tree backs it. extract_globals.py lists it ABSENT on every run, deliberately.
LOGIC_RANGE_EXTENSION_TO_KEEP_TARGET.meaning: Retarget hysteresis: a unit keeps its current target until the target is this much beyond range. Without it, units at the range boundary oscillate between targets every tick.

history.provenance: globals.csv
history.overturned_by: extract_globals.py 2026-09-13: key absent from the vendored globals.csv the provenance cited

LOGIC_RANGE_EXTENSION_TO_KEEP_TARGET.promotion_rules: Vendor the data it came from and let extract_globals.py cross-check it, or measure retarget hysteresis at the range boundary.

supersedes: keep, status hypothesis, shipped until 2026-09-26 (flipped together with pathfinding.GOAL_TARGET_POSITION, pathfinding.FLYER_GOAL_WATER, movement.ATTACK_FACING, targeting.SPAWNED_UNIT_ACQUIRE_DELAY, spawner.SPAWNED_FIRST_STEP, targeting.DOOMED_TARGET_DROP and movement.WAITING_HEADING). Its confidence: 'LOW for the shipped arm keep, which is today's engine: a walking Minion keeps a target that a tower arrow in flight will kill, a Minion in its windup fires at it, and a crown tower in its windup keeps it. HIGH for projectile_attackers on client 15.535.29: 62 of 62 drops over 40 scenario runs, the ETA gate seen on both sides by 28 attackers, and 1,362 of 1,362 keeps by attackers that had fired; OPEN on a fired attacker out of reach, on melee attackers' first swing and on targets that are not troops'

"projectile_attackers", status measured, shipped until the 2026-09-26 integration flip (RoyaleSim fc3a790). Its confidence: 'HIGH. An attacker with a projectile that has not fired at its target drops a doomed target on the next tick: 62 of 62 in 40 runs, where doomed means the pending damage (crown arrows included) is at least its hitpoints, with ETA at most 600 ms. None of the 62 took it back. 44 of 44 ticks with lethal damage 650-750 ms away were keeps. A walking Knight and a walking Ronin keep a doomed target. All client 15.535.29 scenario runs.'. Its provenance: 'MEASURED on client 15.535.29, the per-frame records of the 15.535.29 scenario runs (435 runs read). DOOMED: a unit whose pending damage (the projectiles flying at it) is at least its hitpoints, with the pending damage's ETA at most 600 ms, both read at the end of the previous tick. (1) An attacker with a projectile that has not fired at its target drops a doomed target on the next tick: 62 of 62 cases in 40 runs, 14 walking Minions (the Minions-walking, attack, slow-arrow and fast-arrow scenarios and a Phoenix scenario) and 48 in their windup, not yet fired: princess towers 19, Musketeer 11, Goblin Hut Spear Goblins 10, Cannon 4, Minions 3, Mother Witch 1. Every one of the 62 targets was a troop. 2 of the drops (two walking Minions at a Phoenix, hp 317) came when only the sum of two shots in flight (217 and 107) was lethal. None took the doomed unit back while it lived; the new target was a tower (38) or another unit (24). 29 of the drops read an ETA of exactly 600, so the gate is <= 600, not < 600. No attacker dropped a target on the frame the doom first showed: the drop always comes one tick later. (2) The ETA gate: 44 of 44 ticks on which such an attacker's target had lethal pending damage 650-750 ms away were keeps, and 28 attackers were seen on both sides (keep while the ETA read above 600, drop the tick after it read 600). (3) An attacker with a projectile that has fired at its target and is in reach keeps it until it dies: 1,362 of 1,362 ticks over 219 attacker-target pairs (towers, Minions, Musketeer, Mother Witch, Hunter, Cannon and others). (4) An attacker without a projectile keeps a doomed target: 160 of 160 ticks over 34 pairs, among them a walking Ronin (12 ticks, 2 targets) and a walking Knight (4 ticks), a Knight and an Inferno Tower attacking, an Electro Wizard; the ranged ones (Inferno Tower 76, Electro Wizard 4) kept on 80 of 80 ticks. Not scoped: a fired attacker out of reach (3 Minion drops at 3757-3934 and an Electro Dragon drop; 12 keeps by a Mother Witch 62-147 out, a Minion 15 out and a tower). The engine before this key flipped keeps every doomed target. Pre-scored 2026-09-26 on RoyaleSim 8648486, alone: corpus +710 / -25 / +204 (124946 +579, 072148 A and B +53 and +72, 090825-B +6), sweep 0. With the other six keys (window AV, RoyaleSim 1c75632): corpus +2,839, sweep +3,197.'
DOOMED_TARGET_DROP.confidence: HIGH. An attacker with a projectile that has not fired at its target drops a doomed target on the next tick (62 of 62 in 40 client 15.535.29 scenario runs), and a re-evaluation never takes a doomed unit, even one the attacker has shot at: 4 of 4 launches from beyond reach at a doomed target were followed by a drop and none was retaken, while 245 of 245 launches in reach kept it, and 64 of 64 re-evaluations after a launch beyond reach at a target that was not doomed returned it.
DOOMED_TARGET_DROP.measured_2026_09_26: MEASURED on client 15.535.29, the per-frame records of the 15.535.29 scenario runs (775 runs read): an attacker with a projectile that LAUNCHED at its target from beyond its reach (Range + both radii + 25, LOGIC_RANGE_EXTENSION_TO_KEEP_TARGET) re-evaluates its target on the next tick, and the re-evaluation does not take a doomed unit, even the one it has just shot at. (1) 4 of 4 launches beyond reach at a doomed target were followed by a drop on the next tick, and none of the four took the target back while it lived: three Minions at a Knight 257, 362 and 434 beyond reach (the three runs of the Minions-at-a-walking-Knight scenario; the Knight had 155 or 46 hp against 216 or 107 in flight) and an Electro Dragon at a Skeleton 952 beyond. Each was attacking on the launch tick and walking on the next, with attack progress 0, toward a crown tower. (2) Control: a launch beyond reach at a target that was NOT doomed and was in sight returned that target on the next tick 64 of 64 times (Archers 19, Mega Minions 5, Minions 40); at a troop out of sight the target was not kept, 11 of 11 (princess towers 8, Musketeers 3, one of them taking a Cannon nearer). (3) Control: a launch within reach + 25 at a doomed target kept it on the next tick 245 of 245 times (princess towers 191, Mother Witch 14, Musketeer 13, Cannon 10 and others), among them a Minion 15 beyond reach, inside the 25. This settles the 'fired attacker out of reach' left open when the key flipped: the four drops were these launches, and all twelve keeps were attackers still in their attack on the next tick, attack progress running on.
DOOMED_TARGET_DROP.meaning_projectile_attackers_rescan: projectile_attackers_rescan: as projectile_attackers, except that the exemption for a unit the attacker has launched at covers KEEPING it only. Whenever the attacker re-evaluates its target (its current target left the keep test, or it launched at it from beyond Range + both radii + 25), the candidates exclude every doomed unit, the one it has shot at included, so it drops a doomed target it can no longer keep and does not take it back while it lives. An attacker that keeps its target without a re-evaluation (in reach, or inside the hold of a started hit) still keeps a doomed unit it has shot at.
DOOMED_TARGET_DROP.provenance: MEASURED on client 15.535.29, the per-frame records of the 15.535.29 scenario runs (435 runs read). DOOMED: a unit whose pending damage (the projectiles flying at it) is at least its hitpoints, with the pending damage's ETA at most 600 ms, both read at the end of the previous tick. (1) An attacker with a projectile that has not fired at its target drops a doomed target on the next tick: 62 of 62 cases in 40 runs, 14 walking Minions (the Minions-walking, attack, slow-arrow and fast-arrow scenarios and a Phoenix scenario) and 48 in their windup, not yet fired: princess towers 19, Musketeer 11, Goblin Hut Spear Goblins 10, Cannon 4, Minions 3, Mother Witch 1. Every one of the 62 targets was a troop. 2 of the drops (two walking Minions at a Phoenix, hp 317) came when only the sum of two shots in flight (217 and 107) was lethal. None took the doomed unit back while it lived; the new target was a tower (38) or another unit (24). 29 of the drops read an ETA of exactly 600, so the gate is <= 600, not < 600. No attacker dropped a target on the frame the doom first showed: the drop always comes one tick later. (2) The ETA gate: 44 of 44 ticks on which such an attacker's target had lethal pending damage 650-750 ms away were keeps, and 28 attackers were seen on both sides (keep while the ETA read above 600, drop the tick after it read 600). (3) An attacker with a projectile that has fired at its target and is in reach keeps it until it dies: 1,362 of 1,362 ticks over 219 attacker-target pairs (towers, Minions, Musketeer, Mother Witch, Hunter, Cannon and others). (4) An attacker without a projectile keeps a doomed target: 160 of 160 ticks over 34 pairs, among them a walking Ronin (12 ticks, 2 targets) and a walking Knight (4 ticks), a Knight and an Inferno Tower attacking, an Electro Wizard; the ranged ones (Inferno Tower 76, Electro Wizard 4) kept on 80 of 80 ticks. Not scoped: a fired attacker out of reach (3 Minion drops at 3757-3934 and an Electro Dragon drop; 12 keeps by a Mother Witch 62-147 out, a Minion 15 out and a tower). The engine before this key flipped keeps every doomed target. Pre-scored 2026-09-26 on RoyaleSim 8648486, alone: corpus +710 / -25 / +204 (124946 +579, 072148 A and B +53 and +72, 090825-B +6), sweep 0. With the other six keys (window AV, RoyaleSim 1c75632): corpus +2,839, sweep +3,197. Flipped to projectile_attackers_rescan at the 2026-09-26 integration flip (RoyaleSim fc3a790). Reverted alone to projectile_attackers on that build: sweep +712 within 250 / 0 / +46 hp exact (the Minion Horde and the Minions), corpus 0; the three Minion scenario runs of the rescan measurement match the client on every tick.
DOOMED_TARGET_DROP.meaning: projectile_attackers: at the Target phase of tick t, an attacker whose card fires a projectile (troops, buildings and crown towers) and whose current target X was doomed at the end of tick t-1 drops X unless it has launched a shot at X since acquiring it; its windup is cancelled and it rescans with every doomed unit excluded from the candidates, so it does not take X back while X lives. Doomed: the summed damage of the projectiles in flight at X (crown-tower arrows included) is at least X's hitpoints, and that damage's ETA, a countdown fixed at launch (the flight in whole ticks x 50 ms: ceil(distance / speed) fits 3,109 of 3,202 single-shot launches on client 15.535.29, the rest are a few units past a whole tick and read one tick less), is at most 600 ms (LOGIC_PENDING_DAMAGE_IGNORE_IF_DURATION_LESS). With two shots in flight the countdown followed the one that lands later, in both cases seen. Attackers without a projectile (whatever their range, flying or not), and attackers that have fired at X and are in reach, keep X. keep: the engine before this key flipped, where a doomed target is kept like any other.
DOOMED_TARGET_DROP.open: A fired attacker out of reach (Minions dropped at 257-434 beyond reach; a Mother Witch kept at 62-147 beyond). A melee attacker's first swing (the records cannot show whether a direct hit has started). Whether the ETA of several pending shots is the later or the earlier landing (two cases, the later in both, but both under 600, so no decision turned on it). A doomed building or crown tower as the target (all 62 measured drops were at troops). Whether a unit that was not already after X may acquire a doomed X. A moving target: the countdown is fixed at launch, but the tests use a still target and cannot tell it from an ETA recomputed each tick. The 16.402 reading of combat.POST_KILL_RETARGET_WAIT counts homing projectiles only; on client 15.535.29 the princess tower's arrow is in the pending damage. A projectile attacker that has fired at its target and then WALKS after it: the sweep's Skeleton Dragons drop the doomed Knight while walking (client 15.535.29), one scenario Sparky keeps its doomed target while walking, and on client 16.402 walking Witches keep doomed Skeletons. Not settled.

DOOMED_TARGET_DROP.engine: combat.rs doomed_by_shots_in_flight (the doomed set from the projectiles in flight at the tick's start: summed damage against hitpoints and shield, and ticks_to_land of the last shot against target.rs DOOMED_ETA_LIMIT_MS), built in state.rs phase_target before the decisions and handed to target.rs can_target through TargetCtx::doomed, where a projectile attacker neither keeps nor takes a doomed unit it has not fired at (entity.rs fired_at: set when it launches, cleared when its target changes). Pinned by crates/royalesim/tests/doomed_target_drop.rs and tests/test_doomed_target_drop.py.

LOGIC_CANCEL_HIT_FROM_LONG_DISTANCE_RANG.confidence: LOW (the recorded corpus contradicts 1500 on all 3 swings that test it; measured_2026_09_22)
LOGIC_CANCEL_HIT_FROM_LONG_DISTANCE_RANG.meaning: An attack already started is only cancelled if the target gets this far beyond range.
LOGIC_CANCEL_HIT_FROM_LONG_DISTANCE_RANG.measured_2026_09_22: Read from the attack timers of the recorded corpus (data/derived/replay, attack_progress_ms and attack_load_timer_ms). A swing is under way when attack_progress_ms % HitSpeed > 50 (the engine's own hit-started test) and lands when the counter crosses the next multiple of HitSpeed; distance beyond range follows targeting.ATTACK_RANGE_RULE (centre distance less Range and both CollisionRadius, cards.json). Across the 40 distinct battles, 13 swings of attackers that fire a projectile (crown towers included) had their target leave range while the swing was under way. 11 were kept to the hit, 10 of them with the target at most 887 beyond range and one far past 1,500: a Lava Pup (20260920-071744-A, key 59, ticks 1957-1983) whose Goblin walked away fired with it 2,506 beyond range. 2 were dropped well inside 1,500: a Spear Goblin (20260918-112751, key 57, tick 1965) dropped its Valkyrie at 501-550 beyond range, on the tick after the Valkyrie first stood beyond the Spear Goblin's own SightRange (5,500 edge to edge, passed by 1), and the king tower (20260918-124946, tick 2517) dropped a Knight that had gone 500 beyond its range. So 1500 predicts none of the 3 swings that test it. The rival attacker_sight_range (a started swing holds while the target stays within the attacker's own SightRange, edge to edge) predicts the Lava Pup (its SightRange sits 3,900 past its Range) and the Spear Goblin, and misses the king tower, whose SightRange equals its Range and which held its Knight 500 past both. Ground melee attackers are LOGIC_PRESERVE_TARGET_IF_HIT_STARTED's business: they drop a target that leaves range when a nearer enemy is in reach. With no nearer enemy their swings also land with the target out of range, a Skeleton's 1,131 beyond (20260918-134739-A, tick 603); four melee swings were dropped 34 to 467 beyond range with no nearer enemy, which neither value explains. Recorded on client 16.402 by the client instrument that records ground-truth traces from the real game.
LOGIC_CANCEL_HIT_FROM_LONG_DISTANCE_RANG.proposed_value: attacker_sight_range, once it is implemented in target.rs and the corpus parity run does not get worse; it fits 2 of the 3 deciding swings where 1500 fits none, on a sample of three. Left at 1500 here because a value change alters engine behaviour and must ride one announced rebuild with a parity score beside it.

LOGIC_PRESERVE_TARGET_IF_HIT_STARTED.measured_2026_09_25: MEASURED on client 15.535.29, the reach-loss scenarios (a red Knight engaging a blue Hog Rider at x 9500, the Hog running on up the lane; four runs). Cannon in range: a blue Cannon at (12500, 12500). The Knight swings at the Hog, which stands 2296 from it on tick 290 and 2415 on 291, beyond its reach on the Hog (Range 1200 + radii 500 and 600 = 2300, plus the 25 of LOGIC_RANGE_EXTENSION_TO_KEEP_TARGET). On 292 its target is the Cannon, 1331 away, its attack progress 1050 -> 1100 unbroken, and it hits the Cannon on 294 (progress 1200), the tick the no-Cannon control hits the Hog. The control, with no other enemy in sight: the Knight keeps the Hog and hits it on 294 at 2773, 473 beyond reach. Royal Hogs: the first Royal Hog stands 2322 on 292 (inside reach + 25) and 2380 on 293; on 294 the Knight targets another Royal Hog 1979 away, progress 3100 -> 3150, and hits it on 303 at progress 3600, the running cycle. So a Knight's windup does not lock its target: it keeps a target inside Range + 25 and rescans the tick after the target stood beyond, the rescan returning the same target when no other enemy is nearer. This is the ground melee half of the 16.402 corpus reading above (eight direct strikers switched on the first tick beyond range + 25). THE PROJECTILE HALF, measured on client 15.535.29 (a Musketeer and Minions whose Hog Rider leaves reach, with and without a Cannon nearer; 26 runs with the whole scene or the attacker alone shifted by 1-6 frames): a projectile attacker keeps a leaving target while the target's start-of-tick centre distance is within reach + H, H in [499.45, 544.52) (every one of 15 switches or drops lands on the frame the distance first exceeds reach + 499.45, at every frame residue, so it is a per-tick test, not a periodic scan). A launch at the target beyond reach also ends the hold: a Musketeer that fired at the Hog 7314.3 and 7508.4 away (reach 7100) re-evaluated on the next frame (2 events). The re-evaluation picks the nearest enemy in sight by start-of-tick distance, and returns the same target when none is nearer; the Minions then launched at it 1225 beyond reach. projectile_attackers_only: an attacker whose card fires a projectile keeps its target within reach + 500 until it launches at it beyond reach, and re-evaluates on the next tick after either; an attacker that strikes directly keeps its target only inside Range + LOGIC_RANGE_EXTENSION_TO_KEEP_TARGET. What happens to the swing on the switch is combat.RETARGET_PROGRESS.

SPAWNED_UNIT_ACQUIRE_DELAY.confidence: HIGH. A troop created by a death spawn is first targeted on F+7 (its 8th frame): 35 first targeted on exactly F+7 and none on F+1 to F+6, over 402 client 15.535.29 scenario runs. The Golemite row has no DeployDelay, so the delay is not DeployDelay. Hand-played troops, a Tombstone's periodic Skeletons and spawned buildings are not delayed.
SPAWNED_UNIT_ACQUIRE_DELAY.provenance: MEASURED on client 15.535.29, the per-frame records of the 15.535.29 scenario runs (402 runs). A death-spawned troop is first targeted by an enemy on its 8th frame F+7 (F = its first frame; the parent's last frame + 8). Of the troops that appeared as a same-side unit vanished beside them, 35 were first targeted on exactly F+7, none on F+1..F+6, 42 later and 16 never. The witnesses include the Goblin Cage scenario (an idle Cannon and the Knight that killed the cage both first target the Brawler on F+7; the Cannon stood idle from F+1 to F+6), the Golem scenarios of both sides (an Inferno Tower, a Knight and a Musketeer all switch to the Golemites on F+7), the Lava Hound's Pups and the Goblin Giant's Spear Goblins. The Golemite row has no DeployDelay, so the delay is not that column. The same F+7, and never earlier, holds for troops released by the Skeleton Barrel's container (22 Skeletons), for the Phoenix's egg (3) and for troops spawned by a Goblin Hut (65 waves), a Graveyard (36 Skeletons) and a Suspicious Bush (12 Goblins). Hand-played troops are targeted from their first frame (39 first targeted on it; a Barbarian beside the Goblin Cage scenario). A Tombstone's periodic Skeletons are born active and are first targeted on their 2nd frame: an idle Cannon took the first Skeleton of each pair on F+1 in 4 of 4 cases (the 15.535.29 Tombstone scenarios at two distances), and a Knight switched to one on its 2nd frame (the Tombstone sweep scenario). A spawned BUILDING is exempt: both princess towers target the Goblin Drill's emerging building on F+1. The engine before this key flipped: the idle Cannon targets the Brawler and a Golemite on F+1. Pre-scored 2026-09-26 on RoyaleSim dd556f1, alone: corpus +5 / +5 / +34, sweep -10. In the Goblin Cage sweep scene the Knight becomes exact from its first look at the Brawler (0 against 85-92 native). The -10 is the Brawler's own first step, which bends the other way in the client. The death-spawn scenarios' -44 is one scene whose Lava Hound dies 58 ticks late under both arms.
SPAWNED_UNIT_ACQUIRE_DELAY.meaning: client_8th_frame: a troop created by a death spawn (a troop's or a building's DeathSpawnCharacter, including a container's release) cannot be acquired as a target by any enemy before its 8th frame: it becomes acquirable on F+7, where F is its first frame. Hand-played troops, spawned buildings and the periodic Skeletons of the Tombstone are acquirable at once. The exemption is measured on the Tombstone only and is not a column rule: the Goblin Hut's row carries the same SpawnCharacter and SpawnInterval columns, and its waves, which come from its action graph, wait for F+7 (65 waves). A SPELL's spawn is not a death spawn either: the Barbarian Barrel's released Barbarian is first targeted on F+1 in every scene where an enemy took it (23 of 23 in the 15.535.29 Barbarian Barrel scenarios), so an engine that releases it through a death-spawn path must not mark it. none: the engine before this key flipped, where a death spawn is acquirable from the tick after it appears.

CENTRE_LANE_FRAME.meaning: Which frame decides a unit's lane for LOGIC_XPOS_BASED_TOWER_TARGETING, and therefore which enemy princess tower a targetless unit walks to. own_frame_tie_left: the attacker's own (rotated) frame, centre going own-left. engine_frame_tie_right: the absolute arena x, centre going engine-right.
CENTRE_LANE_FRAME.candidates_differ_only_at: BLUE STANDING EXACTLY ON x = W/2, and nowhere else in the arena for either seat. Verified over every integer x for both seats. That value is unreachable by a deploy, because a tap snaps to its tile centre: x=9000 and x=9001 both land a unit at 9500. So no tap-driven scenario can ever discriminate these arms, and the 12 rows above never stood on the line. To settle it, a unit must WALK onto x = W/2 and be read on the tick it is there.
CENTRE_LANE_FRAME.why_this_arm: Chosen on a structural prior, the 15.535.29 scenarios being silent. own_frame_tie_left is seat-symmetric at every x; engine_frame_tie_right breaks the 180-degree seat rotation at x = W/2 exactly. RoyaleGym's rotation gate measured that break on build 1b8fc1eace21feb7 (one seed of three -- a tie is rare, which is the signature of a tie rather than a systematic flip). Both seats share one policy head and the observation is built in the acting side's own frame so that Blue and Red are the same problem, so an absolute-direction tie makes the same board a different game depending on colour. No evidence for the other arm, a measured cost against it.

history.provenance: the 12 client 15.535.29 scenarios, read as showing that the seats do not mirror on the centre line
history.overturned_by: parity session the same day: both arms reproduce all 12 rows, so the experiment never discriminated them. The divergence it was introduced to fix was a DEPLOY POSITION -- the harness spawned the fixtures at their raw tap (x=9000, a tile corner) where the client spawns at the tile centre (9500), and at 9500 the own-frame rule already agrees. Across all 21 fixtures the only lane divergence was side 0 at x=9000, while x=8999, x=9001 and every side-1 row agreed, which is exactly what 'the arms differ only at 9000' predicts. Changing this rule moved the engine to agree with a fixture convention and cost seat symmetry to do it.

CENTRE_LANE_FRAME.observability: THE ARMS MAY BE BEHAVIOURALLY INDISTINGUISHABLE IN REAL PLAY, measured over the 73-battle corpus on 2026-09-23. (a) x = W/2 = 9000 is NOT a path-node x: nodes sit on half-cell centres k*500+250, so the nearest are 8750 and 9250 and a unit walking the grid never stands there. (b) 3477 non-tower truth entities yield 72 unit-ticks with a unit exactly on x=9000 -- 55 Archer and 14 Goblins in behaviour_state 4, 3 Archer in state 1 -- and ALL 72 carry target = -1, no resolved pointer. (c) ZERO unit-ticks in the corpus have a unit on x=9000 while holding a resolved crown-tower pointer. Positive control on that scan: the same logic finds 557705 such unit-ticks off the centre line across 63 cards, so the zero is a measurement and not a broken query. A unit reaches the exact centre line only while DEPLOYING, before any tower pointer exists. So the corpus cannot settle this, and the behaviour difference between the arms was never observed in 73 recorded battles -- which is also why the fixture score moved when this key was flipped: the movement came entirely from the oracle fixtures placing units on a tile CORNER, which real play does not do.
CENTRE_LANE_FRAME.promotion_rules: Reach x = W/2 by MOVEMENT rather than by a tap -- a unit whose walk crosses the centre exactly on a tick boundary, or a placement that is not tile-snapped -- and record which tower it then walks to. Until then neither arm may be cited as measured, and a figure that improves after flipping this key has not confirmed anything: the arms differ at one coordinate that the game never places a unit on.

CONTACT_LAW.provenance: SETTLED ON THE LIVE 16.402 CAPTURES on 2026-09-19/20 and VERIFIED against every one of them. The per-tick contact and locomotion update (the step, the avoidance and separation scans, the position write and the update order) is implemented in crates/royalesim/src/move16402.rs; the evidence for every rule is the live capture set. THE LAW: (1) each tick every attack update runs before every move update, and the move updates run one unit after another in CREATION order against a bucket index of collision circles (each grown by 250 for movers) built from the start-of-tick positions -- unit i sees units j < i already moved and j > i where they started (a replay with previous-tick neighbours reproduces 46 % of the contact ticks, the sequential order 98 %). (2) avoidance (states 1 and 4, not while attacking): the entities whose circle overlaps the circle of radius min(R,500) around pos + facing (facing has length 256) vote; a static (a unit that does not move) wins over movers, the last seen wins; offset 0 -> +-200, a running offset +-20 only when a static is seen, clamped to +-200, then -10 toward zero every walk tick (so 190 is the visible onset and +10/tick the visible ramp); a static whose circle contains the current waypoint's centre pops that waypoint. (3) separation (states 1, 2, 4): every overlapping neighbour of either side -- buildings and towers included, touching counts (d2 <= (R1+R2)^2; my radius capped at 500 against a static) -- adds trunc(dx x mag / d), trunc(dy x mag / d) away from it with mag = min(299, trunc(min(R1+R2-d, 300) x M_other / M_self)) + 1, and one count; coincident centres push +-1 in y by team. (4) the step: dist = max(1, isqrt(dist2)); step = min(speed, dist, 250); heading = trunc((aim - pos) << 8 / dist); step vector = trunc(heading x step / 256) per axis; facing := normalize256(aim - pos); if the offset is nonzero the step is rotated by the blend v' = ((256 - |a|) v + a perp(v)) >> 8 renormalised to the step length (tan theta = a / (256 - |a|)); the accumulator's MEAN (trunc(acc / count)) capped at 150 is added; pos += step, an axis that crosses out of the grid clamps to the cell edge, and only a DEPLOYING ground unit is clamped at a water edge; then reached := proj(aim - pos', segment) <= 1000. (5) Mass as loaded from the card data: an empty Mass column becomes tdiv(floor(R^2/250) x R, 62500) and every Mass is clamped to [1, 20] -- towers, Tombstone and Goblin Hut weigh 20, a Cannon 13, a Tesla 8 -- which is why a unit touching a tower flies back at the 150 cap. (6) With an empty path and a target out of range the unit walks at the point reach = Range + own CollisionRadius away from the target on the line to itself. VERIFICATION (over the 31 live captures, every frame pair, the world rebuilt at the start of each tick): 240389 / 242232 unit-tick positions exact (0.99239); isolated 0.99367, separation active 0.98319, two or more overlaps 0.98406, against buildings 0.99829, avoidance active 0.98221, spawn overlaps 0.99656, attacking 0.99277; the post-decay avoidance offset exact on 0.99962. The 1843 misses are diagnosed (Skeleton crowds with dying neighbours, missed stomp pauses / freezes, replanned aims, Rage inference, knockbacks not in the trace); no contact-law alternative explains more than 0.005 % of them. The Rust implementation is gated by equivalence with an independent reimplementation on random worlds (20 000 / 20 000 per seed).
CONTACT_LAW.why_it_matters: 27 % of all live moving ticks are crowded; nothing crowded reproduced before this law. Head-on units now pass each other the way the game's do.
CONTACT_LAW.promotion_rules: SETTLED by 242 232 live unit-ticks. Re-open only against a new client build.
CONTACT_LAW.engine_contract: state.rs phase_path16402 runs it under pathfinding.PATH_SEARCH = client16402 (the same arm that selects the measured 16.402 search): units update one after the other in creation order, the position write is the game's, collide::separate and the river ejection are bypassed. The frame-planned arm keeps the engine's own guessed separation (PUSH_MODEL below).

PUSH_MODEL.provenance: NONE. The data ships a Mass column (Skeleton 1, Knight 6, Giant 18, Golem 20) and the wiki says mass matters qualitatively -- but a field existing is not a formula, and the best public reimplementation ignores Mass entirely and weights by speed ratio instead.
PUSH_MODEL.why_it_matters: Unit push governs body-blocking, swarm spread, and whether a tank walks through or around its own support -- i.e. most of what a player is actually doing. The old engine had NO unit collision whatsoever, which is the single biggest reason it could not model the game.
PUSH_MODEL.promotion_rules: Directly measurable from captures: record scripted head-on collisions across a mass ladder (Skeleton 1 / Knight 6 / Giant 18 / Golem 20) and a speed ladder, then fit the displacement ratio against mass-ratio, speed-ratio and the product. Also check for a per-tick displacement cap, which is invisible in aggregate.
PUSH_MODEL.offline_note: NOTHING RECORDS THE PUSH. It is not separately observable in the offline trace corpus -- it must be fitted from the movement RESIDUAL (movement.CONTACT_DOMAIN): |step| about S plus a 15-28 unit lateral residual perpendicular to the heading for crowd separation, and 0.06-2.5 x S, possibly opposing the heading, for combat pushback. SEPARATION_ITERATIONS.provenance: NONE. Affects how tightly a crowd packs.
SEPARATION_ITERATIONS.promotion_rules: Measure the steady-state spacing of a Skeleton Army against a wall and fit.

BUILDING_FOOTPRINT_MODEL.provenance: Three candidate models disagree for exactly the cases that decide games. The King Tower's shipped no-deploy block is 3x3 tiles but its CollisionRadius is 1400 (2.8 tiles diameter) -- those do not reconcile. Princess towers are NOT in the static map at all, so their footprint must come from CollisionRadius 1000 (a 2x2 box), which contradicts the commonly-quoted 3x3.
BUILDING_FOOTPRINT_MODEL.why_it_matters: Decides whether a unit can squeeze between a princess tower and the arena edge, and where a melee unit stands to hit a tower.
BUILDING_FOOTPRINT_MODEL.promotion_rules: Walk a minimum-radius unit (CollisionRadius 400) along a tower edge and record closest approach. Repeat for king and princess.

placement.$comment: WHERE A BUILDING MAY BE PUT, which is a different question from what its body does to movement (collision.BUILDING_FOOTPRINT_MODEL). A building occupies a whole number of TILES when it is placed, and troops walk through that box freely: over the recorded corpus a troop centre is inside a Cannon's box on 394 of 943 nearby frames and inside a princess tower's on 11923 of 49173. Settled 2026-09-22 over 114 recorded building placements.

FOOTPRINT_TILES.confidence: HIGH for the cards the recordings pin, MEDIUM for the rest
FOOTPRINT_TILES.provenance: MEASURED on 114 unique building placements recorded from the real game on client 16.402 (the A/B twins of one battle deduplicated), through the client instrument that records ground-truth traces. The footprint is an N x N tile box with N = ceil(2R / tile) + 1 from CollisionRadius: R 500 gives 2, R 600 gives 3, R 1000 gives 3 and R 1400 gives 4. Pinned per card by sweeping N against every placement's legality and every relocation: Cannon 3 (N = 1 refuted by two placements, N = 5 by four), Tombstone 3, Goblin Hut 3, Bomb Tower 3, Goblin Cage 3, Barbarian Hut 3, Tesla 2, the surfaced Goblin Drill building 2. Inferno Tower, Mortar, X-Bow and Elixir Collector follow the rule and are NOT individually pinned, because no recorded placement of them discriminates. The losing arms: an all-odd N of 1 explains 31 of the 64 tapped placements and N of 5 explains 30, against 64 of 64 for the rule; floor + 1 and round + 1 both fail on R 600, which is the witness, because 2R is 1.2 tiles.
FOOTPRINT_TILES.why_it_matters: It decides whether a Cannon can be put against the arena wall or flush inside a tower, which is a large part of defensive placement.
FOOTPRINT_TILES.promotion_rules: To pin the four unpinned cards, record a placement of each whose legality differs between N = 1, 3 and 5: tapped one tile from a wall separates 3 from 1, and tapped two tiles from a tower separates 3 from 5.
FOOTPRINT_TILES.engine_contract: crates/royalesim/src/arena.rs placement_tiles; the box is built by Arena::placement_box and judged by Arena::box_zone. It is NOT a collision shape: collision.BUILDING_FOOTPRINT_MODEL still decides what movement sees.

TOWER_FOOTPRINT_TILES.confidence: HIGH on the king, MEDIUM on the princess
TOWER_FOOTPRINT_TILES.provenance: MEASURED on the same 114 placements: a crown tower blocks a building the way another building does, and the same size rule gives a princess tower 3x3 and a king tower 4x4. Scoring the alternatives against every placement, a princess of 1 tile fails one placement, a princess of 4 or 5 fails at least five, and a king of 5 fails five. THE CORPUS CANNOT SEPARATE a 3x3 princess from a 2x2 one, nor a 4x4 king from a 3x3 one, because every building box has integer tile edges, so a box overlaps the closed 2.5-to-4.5 span exactly when it overlaps 2-to-5. The shipped reading is the one that needs no special case: a tile-aligned box centred on a tile centre must be odd, and one centred on a corner must be even.
TOWER_FOOTPRINT_TILES.why_it_matters: It decides how close a defensive building may sit to a tower, and the viewer draws it.
TOWER_FOOTPRINT_TILES.promotion_rules: Record a building tapped so that its box would overlap the disputed ring of a tower by exactly one tile, on each of the two towers.
TOWER_FOOTPRINT_TILES.engine_contract: The towers take the same arena.rs path as buildings, through their own CollisionRadius.

SNAP_EVEN_CORNER.confidence: LOW. The recordings do not discriminate it, and the arm that ships was chosen for its consequences rather than on evidence.
SNAP_EVEN_CORNER.provenance: THE SNAP ITSELF IS MEASURED and the corner is not. Of 114 recorded placements, all 102 with an odd footprint sit on a tile centre and all 24 with an even one sit on a tile corner, without exception. But every even-footprint placement in the corpus was made by ONE SEAT (18 Tesla and 6 Goblin Drill, all on the same side), so 'the arena's own lower-left corner' and 'the placer's lower-left corner' fit the corpus equally, and nothing recorded separates them.
SNAP_EVEN_CORNER.why_it_matters: The two arms put an even-footprint building a whole tile apart for one of the two seats. Under the absolute arm a policy shared between seats sees a seat-dependent offset, and the rotation gates fail on 2x2 buildings.
SNAP_EVEN_CORNER.promotion_rules: Record a Tesla placed by the seat that defends high y, at a tap whose two candidate corners differ. One placement settles it.
SNAP_EVEN_CORNER.engine_contract: crates/royalesim/src/arena.rs snap_placement, selected by state.rs Calib::placement_snap_even.

TAP_SNAP.confidence: LOW for the shipped arm none, which is today's engine. HIGH for client16402_tile_centre: both clients, every tap that separates the rules
TAP_SNAP.provenance: MEASURED on client 15.535.29 and the 16.402 corpus. A troop or spell tap is snapped to the PLAIN centre of its tile, tile * 1000 + 500 on both axes, both sides, both halves: 37 of 37 unique corpus spell casts where the rules disagree land on it, as do 5 of 5 left-half air deploys and the 15.535.29 air scenarios. A GROUND unit then takes the one-native deploy-point offset of formation.GROUND_DEPLOY_POINT (x - 1 on the absolute left half, y - 1 for side 1), which the engine applied only to multi-member rings: the seven single Knights of the 15.535.29 scenarios stand on it, 7 of 7. A Log or a Fireball cast from a raw tap then behaves exactly as from its snapped centre.
TAP_SNAP.meaning: client16402_tile_centre: every troop and spell tap is snapped to its tile centre before the formation is laid or the spell is cast, and formation.GROUND_DEPLOY_POINT applies to a single ground unit as to a ring. Buildings keep their own snap (placement.SNAP_EVEN_CORNER). none: today's engine, a single unit and a spell at the raw tap.
TAP_SNAP.open: Where the snapped tile is illegal for a troop or a spell, the relocation is placement.TROOP_TOWER_TAPS's and the Log's own rule; this key only snaps.
TAP_SNAP.promotion_rules: Pass the 15.535.29 checks (the seven Knights, raw against snapped Log casts), score by override, then flip.
TAP_SNAP.engine: the deploy path before formation_members and spell::cast; arena.rs snap_placement with a one-tile box

ILLEGAL_TAP.confidence: HIGH that the tap is moved rather than refused; LOW on which of the two relocating arms
ILLEGAL_TAP.provenance: MEASURED: of the 64 recorded building taps whose tap point is known, 39 ended somewhere other than the tapped tile, so the game MOVES a building whose footprint does not fit rather than refusing the play, and 'refuse' is refuted outright. The two relocating arms are NOT separated by the corpus: every relocation with a reliable tap moves 1 or 2 tiles (two at ring 1, three at ring 2), and the two orders agree below ring 3, because a ring-r diagonal is r x sqrt(2) away while a ring-(r+1) axial cell is only r + 1. Relocation is only ever observed INSIDE the placer's own half, because a player's own client never sends a tap from outside it, so the engine refuses a tap whose own point fails the cell or territory rules rather than extrapolating past what was seen.
ILLEGAL_TAP.why_it_matters: It decides whether a building tap is a refusal or a different building, which changes what a placement mask means and what a policy can learn.
ILLEGAL_TAP.promotion_rules: Record a building tap whose only fits are three or more rings away, with a ring-r diagonal fit and a ring-(r+1) axial fit both available. The two arms then land it on different tiles.
ILLEGAL_TAP.engine_contract: crates/royalesim/src/state.rs building_placement, bounded by PLACEMENT_SEARCH_RINGS = 30 tiles, which spans the arena. The ring scan order is built in the placer's frame so the two seats mirror; the corpus leaves exactly one tie, so the order is the engine's choice and not a measurement.

TROOP_TOWER_TAPS.confidence: LOW for the shipped arm closed_block, which is today's engine: 31 of 48 casts measured on client 15.535.29 disagree with it. HIGH for client16402_half_open_relocate on the own king, 48 of 48 casts measured; OPEN on the princess towers' no-deploy rects, which the battery did not probe
TROOP_TOWER_TAPS.provenance: MEASURED on client 15.535.29: a deliberate-tap battery, a Knight, Goblins and Minions tapped at eight own-frame tiles around the own king, both sides, 48 casts, every member's first-frame position. (1) The king's no-deploy block is HALF-OPEN in absolute coordinates, [min, max) on both axes, so it is not mirrored: side 0 refuses own (8500, 1500) and (7500, 1500) and accepts own (10500, 1500); side 1 accepts all three; own (9500, 2500) is refused on both sides. (2) An accepted troop tap whose tile overlaps the own king is moved to the nearest free tile, the way a building's is (placement.ILLEGAL_TAP): own (8500, 1499) lands on (8499, 500), side 1's own (7500, 1500) on (6499, 1501), and a formation is laid around the moved point. (3) Side 1's ground back bound (own y 1000) holds a single unit too: a side-1 Knight at own (8500, 500) stands on own 1000. The 16.402 corpus agrees where it can see: its side-1 Goblins at own (8500, 1500) sit on the 15.535.29 battery's own 850 / 1262 / 1262 / 1000 in 7 of 11 groups, its side-1 Bombers there on own 1000 in 11 of 15, and its side-0 king plays stand where relocation from own (8500, 1500) puts them (singles on (8499, 500)). Units deployed there are the corpus's largest remaining loss (9,980 lost within-250 unit-ticks at the 7b build).
TROOP_TOWER_TAPS.meaning: client16402_half_open_relocate: the three laws above; laws 2 and 3 in the placement resolution a replayed deploy shares, law 1 in the play path's legality. closed_block: today's engine, a closed king block, no troop relocation, single units unclamped.
TROOP_TOWER_TAPS.open: The princess towers' no-deploy rects keep today's rule until a battery probes their edges; the relocation order on an exact tie is the ring order ILLEGAL_TAP already uses, confirmed on one 15.535.29 tie.
TROOP_TOWER_TAPS.promotion_rules: Score the new arm with replay_parity --calibration-override (stacked on formation.STAGGER_WAIT's measured arm), then flip.

OVERLAP_TEST.provenance: MEASURED over 191 near pairs of live boxes in the recordings: none overlaps and 93 touch exactly. One recorded Cannon stands flush against a princess tower's box, a king block and a Goblin Cage at the same time, so contact alone cannot be illegal. Boxes also sit flush against the side wall, the river line and the back no-deploy strip.
OVERLAP_TEST.why_it_matters: Whether a defensive building may be put flush against a tower is a real placement decision.
OVERLAP_TEST.promotion_rules: SETTLED unless a recording shows a refused flush placement.

BUILDING_TERRITORY.confidence: LOW. The corpus cannot discriminate it, and the shipped arm is kept because it is the one already running.
BUILDING_TERRITORY.provenance: NOT SETTLED by the placement work. The two arms agree while every enemy crown tower stands, because the enemy rects then cover the whole enemy side, and no building in the corpus was tapped on the wrong half at all. They part after an enemy princess falls: own_half still refuses the opened band past the far bank, and the rect rule allows it, as it does for troops.
BUILDING_TERRITORY.why_it_matters: It decides whether a building may be put past the river once a lane is open, which is a real attacking option.
BUILDING_TERRITORY.promotion_rules: Record a building tapped past the far bank after an enemy princess has fallen. One placement settles it.
BUILDING_TERRITORY.engine_contract: crates/royalesim/src/state.rs deploy_rule returns Territory::OwnHalf for a building; arena.rs box_zone judges the BOX against it, not the tap.
BUILDING_TERRITORY.gap_box_zone_has_no_rect_test: arena.rs box_zone applies NO enemy-crown-tower no-deploy rect test, and it should, because the BOX is what occupies the ground. The tap rule does apply one (territory_zone, alive enemy rects) but only under EnemyTowerRects, and a building uses OwnHalf, so today nothing consults a rect for a building and the gap cannot fire. It fires the moment this key takes its rival arm: the box would go untested against rects while its snapped centre is tested, which is the wrong one to test. The concrete wrong outcome is a building whose BOX overlaps an alive enemy tower's rect while its centre does not. Whoever flips this key adds the rect test to box_zone IN THE SAME CHANGE. Noted 2026-09-22 after the gym session proved its honest-tap arm lossless on the invariant BOX LEGALITY IMPLIES TAP LEGALITY, which this gap would silently falsify.

Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Cost stage: over 150 recorded first paths, the recorded path is exactly cost-minimal for its own endpoints under road 5 / plain 8 / water impassable / bit-16 impassable / 8-connected / diagonal x sqrt(2) -- 0 suboptimal, 0 infeasible. 4-connected reproduces 44/150; a uniform diagonal leaves 3 paths strictly dearer than the optimum (witnesses lane_sweep_Knight c00_r06 173 vs 171, c08_r04 197 vs 190, c10_r06 181 vs 174); a flat cost 8 fails 96.
ALGORITHM.supercell_2025_release_note: Troops now rely much less on lanes. Previously, they would move horizontally to reach their lane before advancing. Now, they move diagonally. | Troops can now see Buildings and adjust their movement in advance instead of walking straight into them and only navigating around after a collision.
ALGORITHM.why_it_matters: This is the mechanic the whole project is named after, and the version everybody documented is the one Supercell replaced on 2025-03-31.
ALGORITHM.promotion_rules: Black-box discrimination, not archaeology. Design scenarios where candidate models predict visibly different tracks -- a building offset from the lane centre, a building wall forcing a non-lane detour, a building destroyed mid-path -- record the real tracks, and score each model. The engine must therefore keep the pathfinder behind a swappable interface with all candidates implemented.

This strongly favours candidate weighted_grid_astar with these costs over lane_flow and pure lookahead; 'rely less on lanes' reads as road (lane-painted) cells being cheaper rather than mandatory. Value left unchanged until the path_nodes of the 15.535.29 traces confirm grid, costs and cadence. globals.csv of Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029 (2026-08-06 build, post every documented pathfinding change), from a verified 15.535.29 asset pack; compressed sha256 85616b49473308e2690d084bdd3618df8909f489f69c873bc6c9cf3f813574f9, decoded sha256 6b5813e24b3d68f83da2fead5952184b09794853ccdb03a0eaf854a5433ae49a, decoded 2026-09-18 by this repo's tools/decode_sc_assets.py.

history.provenance: The three most complete public engines implement three DIFFERENT algorithms and none was verified against the client. Worse, all three model the PRE-2025 game.
history.overturned_by: the path_nodes published in the 15.535.29 traces: a weighted A* over a 36x64 half-tile grid reproduces the cost of 150/150 first paths; lane_flow, authored waypoints and pure post-2025 lookahead do not.

candidate_meanings.weighted_grid_astar: THE MEASURED 2026 MODEL (royalesim PathModel::Oracle2026, src/path2026.rs): 8-connected weighted A* over the 36x64 half-tile grid, cell-entered costs (PATHFINDING_COSTS), the sqrt(2) diagonal (DIAGONAL_COST_RATIO), CHEBYSHEV heuristic over the GOAL SET (HEURISTIC_FORM; octile is refuted by the live 16.402 corpus), half-open AABB occlusions of EVERY building on the board (OCCLUSION_MODEL; friendly-only is refuted likewise) priced at PATHFINDING_BUILDING_COST rather than blocking (OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT), and the reach goal rule (PATH_GOAL_RULE).
candidate_meanings.weighted_grid_astar_community: The pre-measurement community model royalesim still carries (PathModel::GridAStar): uniform octile 10/14 step costs, no cost table, mover-radius-inflated blocking and a string-pulled waypoint list. REFUTED for the 2026 game -- a uniform diagonal makes road 5 / plain 8 and a flat cost 8 classify every path identically, so the road discount becomes unidentifiable, and the flat model then fails 96 of 150 paths.

ALGORITHM.still_open: The EXPANSION ORDER is not reproduced: the exact node sequence matches 13 of 76 distinct experiments at best (see TIE_BREAK). The cost model, the occlusions and the goal predicate are settled; which of several equally-optimal paths the game takes is not. RESTATED 2026-09-18 against the live 16.402 corpus: it remains the single largest gap, but the ceiling moved -- 192/292 exact node sequences with the goal cell HANDED to the search and 142/292 with the reach predicate (HEURISTIC_FORM, promoted to Chebyshev on that evidence). Two things narrowed it: the tie-break knob provably cannot move the result under strict-better relaxation with an f-ordered open list (TIE_BREAK), and the residual has ONE systematic signature -- the recorded path shifts column one cell earlier than the model, always immediately after a road/bridge segment. Settled on 2026-09-19 (PATH_SEARCH).

PATH_SEARCH.provenance: SETTLED ON THE LIVE 16.402 CAPTURES on 2026-09-19 and verified against every first path they publish (three independent reproductions of the search agree on every rule below). Every tie-break below was chosen because it reproduces the published node lists, not because a different order was ruled out by argument. The rules cover the search and the path request that enters it, the expansion and relaxation, the heuristic, the cell cost, the building box, the per-tick occlusion rebuild, and the move component's goal-cell choice. THE RULES: (1) ONE goal cell, chosen by the move component: scan rows ascending over target_cell +- (reach/500 + 1), columns ascending when the mover's x < 9000 native else descending, keep the highest category (2 = dry and outside every building box, 1 = water or boxed) and within it the strictly smallest squared distance to the MOVER (first scanned wins ties); reach = Range + own CollisionRadius. (2) the cell cost: -1 out of bounds only; water costs BLOCKED = 50 for a walker and is priced, not refused; lane cells cost ROAD = MATCHINGROAD = 5; else DEFAULT 8; then max(base, occlusion[cell]) where every building of BOTH sides stamps BUILDING = 50 over the half-open box [c - R, c + R) after snapping its centre UP to the next multiple of 500 on each axis, and a box that does not fit entirely inside the grid stamps nothing. NO_DEPLOY plays no part in the cell cost; the king block is priced by the king's own R = 1400 box. (3) step cost = entered cell's cost x 10, x 14 on a diagonal (integer); h = 5 x (10 max(|dc|,|dr|) + 4 min(|dc|,|dr|)) (HEURISTIC_METHOD 1, times DEFAULTHEURISTIC_COST 5); f = g + h. (4) among equally cheap routes, the published route is the one an open list ordered on f alone (no g, no h, no insertion order) produces when equal keys keep their existing order. (5) neighbours in the order N, S, W, E, NW, SW, SE, NE; the start is expanded before the loop; a popped cell is closed, expanded, and the loop ends when the GOAL is closed (i.e. after it has been popped and expanded). (6) an open node reached with a strictly better f takes the new parent, g and f (REFRESH_OPENNODES); a closed node is never revisited (REOPEN_CLOSEDNODES = FALSE). (7) the published list is the parent chain from the goal, goal first, without the start cell. VERIFICATION (scored against the captures): over the 747-case fixture, 615/616 live 16.402 first paths and 128/128 offline 15.535 lane-sweep paths reproduce the exact recorded node sequence. Three further live cases are skipped, not scored: Goblins chasing a MOVING target whose goal cell the trace cannot recover (the sample's target position is the previous tick's). The one live case that diverges takes an equal-cost lane route (tests/oracle2026.rs names it). The trace-fitted arm scored 168/345 and 15/128. Controls run on the same harness: water impassable instead of priced 306/388 and 24/128; friendly-only occlusion 336/388; KS_POS_TO_TARGET_GROUND_AVOID_BUILDINGS off 421/425. See docs/pathfinding.md.
PATH_SEARCH.why_it_matters: Which of several equally cheap routes a unit takes is decided by heap order, and the whole engine's positional fidelity in a crowded lane rests on it: 331 of 425 live first paths have a non-unique optimum.
PATH_SEARCH.promotion_rules: SETTLED. Re-open only against a new client build (re-verify); a trace disagreement is a capture or fixture problem first.
PATH_SEARCH.engine_contract: path2026::plan_cells dispatches on this key: client16402 -> path16402.rs (absolute-coordinate planning, Red un-rotated; NavRequest.team). trace_fitted_astar -> the 2026-09-18 goal-set A* driven by TIE_BREAK / HEURISTIC_FORM / OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT, kept runnable as the refuted arm. supersedes: TIE_BREAK (heap order is the tie-break, no neighbour-order knob reproduces it)
HEURISTIC_FORM (octile 14/10 to ONE goal cell, not Chebyshev over a goal set)
PATH_GOAL_RULE (the reach predicate picks the goal SET; the code picks one cell of it by category then mover distance)
WATER_RULE_GROUND (water is priced 50 and pushed, never entered because never cheaper)
OCCLUSION_MODEL (the box snaps the centre up to a multiple of 500 and is dropped when it leaves the grid; the target building is not exempt)
DIAGONAL_COST_RATIO (14/10 in x10 integer units, not 1414/1000)

REPATH_INTERVAL_TICKS.provenance: MEASURED, and RETIRED as a constant. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. The folklore 10-tick cadence is refuted: every observed recompute is explained by REPLAN_TRIGGERS with 0 unexplained recomputes and 0 predicted triggers that produced none.
REPATH_INTERVAL_TICKS.why_it_matters: Cadence governs how fast a unit responds to a building dropped in its path, which is the central defensive interaction in the game.
REPATH_INTERVAL_TICKS.promotion_rules: Measure the lag between placing a building and the unit visibly changing heading.

history.provenance: NONE -- pure folklore, inherited from one community engine that chose it arbitrarily.
history.overturned_by: the 15.535.29 measurements: there is no periodic replan timer. 150 structural path recomputes over 31859 path-ticks (0.47 per 100), evenly spread across trace families; the gaps within a trace are {17, 24, 29, 100, 185, 190, 228, 248, 250} with no common period. A 30-tick timer would give about 10 changes per trace.

REPATH_INTERVAL_TICKS.engine_contract: royalesim reads this as Option<i32> (state.rs Calib::repath_interval_ticks). null = event-driven; a positive value re-arms the legacy periodic cadence for the pre-2026 models only. The 2026 model ignores it entirely.
REPATH_INTERVAL_TICKS.limits: This bounds OBSERVABLE path changes only. A recompute that returns an identical list is invisible in the traces (8 of 94 tail-surviving recomputes leave path_segment_direction frozen and path_node_consumed clear), and PATHFINDING_SAMEPATH_EPSILON = 3 may be suppressing near-identical results.

PATHFINDING_COSTS.water: WATER (7) IS PAID since the river hop was measured (movement.JUMP_WATER_HOP): a JumpEnabled or hovering mover pays WATER_COST for a water cell and any other walker BLOCKED (50), both before the occlusion max. The engine reads it as Calib::path_cost_water and pays it for every mover with a card.rs JumpDef (path16402.rs cell_cost_for; NavRequest.jumper). Over the five live hops, pricing water at 7 for the jumper reproduces every published node list and pricing it at BLOCKED reproduces none of the five (regression plant jumper_pays_blocked, red on 5 of the 8 gates of tests/jump16402.rs). On the shipped arena the cost-7 water DOES move a jumper's route: from the river centre (9500, 12500) the Hog Rider's published list runs through the water cells (26,32), (25,31), (24,30) -- the diagonal to the bridge's far corner cell (27,33), cheaper at 7 than the detour at DEFAULT 8 -- where a walker's never touches water (the fixture's Hog Rider case; tests/jump16402.rs a_jumper_routes_across_priced_water_where_a_walker_takes_the_bridge); from the lane placements (x 3500 / 14500) the straight line north IS a bridge column, so the flag is invisible there. The HOP -- what the walk does when its next node is water -- is movement.JUMP_WATER_HOP, not this table. The `action` text above ('Does ground A* cross water at 7? NO') stands for walkers.

LOGIC_SPAWN_PATHFIND_REACHED_RADIUS_FROM.provenance: MEASURED on client 16.402 from the state-6 frames of 20260920-083112-A and -B (data/derived/replay, truth.path_cells: the unit's path, goal first). They are the only state-6 frames in the corpus: 162 Goblin Drill and 13 Miner, 5 distinct units each seen from both seats. A path node is reached when the list loses its tail between two consecutive ticks; the distances below are from the unit's position after that tick's move to the node's cell centre, counted once per unit and tick. Goblin Drill (SpawnPathfindSpeed 300): the 44 reached nodes are at most 286.1 away and the 41 kept tail nodes at least 306.9 away, so the radius lies in [286.1, 306.9); 300 fits 44 of 44 and 41 of 41. Miner (SpawnPathfindSpeed 650): its 6 reached nodes are up to 580.8 away (no frame keeps a tail node), so a radius of 300 misses 4 of the 6. No single fixed radius fits both units; each unit's own SpawnPathfindSpeed fits every frame. THE RIVAL, the flag false, is the ordinary WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RADIUS of 1000: it would have reached all 41 kept Drill nodes, 0 of 41 kept. NOT SEPARATED: a test before the move with twice the speed fits too (the Drill's window measured that way is [586.2, 605.3), which holds 600); both are a radius from speed, and the unit moves straight at its node so they agree. Also recorded, not modelled: on 1 of the Miner's 5 reaching ticks it reaches two nodes in one tick, where an ordinary walk reaches at most one. Recorded by the client instrument that records ground-truth traces from the real game.
LOGIC_SPAWN_PATHFIND_REACHED_RADIUS_FROM.meaning: The 'waypoint reached' radius for spawn pathfinding is the unit's SpawnPathfindSpeed (per tick) rather than WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RADIUS.
LOGIC_SPAWN_PATHFIND_REACHED_RADIUS_FROM.engine: Not read by the engine: no engine card walks in state 6 (movement.SPAWN_PATHFIND_STATES).
LOGIC_SPAWN_PATHFIND_REACHED_RADIUS_FROM.promotion_rules: Measured on two speeds from one battle, and only two cards carry a SpawnPathfindSpeed in the 15.535 card files (Miner 650, GoblinDrillDig 300). A Miner track with frames that keep a tail node would bound the Miner's side from above; today it is only bounded below.
