PATHFINDING_FRIENDLYONLY_OCCLUSIONS.datamined_flag_disagrees: THE VALUE STANDS -- the flag really is TRUE in the shipped 15.535.29 globals.csv, and this key records what the data says. What it does NOT describe is the pathfinder the game runs: MEASURED on the LIVE 16.402 client, the occluder set is EVERY BUILDING ON THE BOARD, both sides (see OCCLUSION_MODEL, which is the key the engine reads). Friendly-only occlusion fails 119 of 785 live first paths; adding the other side's buildings fixes 113 and breaks 0 (the path sweeps, sweep [b]: 'own buildings only, cost 50' 119 suboptimal vs 'own + ENEMY buildings, cost 50' 6). The independent corpus reads 290/292 -> 292/292. Live traces: 13 captures, both sides, CR 16.402. So either the flag means something narrower than its name (dynamic occluders only? a different subsystem?) or the live build ignores it; nothing here establishes which, and the ledger records the measurement over the datamined name. The decomposition is worth carrying: ~107 of the 113 are the enemy KING footprint and only ~6 are non-king enemy buildings -- 3 to 5 cell-for-cell witnesses (a Goblin Hut at (14500,22500), a Cannon at (14500,12500), a Goblin Hut at (2500,22500)). Real, but thin, and a cheap confirming experiment would settle it.
PATHFINDING_FRIENDLYONLY_OCCLUSIONS.gate: The G6 fixture now carries each building's owner. Every occluders_native entry of crates/royalesim/tests/fixtures/oracle2026/client16402_first_paths.json is [x, y, CollisionRadius, owner side], the side on the same 0/1 scale as the case's own side (tools/make_client16402_paths_fixture.py). The fixture holds 4608 buildings over 747 cases: 2414 the mover's own and 2194 the other side's; 90 cases carry an enemy building that is not a crown tower. tests/oracle2026.rs g6_friendly_only_occlusion_is_a_control_the_published_paths_refute plans every scored G6 case twice, once with every building stamped and once with only the mover's own, scores both exactly as G6 does (the published node list, goal first, the three moving-target cases skipped) and prints both scores. It fails unless friendly-only reproduces fewer live paths, the same number of offline lane-sweep paths, and no path the side-blind arm misses. g6_fixture_each_king_is_owned_by_the_side_whose_half_it_stands_in checks the owner tag against where each king stands, so a swapped tag cannot pass. The 119 of 785 above and the 336/388 in docs/pathfinding.md were taken on earlier corpora; the current friendly-only score is the one the gate prints.

REPLAN_TRIGGERS.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. Trigger 1 (the goal cell moves): 137/137 predicted goal-cell flips are followed by a replan, 0 predicted flips produce none and 0 replans are unexplained; lag {1 tick: 128, 2 ticks: 9}. It fires for a MOVING target the same way -- in meet/Knight_vs_HogRider the Knight replans every 3-5 ticks, all goal-cell moves. Trigger 2 (a friendly building enters the world): the replan lands on the tick the entity first exists, 0 ticks of lag, +1 tick from the accepted deploy command -- command at 160, entity first in a frame at 161, path already replanned in that frame, in both repath_Giant traces, which produce opposite-sign detours from the same state.
REPLAN_TRIGGERS.scope: Friendly TROOPS are not a trigger and do not enter the path grid: a Giant walking directly behind a friendly Knight has 2 structural path changes in 316 path ticks (meet/Knight_then_Giant_behind). Troops are a movement-time term (CONTACT_DOMAIN), not a pathfinding one. ENEMY troops are off the grid too -- LIVE 16.402, 63 of 467 paths cross an enemy-occupied cell, so rule 8.6 generalises.
REPLAN_TRIGGERS.engine_contract: A replan recomputes the ENTIRE remaining route, never a spliced local bypass: the detour appears in the first path the unit publishes, ten rows (5 tiles) ahead of the obstacle, and rows far beyond it legitimately shift.
REPLAN_TRIGGERS.limits: TRIGGER 2 IS NARROWER THAN THE OCCLUDER SET, AND THAT GAP IS DELIBERATE. OCCLUSION_MODEL moved the occluder set to EVERY building on the board, both sides; this trigger is still 'a FRIENDLY building enters the world', because that is the only thing measured -- the offline corpus only ever dropped friendly buildings, and the live 16.402 measurements examined neither the repath trigger nor building REMOVAL. So in royalesim an enemy building appearing changes what the next plan would return without arming a replan by itself (state.rs `build_obstacles` hashes friendly obstacles only); the goal-cell trigger usually replans anyway. Inventing a trigger nothing measured would be worse than the gap. OPEN: dropping a building in front of an ENEMY unit on the live client and timing the heading change against the same experiment on a friendly one would settle it.

HEURISTIC_FORM.superseded_by: SUPERSEDED BY pathfinding.PATH_SEARCH = client16402, whose search uses an octile h = 5 x (10 max + 4 min) to ONE goal cell and reproduces the recorded node sequences outright. The scores below were measured on the trace-fitted arm (path2026.rs), which is kept runnable as the refuted arm; this key steers only that arm.
HEURISTIC_FORM.formula: h(cell) = min over the GOAL SET of PATHFINDING_DEFAULTHEURISTIC_COST * max(|dc|, |dr|), i.e. 5 * Chebyshev, with the goal set unchanged (see why_the_goal_set).
HEURISTIC_FORM.provenance: MEASURED. LIVE CLIENT, CR 16.402 -- recorded from the real game and converted to the offline trace format; 13 captures. Analysis: the expansion pass (exact node-sequence reproduction; corpus 337 first paths, 292 after de-duplicating the two two-client pairs). Report: the live 16.402 measurements. HANDED THE RECORDED GOAL CELL, exact node-sequence reproduction: the engine's shipped ortho-first + octile 78/292; Dijkstra (h = 0) 171/292; forward A* with strict-< relaxation, entered-cell costs and h = W * max(|dc|, |dr|) for W in 3..5, 192/292 (65.8 %). Offline, the same sweep on lane_sweep_Knight reads 36/128 for Chebyshev against 14/128 for ortho-first + octile, so this is not a 16.402 change -- it is a better fit on both builds. THE WEIGHT IS NOT PINNED: W = 3, 4 and 5 are indistinguishable on this corpus; 5 is taken because it is the shipped PATHFINDING_DEFAULTHEURISTIC_COST, a datamined constant that fits rather than a fitted one. With the reach PREDICATE as the goal test instead of the handed goal cell the best falls to 142/292, which is the goal-cell question (PATH_GOAL_RULE `limits`), not the heuristic's.
HEURISTIC_FORM.admissibility: 5 * Chebyshev is admissible and consistent against this cost field, so REOPEN_CLOSEDNODES = FALSE stays safe and the returned path is still exactly cost-minimal. The cheapest cell costs road = 5 to enter and the cheapest diagonal 5 * 1414/1000 = 7, so a route of Chebyshev distance N costs at least 5N; and h changes by at most 5 across any neighbour while a diagonal step costs at least 7. crates/royalesim/src/path2026.rs `the_measured_heuristic_is_chebyshev_and_both_forms_are_admissible` asserts the consequence directly -- swapping the form may not change what a path COSTS.
HEURISTIC_FORM.why_the_goal_set: ADMISSIBILITY TRAP, and it is not cosmetic. THIS HALF IS UNCHANGED BY THE 16.402 PROMOTION -- only the metric inside the minimum changed. The goal is 'any cell within reach of the target' (PATH_GOAL_RULE), so a heuristic computed to the TARGET cell over-estimates the cost to the actual goal by up to reach/500 * 5 and is non-zero at goal cells -- A* then pops a goal that is not the cheapest one. Measured on the walk traces: with h to the target cell the search returns column 7 (cost 152) instead of the recorded column 6 (cost 150) for every one of the six cards; with h as the min over the in-reach cells it returns the recorded path.
HEURISTIC_FORM.still_not_reproduced: The heuristic does not change WHICH paths are optimal (the cost model was validated with Dijkstra), only the expansion order. 192/292 is a ceiling, not a solution: the residual has one systematic signature -- the recorded path shifts column one cell EARLIER than the model, always immediately after a road/bridge segment (witnesses 20260918-112215:25:MiniPekka and 20260918-112751:7:Giant both 8,33 -> 7,32 -> 7,31 -> 8,30 where the model stays 7,30; 112751:32:Musketeer 5,39 -> 6,38 vs 5,38). A heuristic charging more than the 11-vs-8 diagonal premium for a one-column offset would produce it, but every b - a >= 4 member of h = a*(max-min) + b*min scores far worse overall. It may not be a heap A* at all: a different heuristic form, a post-processing pass over the raw route and a hierarchical search are all still live. Keep it swappable.

HEURISTIC_FORM.dropped_candidates: `octile_to_target_cell_minus_reach` and `none` were removed from the candidate list because royalesim implements no arm for either, so naming one in `value` would be refused at load (state.rs `pick`) rather than silently substituted. The registry may still LIST alternatives the engine does not run, as the only()-backed keys do (state.rs documents that); only the value has to resolve. Their evidence is not lost: `octile_to_target_cell_minus_reach` is the admissibility trap described in why_the_goal_set and is refuted on the walk traces, and `none` is Dijkstra, measured at 171/292 above. HEURISTIC_FORM.engine_contract: royalesim reads this into Calib::heuristic_form (state.rs) and path2026.rs `heuristic_weights` SELECTS the chamfer weights from it -- (5, 5) for Chebyshev, (5, 7) for octile -- which `goal_set_heuristic` then runs as a two-pass transform (exact for any weights with straight <= diag <= 2*straight). Both listed candidates are wired; a name with no arm is refused at load, never silently substituted. This key used to be read by `only()` and not stored at all, so its value could not have been changed without an engine edit.
HEURISTIC_FORM.promotion_rules: Raise to HIGH by reproducing the node sequence, not by scoring it better than its rivals: 192/292 is a large improvement and still a minority. Re-open the WEIGHT (3, 4 and 5 are indistinguishable) with a corpus whose h-weight is discriminating, which requires a board where the heuristic's inflation changes the pop order.

TIE_BREAK.provenance: UNVERIFIED AND KNOWN TO BE INSUFFICIENT. Where several successors are equally optimal the recorded paths prefer the orthogonal one on 1568 of 1672 ambiguous steps (93.8 %), but an ortho-first neighbour order still reproduces only 22/140 exact node sequences, and with the sqrt(2) diagonal exact ties are rare -- so the residual divergence is not a classic tie-break at all. 76 distinct experiments over neighbour order x queue discipline x relaxation rule; none exceeds 13/76. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md.
TIE_BREAK.why_it_may_be_unreachable: The recorded path_nodes is a POST-TICK snapshot: a repath can insert one or two nodes below the old waypoint that the unit aims at and consumes within the same tick, so they appear in no recorded frame. 142 ticks in the corpus show this; all carry path_node_consumed == 1 and 140 are explained exactly by a cell 1-2 rows nearer in the same column. Any pathfinder fitted to the recorded node lists is missing those insertions.
TIE_BREAK.why_the_knob_provably_cannot_matter: LIVE 16.402, the expansion sweep over the live corpus: 36 combinations of 6 open-list keys x 6 neighbour orders produce ZERO different paths across 418 samples. The reason is structural, not statistical -- with strict-`<` relaxation and an f-first heap, rival parents of a cell differ in g by 2, 3 or 6 while their h differs by 0 or one cell-weight, so an f-tie between them essentially never occurs and the neighbour order never gets a vote. The offline 1040-configuration sweep therefore had at most ~5 genuinely distinct members. THE VALUE STAYS A PLACEHOLDER AND IT IS A HARMLESS ONE; the note below that 'the three orders give a DIFFERENT path on only 25 of 6802 engine problems' is the same fact measured on the engine's own grid. Whatever settles the expansion order will have to change the open-list key or the algorithm, not the neighbour list -- and the leading suspects are now the HEURISTIC (promoted to chebyshev_over_goal_set on the same corpus, 78/292 -> 192/292) and the possibility that it is not a heap A* at all.
TIE_BREAK.promotion_rules: Do not record a tie-break as settled on this corpus. Settle it with a scenario whose optimum is unique but whose EXPANSION order is observable, or by the measured 16.402 search itself (PATH_SEARCH = client16402 settles it). Note that a scenario cannot settle it while the relaxation stays strict-`<`: see why_the_knob_provably_cannot_matter.
TIE_BREAK.engine_contract: royalesim reads this key into Calib::tie_break and path2026.rs `neighbours()` SELECTS the neighbour order from it -- the three candidates above are the three the engine implements, and Calib::from_json refuses any other name. It used to be read and then ignored, with one hardcoded order underneath, so two of the three values named a discipline that never ran. MEASURED while wiring it: the neighbour order reaches the result ONLY through the push counter in the open-list key (f, then the smaller h, then FIFO), so over a 6802-problem sweep on the shipped grid the three orders give a DIFFERENT path on only 25, and never a different cost. Whatever settles spec 3.6 will therefore have to change the open-list key, not just the neighbour list (path2026.rs `OpenKey`). The two candidates cw_from_n / ccw_from_n were dropped from this list because the engine does not implement them; add them back together with their arms.

OCCLUSION_MODEL.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). OCCLUSION_MODEL.limits: The 500-unit cell quantum brackets the Cannon and the princess tower only to (500, 1000], so the data does NOT show the box scales with CollisionRadius -- it shows that one unfitted rule at three shipped radii reproduces the three observed footprints. A CLOSED box and a ONE-NATIVE-UNIT mover pad each claim 100 cells of the recorded paths over the 37-case fixture -- crates/royalesim/tests/oracle2026.rs `the_two_rival_occlusion_shapes_are_the_ones_the_corpus_refutes` asserts it, so 'half-open, no pad' is falsifiable in the repo rather than only in this text. Still open after the live pass: rule A vs rule H (a square of half-width CollisionRadius, against the building's own tile grown by half a tile) predict identical cells, because every occluder in BOTH corpora also sits on a tile centre.
OCCLUSION_MODEL.king_footprint_bracket: THE KING FOOTPRINT IS MEASURED, both ways, and the shipped CollisionRadius 1400 is inside the bracket. The OFFLINE corpus cannot see it -- nothing in it approaches a king, so R_king = 0 scores identically to 1400 (0/0) there and only R >= 2000 fails. Sweep over 785 first paths (the live path sweeps, king arm): R_king in {0, 500, 1000} -> 113 failures (the extra 107 are enemy-king approaches), {1001, 1250, 1400, 1500} -> 6, 1501 -> 144 (27 extra near the own king, 111 near the enemy). The Goblin Hut is bracketed to (500, 1000] the same way and goblin_hut_rework.toml ships 1000, inside it.
OCCLUSION_MODEL.occluder_set: EVERY BUILDING ON THE BOARD, BOTH SIDES. MEASURED on the LIVE 16.402 client. This supersedes the offline reading 'the DEPLOYER'S OWN, including its own crown towers' in `provenance` above, which held on the offline corpus only because nothing in it ever walked near an enemy building: there, adding the enemy towers as occluders scores identically (0/0/0), because no interior cell of any first path lies inside an enemy tower box, so the datamined PATHFINDING_FRIENDLYONLY_OCCLUSIONS = TRUE looked consistent with it. Live: friendly-only fails 119 of 785 first paths, own + enemy fails 6 -- 113 fixed, 0 broken (the live path sweeps, occluder arm); the independent corpus reads 290/292 -> 292/292. ~107 of the 113 are the enemy KING footprint and ~6 are non-king enemy buildings, resting on 3-5 cell-for-cell witnesses (cell-for-cell, in the live corpus) -- act on it, but that half is thin. Live traces: the live corpus, 13 captures of CR 16.402 (two pairs are the same battle recorded from both clients, byte-identical in path_nodes on all 45 overlapping paths -- an independent check on the capture, and a reason the raw counts double those samples).
OCCLUSION_MODEL.engine_divergence_target_building: KNOWN, DELIBERATE, AND NOT MEASURED EITHER WAY. royalesim exempts the building a unit is currently attacking from its own occluder set (state.rs `NavRequest.ignore`, path2026.rs `CostField::for_mover`). The scored reference model (779/785) does NOT -- it occludes every building including the target, and that is how the 97 enemy-king crossings were scored, so on a unit walking at a king the two models differ: the reference model charges 50 for the last cells, the engine sees plain terrain under them (and the bit-16 goal exemption, OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT, carries the goal cell). Kept because it is the older separately-argued rule -- a unit must be able to reach the thing it is attacking -- and because removing it is not free: with the box gone the engine would need the goal exemption back for exactly those cells. It costs nothing on any gate in the repo. OPEN: scoring the live corpus with the target building exempted would settle it; the corpus already has the 97 king approaches that discriminate.
OCCLUSION_MODEL.corpus: RE-SCORED 2026-09-18 after the oracle2026 fixture was regenerated from the traces (tools/make_oracle2026_fixture.py): the box admits ALL 37 published first paths -- no INTERIOR cell of any of them lies inside a friendly box. The three cases previously recorded here as 'the model's domain showing its edge' were a FIXTURE defect, not a model limit: the occluding building's centre had been taken from the deploy COMMAND, and the game snaps a deploy to a tile (cannon_dx-0.5 commanded x = 3000 and the Cannon stands at 3500), plus a Tesla's CollisionRadius is 500 in csv_logic, not the 600 that had been assumed. Two consequences worth keeping: (a) cannon_dx-0.5 and cannon_dx+0.5 snap onto dx+0.0 and dx+1.0, so the building corpus is 10 distinct boards, not 12; (b) the Tesla runs put a building on a tile CORNER (3000, 9000) and (2000, 9000), not a tile centre, and the box admits them -- so the 'building on a tile centre' scoping below is narrower than it looked. A half-tile building sweep is still owed; the corpus does not contain one.

OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.meaning: An occluded cell is ENTERED at PATHFINDING_BUILDING_COST = 50 (the entered-cell cost, so a diagonal pays 50 * DIAGONAL_COST_RATIO = 70). It is not a wall.

Analysis: the cost-model / occlusion / goal-rule fit, driven by the path sweeps and cross-checked against an independent 292-path corpus. THE DISCRIMINATOR THE OFFLINE CORPUS LACKED: 97 of 785 live paths cross a building-box INTERIOR -- always exactly one cell, always the cell before the goal, always inside the enemy king's R = 1400 box ((17,8) x68 and (18,8) x17 for side-1 units attacking the side-0 king, (18,55) x9 and (17,55) x3 the other way). Scores over the 785 (the live path sweeps, own + enemy occluders throughout): hard block with no goal exemption 6 suboptimal + 456 infeasible; hard block WITH the goal exemption 20 suboptimal + 97 infeasible; cost 50 6 suboptimal + 0 infeasible. The independent 292-path corpus: 257 pass under hard block, 292 under cost 50.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.the_value_is_bracketed_not_pinned: Anything >= 14 scores identically: cost 12 -> 114 failures, 13 -> 99, 14 / 16 / 20 / 25 / 50 / 100 / 1000 -> 6. Also open: whether the occluded cost REPLACES the terrain cost or is ADDED to it. Every discriminating cell in the corpus is road (5) or plain (8), so 50 and 50 + terrain are indistinguishable at this resolution; the engine replaces.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.an_alternative_reading_survives: All 97 crossings are the ENEMY KING. OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.promotion_rules: SETTLED as 'a cost, not a block'. Re-open only against a capture that shows a path refusing a strictly cheaper crossing, or against a second reading of the same corpus. The exact CONSTANT is a separate question (see the_value_is_bracketed_not_pinned) and is still open below 50.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.scope: APPLIES TO BUILDING OCCLUSION BOXES ONLY -- never to water, and, since 2026-09-18, no longer to bit-16 terrain either. WATER: the two used to share one branch in path2026.rs `CostField::terrain`, so selecting `cost_50` here silently made the river traversable and overrode WATER_RULE_GROUND, which Calib::from_json refuses to load with any value but `impassable`. BIT-16: the same defect, one key deciding another's question -- `cost_50` is a statement about BUILDINGS and it used to make the deploy-restricted arena-edge strips walkable as a side effect. path2026.rs `CostField::terrain` now writes the goal-exempt OCCLUDED sentinel for bit 16 unconditionally and `CostField::occlude` overwrites it with the box cost where the two overlap (see precedence). One ledger key may not quietly override another.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.precedence: THE BOX COST TAKES PRECEDENCE OVER THE TERRAIN FLAG, and that is the actionable finding -- neither analysis stated it, and their apparent disagreement about bit 16 was entirely this. A bit-16 cell inside a building box costs 50 like any occluded cell. An engine that resolves terrain FIRST and lets an impassable bit-16 flag win costs 39 of 337 live paths, because the tilemap's bit-16 king 3x3 block IS the king tower's own R = 1400 half-open box, cell for cell. Live paths use 744 distinct cells, of which 13 carry bit 16 and ALL 13 lie inside a king box; the other 104 bit-16 cells (the arena-edge strips) are never entered by any path, and no live path touches water anywhere. So bit 16 has no measurable pathfinding meaning of its OWN -- impassable, 5, 8, 12, 50 and 1000 all score 6/785 once enemy occlusion is on -- and spec rule 2.2 is NOT refuted. It is kept impassable outside every box as the conservative reading of an unidentifiable flag.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.engine_contract: royalesim reads this into Calib::occluded_cells (state.rs) and path2026.rs `CostField::occlude` selects the value it stamps: PATHFINDING_BUILDING_COST under `cost_50`, the goal-exempt OCCLUDED sentinel under `block`. Both candidates are wired and a name with no arm is refused at load. The SHAPE is kept separately from the cost -- `CostField::in_building_box` answers 'is this cell inside a box' whichever treatment is selected -- because under `cost_50` nothing is refused and every gate that asked `refused` would have passed vacuously.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.goal_cell_exemption: SPEC 4.6 BECOMES UNNECESSARY, and deleting it is an improvement. 456 of 785 live goal cells sit inside a building box, so under the old hard-block reading the exemption was load-bearing; under cost 50 it can go and the score IMPROVES -- 6 failures without it against 12 with it, otherwise identical settings. In royalesim the exemption is now unreachable for building boxes (they are a price, not the sentinel) and survives only on the bit-16 king block, where it is what keeps a short-reach card able to path to a king tower at all and where the live corpus cannot see it either way (path2026.rs OCCLUDED).

PATH_GOAL_RULE.superseded_by: SUPERSEDED BY pathfinding.PATH_SEARCH = client16402, whose ONE goal cell comes from `choose_goal_cell` in path16402.rs. The rule below is read only by the trace-fitted arm (path2026.rs), kept runnable as the refuted arm.
PATH_GOAL_RULE.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. The path is truncated at the FIRST cell whose CENTRE is within Range + CollisionRadius of the TARGET'S CENTRE POINT -- the target's centre, not its footprint, and not the sum of both collision radii. Verified two-sided (the goal is in reach AND its predecessor is out of reach) on 150/150 first paths, including the meet/ traces with moving targets and side-1 units. Rivals: 'Range only' 1/140, 'Range + both radii' 0/140, 'footprint edge' 0/140. Per-card stop cells from one deploy tile: Giant (reach 1950) row 47; Knight 1700, Golem 1500, HogRider 1400 all row 48; MiniPekka 1250 and Skeletons 1000 row 49.
PATH_GOAL_RULE.limits: NECESSARY, NOT DETERMINATIVE. It is a condition on the last node, not a predictor of which cell the search stops at: between 12 and 52 cells per sample satisfy it (median 32) and the recorded goal cell is not the cheapest reachable in-reach cell in 114 of 140 samples, with no cost ties among them. Handing an A* the recorded goal cell raises exact-sequence reproduction from 22/140 to 43/140 -- THE GOAL CELL IS AN OUTPUT OF THE EXPANSION ORDER. Implement the reach test as the goal PREDICATE and let the pop order choose; do not implement 'pick the nearest or cheapest in-reach cell'. A constant k added to Range + CollisionRadius fits all 150 paths for any k in [-125.2, +24.8), so the reach is pinned to about +-75 units, not exactly.
PATH_GOAL_RULE.sign: The standoff is on the APPROACH side, not unconditionally negative in y: in meet/Knight_vs_HogRider ticks 250-273 the Knight's target is BELOW it and the goal row is cell_centre_y + reach. An unconditional minus puts the goal on the far side of the target. The predicate form (a radius about the target centre) carries this for free.
PATH_GOAL_RULE.cadence: Re-derive the goal cell every tick and replan only when the resulting CELL changes (REPLAN_TRIGGERS): that reproduces the 137 observed goal-driven replans with the observed 1-2 tick lag.

WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RADIUS.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. At most ONE node is consumed per tick: 0 of 3851 tail-drop ticks dropped more than one. Threshold sweep on the post-move Euclidean distance: 1000 is the one-sided exact value (zero false drops across 27824 keep-ticks); 1001 buys 27 fewer misses and costs 3 false drops, 1003 gives 107 total against 148, 1005 and beyond are worse. NOT TUNED to hide the residual -- see WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RULE, which explains it instead.

candidate_meanings.segment_projection: Consume the tail node when the REMAINING DISTANCE ALONG THE SEGMENT, dot(node_centre - post_move_position, segment_direction) / 256 with integer truncation, is <= WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RADIUS. segment_direction is the 1/256 unit vector frozen when the node was assigned (norm256(node_centre - POST-move position), the engine's own path_segment_direction field).
candidate_meanings.euclid_post_move: the pathfinder spec's rule 7.5 as written: consume when the post-move EUCLIDEAN distance (floored integer sqrt) to the node centre is <= WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RADIUS.

WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RULE.provenance: MEASURED, and it SUPERSEDES the spec's rule 7.5 on the same corpus. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. Scored over all 34644 stable-list tick pairs (3975 ordinary drops, 30669 keeps) (reproduced by tools/oracle_diff.py --rule): euclid_post_move misses 153 drops and fires 3 times early (156 errors); segment_projection misses 6 and fires 10 times early (16 errors), and ALL TEN of its early fires carry avoidance_offset != 0 (110, 190, 150, 140, 130, -160) -- the avoidance regime that is outside the domain of every movement law here (CONTACT_DOMAIN). On the walk family (the isolated-unit gate) segment_projection has ZERO errors; euclid_post_move misses 4, which is exactly why the spec expected '~4 % of pop ticks to diverge'. The mechanism it adds was already in the spec as rule 7.7 -- the segment direction is frozen at consumption and held for the whole segment, zero exceptions on the walk traces -- it was simply never connected to the consumption predicate.
WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RULE.disproof_of_a_pure_radius: No radius on the post-move distance can be right: restricted to ISOLATED units (single-unit traces, avoidance_offset == 0, behavior_state == 1) the Knight corpus contains a DROP at distance 1004.478 and a KEEP at 1000.648, so drops and keeps overlap in distance. They do not overlap in the projection.
WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RULE.engine_contract: royalesim stores the frozen direction per entity (entity.seg_dir) and evaluates the predicate AFTER the move, at most one pop per tick (state.rs phase_path_2026). Setting this key to euclid_post_move runs the spec's rule 7.5 instead.

LEVEL_SCALING.note: The old engine used 1.1^(level-1), which drifts from level 4 onward (1065, 1171, 1288...). It also scaled princess towers at level 11 while leaving the king at level 1, putting the two tower types on different regimes inside one match.

STAT_BASE_LEVEL.formula: stat(L) = floor(base * ladder(objectRarity)[L - RelativeLevel(objectRarity)] / 100), where `base` is the row's own column value, `objectRarity` the Rarity column of the OBJECT carrying the stat (the character / projectile / area-effect row), and the CARD's rarity only bounds L to RelativeLevel(card) + 1 ..= RelativeLevel(card) + LevelCount(card)
STAT_BASE_LEVEL.provenance: MEASURED on the live 16.402 captures: every unit's level and maximum hitpoints over all 73 captures (tools/make_live_levels_fixture.py -> crates/royalesim/tests/fixtures/live_levels.json): 95 of 109 distinct (card, level, max_hp) rows across 61 cards at levels 3, 4, 5, 6, 11 and 12 are floor(base x Common ladder[L] / 100) of the 15.535 row (Knight 690 -> 834 at 3, 1104 at 6, 1766 at 11; the RARE Hog Rider 663 -> 1697 at 11; the Rare Musketeer 282 -> 451 at 6, 721 at 11; the Epic Prince 750 -> 1920; the Legendary Bandit 354 -> 906). The other candidate, the card's own rarity ladder from its local level 1 (the 2018 file's convention, where the character row carried the card's rarity: Hog Rider Rare 800 at unified 3), gives that Hog 663 x 212 % = 1405 and the Musketeer 597 -- no live row has them. The 14 unmatched rows are 15.535 -> 16.402 balance changes (Ice Golem 514 -> 480, the Spirits 85 -> 84, Goblin Brawler 422 -> 438) and units the extractor's spawn walk does not reach (the Goblin Drill's building), listed in the fixture with a note each. In 15.535 every base object's Rarity column is Common (unified level-1 bases); the Skeleton Army's SummonCharacterLevelIndex 5 (= Epic RelativeLevel) is the same rule seen from the card side in both vintages. Rounding: floor, separated by the Musketeer (721.92 -> 721) and the Hog Rider (1697.28 -> 1697).
STAT_BASE_LEVEL.towers: NOT this ladder: the same captures give the king 3312 / 4824 and the princess 2030 / 3052 at tower levels 6 / 11 against the 2400 / 1400 rows -- the tower regime is its own key, TOWER_HITPOINT_LADDER (measured: the globals' per-level percent compounded with an integer floor per level, 7 / 8 to level 9 and 10 above), applied to the two tower records in BattleState::spawn_now.

STAT_BASE_LEVEL.engine: tools/extract_cards.py writes the decision into cards.json (`level_scaling.reading`, `base_level`, `ladder_rarity`, the ladder rarity's table; `--level-base` selects the candidate); card.rs `level_table_of` refuses a reading it does not implement and `level_multiplier` enters the table at level - base_level (plant level_card_rarity_local: the card ladder from local 1 whatever the block says, red on tests/levels.rs); tools/check_data.py refuses a cards.json built under a reading other than this value. ATTACK_CYCLE.confidence: HIGH -- measured on 1690 fresh attack entries and 911 first projectile launches of the live corpus (below); the windup arm misses every one of them
ATTACK_CYCLE.provenance: MEASURED on the whole live 16.402 corpus (73 captures): the captures carry two per-unit attack counters, and on the frame a unit starts attacking a fresh target they read LoadTime + 50 and LoadTime on 1690 of 2024 entries (the misses are spawned units filed under their spawner's card, whose LoadTime is not the spawner's); 911 of 1004 projectile units launched their first projectile exactly (HitSpeed - LoadTime) / 50 - 1 ticks after that frame (Musketeer 13, Archers 9, Bomber 3, Bowler 9, princess tower 15, king tower 9; the misses are interrupted cycles); 453 of 520 uninterrupted melee cycles dropped the target's hp on that tick (Knight 9, Barbarian 7, Skeleton 9, Goblin 11); 113 of 172 re-entries with the second counter still running show the first at LoadTime + 50 - (load - 50); every later hit HitSpeed apart, the first counter running on across hits (1400, 2800, 4200 on a Prince) and the second reset to LoadTime on every hit. The princess tower of capture 20260920-003751: attacking at t280, progress 50, the first arrow at t295 (progress 800), then t311 and t327; the engine fired on the acquisition tick. THE RULE (combat.rs attack_step_progress): every tick the LOAD TIMER counts down 50 clamped at 0, whatever the state; with a target, the unit attacks this tick when the target is in range (targeting.ATTACK_RANGE_RULE) OR a hit is already started (progress % HitSpeed > 50), else its progress is RESET to 0 and it stops attacking; attacking, a fresh cycle (progress == 0, not charged) is CREDITED progress = LoadTime - loadTimer (with loadTimer := LoadTime) and then += 50, so a unit whose load timer has run out starts its first cycle at LoadTime + 50 and every later tick adds 50; when LoadTime > HitSpeed no credit is given and the cycle waits until the load timer is <= HitSpeed; a CHARGED entry snaps progress to the next multiple of HitSpeed instead (charge.CHARGED_HIT_TIMING). THE HIT lands on the tick progress crosses a multiple of HitSpeed, which sets loadTimer := LoadTime and leaves progress running. So the FIRST hit on a fresh target lands (HitSpeed - LoadTime) / 50 - 1 ticks after the entry frame, the cadence is HitSpeed, and a unit re-entering range within LoadTime of its last hit or entry gets only LoadTime - (remaining load) of credit. TWO BOUNDARIES OF THE RULE, both corrected against the corpus: (a) the hit-started test is STRICTLY GREATER than 50, not >= 50 -- a fire leaves the progress on an exact multiple of HitSpeed, so the next credited tick puts the remainder at exactly 50 on every cycle of every shipped card (Knight 1250 % 1200, Prince 1450 % 1400, Musketeer 1050 % 1000), and under >= a unit whose target stepped out of reach on that tick kept swinging instead of resetting; the corpus moves with the correction (Skeletons 43.6 -> 43.9 % within 250 with the alive-mismatch share 14.6 -> 13.5 %, Bomber 75.8 -> 76.1 %). (b) A HELD unit's load timer keeps counting down: the hold (a -100 HitSpeedMultiplier, combat.HIT_SPEED_BUFF) stops the PROGRESS step alone, so a unit frozen mid-cooldown does not keep its whole remaining reload and its first hit after the hold is not LoadTime / 50 ticks late.
ATTACK_CYCLE.meaning: progress_credit: the measured progress counter -- first hit HitSpeed - LoadTime after entering range (a princess tower, LoadTime blank = 0, waits a full HitSpeed = 16 ticks for its first arrow), HitSpeed between hits, a swing already started finishes on a target that stepped out of range, the load timer's remainder reduces the credit on re-entry. windup_load_time: the earlier engine -- a LoadTime windup after entering range, then HitSpeed - LoadTime of cooldown -- so every first hit landed 2 x LoadTime - HitSpeed later than the game's (a Knight 400 ms late, a princess tower 800 ms EARLY).
ATTACK_CYCLE.promotion_rules: Measured. The hit-speed buff is combat.HIT_SPEED_BUFF (Rage's HitSpeedMultiplier into the 50 ms step); LoadFirstHit (Sparky) is not modelled. Re-open only against a live first hit that parts from the rule on an uninterrupted cycle.
ATTACK_CYCLE.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json -> attack_cycle); combat.rs attack_step runs the progress / load-timer counters (Entities::attack_ms = progress, Entities::attack_load_ms = the load timer, snapshot format 16), AttackPhase::Windup = attacking with the swing under way (the target lock), Cooldown = attacking on the hit tick, Idle = not attacking; the Path phase holds any attacking unit. The old arm stays runnable as windup_load_time. tests/reach.rs pins the tower's first arrow and the Knight's first hit from the card data.

RETARGET_PROGRESS.meaning_keep_when_dead_or_in_reach: keep_when_dead_or_in_reach: as keep_when_dead when the old target died; when a unit switches away from a live target to one already inside its attack range (Range + both radii) on that tick, it keeps its attack progress and stays in its attack, so the next hit lands on the new target on the running cycle; a switch to a target out of range cancels the swing as before. RETARGET_PROGRESS.meaning: keep_when_dead: a unit whose target DIED keeps its attack progress and fires on its own cadence; switching away from a target still ALIVE cancels the swing as before. reset_always: any target change cancels, which is what the engine did before this key existed. The size of the difference is set by LoadTime, because the fresh cycle credits back min(LoadTime, elapsed) through the load timer (combat.ATTACK_CYCLE): a princess tower's LoadTime is 0, so under reset_always it lost the whole interval and reloaded in 19 ticks instead of 16, while a Musketeer's 300 ms covered the gap and it measured the same under both arms.
RETARGET_PROGRESS.promotion_rules: Measured on two populations. What would REOPEN it: a scenario where a unit switches away from a LIVE target -- this key says nothing about that case, which still cancels, and nothing here measured it. A client 15.535.29 scenario would settle both halves at once by firing at a swarm and at a passing target. reset_always is kept runnable as the arm the engine shipped through 2026-09-23, so the defect can be reproduced rather than only described.
RETARGET_PROGRESS.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json -> retarget_progress); applied in state.rs phase_target, which suppresses BOTH routes into the cancel -- the `changed` test and target.rs's cancel_attack, which is the route a LOCKED unit whose target dies actually takes. Gating only `changed` leaves the tower's own case untouched.
RETARGET_PROGRESS.open: Whether the game cancels a swing when a unit switches away from a live target at all. This engine keeps that behaviour because nothing measured it, not because anything confirmed it.

START_MANA.measured_2026_09_22_tick0_ramp:
Read off truth.elixir_raw of all 73 regenerated replay fixtures, every one of which now carries it (data/derived/replay; 10,000 raw is one elixir). Rates are counted only on CONSECUTIVE-tick pairs that ROSE, so a spend and a full bar cannot enter the count. 63 of the 73 fixtures begin at tick 0, giving 126 (side, tick-0) readings. ALL 126 read raw 60000, which is 6 elixir. None reads 5.

IS THAT THE START VALUE, OR THE START VALUE PLUS REGEN ALREADY CREDITED? Three things say it is the start value. (a) The tick-0 raw is EXACTLY 60000, which is exactly 6 elixir. 5 elixir plus one tick of the 1x rate would be 50178, and reaching 60000 from 50000 needs 56.18 ticks of that rate, which cannot be credited to a frame labelled tick 0. (b) Where a capture publishes frames at both tick 0 and tick 1, the step between them is 178, exactly ONE tick of the 1x rate, so tick 0 is the origin of the ramp and not a point part-way up it. (c) The 126 readings AGREEING is itself the argument, not just a sign of a stable reading: elixir rises every tick, so a first frame published at an arbitrary point after the battle began would catch a different value in every capture. 126 identical readings mean tick 0 is a common anchor. The ramps check out from that anchor: 20260918-122757.b2 publishes ticks 0, 3, 4, 6, 7 as 60000, 60534, 60712, 61068, 61246, which is 60000 plus 178 per elapsed tick exactly.

TICK_ORDER.provenance: MEASURED on the 31 live 16.402 captures. THE ORDER: every unit's attack update runs before any unit moves; the move updates then run one unit after another in CREATION order -- unit i sees units j < i already moved and units j > i at their start-of-tick positions, against a spatial index and an occlusion grid built from the start-of-tick positions; the per-unit character update (the state machine and the DEPLOY COUNTDOWN) runs AFTER the move pass. THE EVIDENCE: (1) the creation order -- the units of every capture keep the order they were created in on 16151 consecutive frame pairs with no reorder, and the sequential pass in that order reproduces 98 % of the contact ticks against 46 % with previous-tick neighbours (collision.CONTACT_LAW); (2) a 1 -> 2 (walking -> attacking) transition takes effect BEFORE the move pass -- on 819 transition ticks the unit never took its walking step (621 stood still, 198 were only pushed), where an order with the move before the attack predicts a step on every one; (3) a 2 -> 1 unit walked in the SAME tick (412 / 413); (4) a 4 -> 1 (deploy finished) transition takes effect AFTER the move pass -- 398 / 445 stood still, the rest were pushed -- where a countdown run before the move predicts a full first step on that tick. movement.DEPLOY_TIMING's 'the movement state flips one tick early (4 -> 1 before the first displacement)' is the same fact seen in the offline 15.535 corpus.
TICK_ORDER.meaning: client16402: lib.rs TICK_PHASES = Upkeep, Status, Spawn, Target, Attack, Path, Move, Projectile, Resolve, Reap, Judge -- Target and Attack before Path and Move, the deploy countdown at the end of Move, the sequential move pass (state.rs phase_path16402) ordered by entity.rs `creation_seq` (a monotonic per-battle counter: the six towers take 0..5 in the order Blue king / own-left / own-right, Red king / own-left / own-right, then every spawn in queue order, so ascending creation_seq is the order the captures show). legacy_move_before_attack: lib.rs LEGACY_TICK_PHASES -- Path, Move, Attack with the deploy countdown in Upkeep, the order this engine ran before the measurement ('a unit that moves into range attacks the same tick'), under which a unit entering range winds up one tick early and a unit whose deploy ends walks on that tick; kept runnable as the refuted arm. Under both, the same three rules follow for the frame-planned path arms (phase_path_2026 / phase_path skip a Windup unit and a deploying one).
TICK_ORDER.promotion_rules: SETTLED on 819 / 413 / 445 transition ticks and 16151 frame pairs. Re-open only against a new client build; one designed capture re-verifies it: a single Knight walking into a tower's range with a frame on the transition tick (no step, state 2), and a deployed unit's first two frames after its countdown ends (state 1 with no displacement, then the full first step).
TICK_ORDER.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json, calib_enum TickOrder); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted. state.rs BattleState::tick picks TICK_PHASES or LEGACY_TICK_PHASES by it; phase_upkeep / phase_move run the deploy countdown (deploy_countdown) under the arm that owns it; tests/tick_order.rs pins the three transition rules and the creation-order visibility; the regression plant `phase_order` forces the legacy order and turns tests/tick_order.rs and every phase-traced battle red. Snapshot format 12 carries creation_seq.
TICK_ORDER.not_modelled: (1) A unit in Windup is skipped by the whole move pass (no separation push either), where the corpus's attacking unit is pushed without walking (the 198 'only pushed' transition ticks) -- the engine's Cooldown / in-range unit is pushed, its Windup unit is not. (2) The start-of-tick spatial index is `Index` in move16402.rs; the occlusion rebuild is Grid16402::refresh. (3) Projectile arrivals and spells land after the move pass here (Phase::Projectile); where they fall within the game's tick is unmeasured. (4) A unit mid-windup whose live target moves out of range keeps winding up (combat.rs attack_step tests no range in Windup; status.PRESERVE_TARGET_IF_HIT_STARTED) and does not walk that tick, where the 412 / 413 measurement counts every 2 -> 1 transition; that case is the attack rule's, not the order's.

GENERATOR.provenance: Supercell's own PRNG has never been recovered publicly. A real replay is a function of a single rndSeed int, so the generator is a REQUIRED component of reproducing a real match -- and an unavailable one.
GENERATOR.consequence: We cannot replay a real recorded match. We CAN guarantee bit-identical reproducibility within our own build, which is a different and entirely attainable property, and the one every test depends on.
GENERATOR.engine_contract: The RNG is owned by battle state and its bit-state is part of the serialized state. A replay is seed + action log + periodic state hash. The old engine had 23 module-global `random` call sites and zero occurrences of `seed`, so nothing it produced was reproducible at all.

$comment: Stated explicitly so nobody re-litigates it or quietly aims higher and stalls.
BIT-EXACT replication of Clash Royale is NOT achievable from public evidence,
and no further archaeology makes it achievable: unknown tick rate, unknown
speed divisor, unknown internal fixed-point scale and rounding, unrecovered
PRNG, unknown intra-tick ordering, and a pathfinder Supercell rewrote in 2025
and never documented -- against a data corpus that stops in 2023 and an arena
map that stopped shipping entirely.
THE TARGET IS: behavioural fidelity sufficient that strategies transfer, plus
bit-identical determinism WITHIN this build. That is RocketSim's own posture
and it was enough to train superhuman Rocket League agents.
The engine's job is to make every disputed constant cheap to change and cheap
to test, so that each measurement promotes a number instead of triggering a
rewrite.
Spell mechanics that NO shipped column settles (docs/spell-spec.md, PARTIALLY VERIFIED).
Card STATS for spells (damage, radius, pushback distance, crown percent, waves, roll
range, stun time, spawn count) are NOT here: they are card data, read from
data/derived/cards.json. WHICH VINTAGE THAT FILE HOLDS IS NOT FIXED: it is a
generated name, gitignored, and tools/extract_cards.py writes whichever vintage it
was asked for to it -- the published README's --vintage 2018 gives a clone the 2018
table under that name, a run with no flag gives the 15.535 one. Only the file's own
provenance.vintage says which is on disk, and the engine reads it at RUNTIME through
CardDb::load_repo rather than compiling it in, so the stale-build guard that covers
calibration.json, arena.json, globals.csv and rarities.csv does not cover the card
table. Anything comparing two engine results has to carry the table's hash: the
replay harness does (each report's cards_json_fixture / cards_json_engine, and
data/derived/replay/card_census.json), and that is what makes two runs comparable.
The live-2026 values the spec quotes (Fireball pushback 1000, Arrows 3 x 48 at
r 3500, Log range 10100, ...) are evidence for a data-vintage decision, not engine
inputs.

DISPLACEMENT_LAW.confidence: HIGH on the ladder (one live push, eight steps, each step discriminating); the candidates below all predict a different track
DISPLACEMENT_LAW.provenance: MEASURED on the Giant of capture 20260918-122757.b1, ticks 1216..1223, and implemented in crates/royalesim/src/move16402.rs start_pushback / pushback_step. THE LAW: a landing push does not displace the unit, it ARMS a countdown. From (dx, dy) = unit - source and d = isqrt(dx^2 + dy^2) (d == 0 -> see ZERO_VECTOR_DIRECTION), L = min(Pushback, MAX_PUSHBACK_LENGTH); the target point is unit + (tdiv(dx x L, d), tdiv(dy x L, d)) and the speed is loaded with 25n, n the smallest with 25n(n+1)/2 >= L. Every tick after, the ladder REPLACES the walk: the separation scan runs while the speed is > 0 and so does the water ejection (WATER_RESOLUTION); speed -= 25 BEFORE the move; move_towards(target, speed) with the step min(speed, dist, 250) and no lower clamp (the facing untouched; the avoidance offset rotates the step but is neither scanned nor decayed); the ladder is active while speed >= 0, and the path is dropped the tick it turns negative (a replan follows). THE MEASUREMENT: the Giant's per-tick |step| reads 150, 125, 100, 75, 50, 25, 0, then 25 BACKWARD (v0 = 175, so L in (525, 700]); its nodes and facing are unchanged during the ladder, the path is cleared on the last tick and replanned on the next -- TRUE OF THAT PUSH AND NOT OF EVERY ONE, see open item (4); the engine reproduces all eight steps from the card data alone (tests/knockback16402.rs). fixed_distance predicts one displacement of Pushback on the hit tick and no track; linear_falloff_with_distance and half_distance_constant_speed predict no back-step and a different first step; none of the three produces the 25-per-tick ladder. Over the replay corpus the `pushback` family's unit-ticks within 250 native rose from 35.0 % to 70.4 % with the ladder (20392 unit-ticks). The unit therefore ends 25n(n-1)/2 - 25 along the line when the ladder covers L (the 2018 Fireball's 1800: v0 = 300, steps 250 250 225 ... 25 0 -25, total 1600), which is what tests/spells.rs and tests/knockback16402.rs derive. The engine arms the ladder in the Resolve of the hit tick and takes its first step in the next tick's Path phase; the eight steps are compared from the first ladder step. The hit displacement AttackPushback (a characters.csv column) is not modelled: unexercised by the replay, and no thin-slice card carries it.

DISPLACEMENT_LAW.open: (1) A stunned or frozen victim mid-ladder: whether the game carries it through the ladder is unmeasured -- no capture has a stunned unit mid-ladder; the engine carries it (phase_path16402 step 0). (2) The charge tail inside every pushback tick (charge.RESET_ON_KNOCKBACK, hypothesis: no capture has a charging unit mid-ladder); the tick a charged unit's hit lands on is charge.CHARGED_HIT_TIMING. (3) The tilemap's blocked bits (WATER_RESOLUTION not_modelled). (4) WHETHER THE LADDER HOLDS THE TARGET AND THE ROUTE. The engine keeps both while the ladder runs (target.rs, state.rs's replan skip) and tests/knockback16402.rs asserts it, on the strength of the one Giant above. This item previously said the corpus refuted the general form. It does not, and the correction is 2026-09-23. The cited evidence was the Golem of capture 20260920-071744-B going target 6 -> none at t2043 -> 4 at t2044 with its path node count 3 -> 14, mid-ladder. Read again by FRAME INDEX (the entity arrays run from t0 over the frames of `ticks`, not by tick number), the same transition happens on the same ticks to key 3, a side-0 PrincessTower with path_n 0 throughout, and to key 1, a KingTower: 6 6 6 -1 4 4 4 and 6 6 6 -1 -1 -1 -1. Neither can move, be pushed, or retarget mid-ladder. What actually happened is that key 6, the side-1 princess the Golem was walking at, has its LAST FRAME on that tick: it died, and every side-0 entity that named it fell back at once. The node count moved because the destination moved. The misreading has one cause, shared with the harness's target_match column: the truth's `target` is the client's own pointer, which names the DESTINATION crown tower whenever a unit is not fighting, while the engine's e.target is only ever an attack target -- default_tower is a local walk goal at four sites and is never stored. So the hold is UNREFUTED rather than refuted, which is not the same as confirmed: it still rests on the one Giant, and a capture of a unit pushed while it is walking at a tower that stays alive would settle it.

ATTRACT_LAW.provenance: MEASURED on the two Tornado casts of capture 20260920-081819 (level 11, side 0): tick 1307 at (4500, 22500) and tick 1775 at (16500, 18500). THE LAW: every tick of the area effect's life each eligible victim takes an EXTRA step of length L = tdiv(S * AttractPercentage, 100) native straight at the centre, where S is the victim's own effective speed in native units per tick, taken from its position at the START of the tick, ADDED to whatever else moves it, with no arrival clamp, for exactly life_duration_ms / TICK_MS = 21 ticks. THE BASE IS THE EFFECTIVE SPEED: the Giant (key 17) is pulled 187 and tdiv(52 * 360, 100) = 187, where 52 is its stomp-corrected speed; its raw Speed column 45 gives 162, which puts the step at (33, 157) where (39, 182) is recorded on both ticks 1314 and 1315. Those two ticks are its stomp pause, identified independently by its 15-tick pause cadence outside the effect, and they also settle that the pull does NOT scale with the walk's speed for the tick, which is zero there. PER UNIT, NOT CONSTANT: the Knight (key 28) is pulled 216 = 60 * 360 / 100. ADDED, NOT SUBSTITUTED: subtracting the pull leaves a residual that is the victim's own walk, 51-52 on the Giant's 19 walking ticks and exactly (0,0) on its two paused ones. FROM THE TICK-START POSITION: over the Knight's 11 ticks within 254 native of the centre, 'pull from the pre-move position then walk' admits a legal walk on 11 of 11 while 'walk then pull from the moved position' admits none on 9 of them. OVERSHOOT, NOT A CLAMP: at 12 native out the Knight's recorded step is 169, landing 157 past the centre, and the whole 1784..1795 oscillation is reproduced by pull 216 plus a constant (-42,-42) walk, the two alternating step sizes being 216-60 and 216+60. TRUNCATION: 187.2 lands on 187 twice, so ceil is refuted; floor, trunc and round agree on this data. CENTRE: a +/-600 native grid search at 20-native steps leaves the tap point (16500, 18500) as the unique survivor. DURATION: first pulled tick to last is 1307..1327 and 1775..1795, both 21 moves, counted from positions alone so the estimated cast tick cannot shift it. THE SOURCE IS THE LIVE AREA EFFECT, NOT THE BUFF SLOT: BuffTime is 500 ms with CapBuffTimeToAreaEffectTime false, so the last application outlives the area by ten ticks, and the Giant's displacement is (0,0) on two of them. NOT GATED BY THE KNOCKBACK RULES: the Giant is IgnorePushback and was pulled, and the Knight was pulled through eight ticks of its own Bowler ladder -- subtracting the 216 leaves exactly the 200, 174, 149, 124, 99, 75, 49, 24 ladder knockback.DISPLACEMENT_LAW already records, which corroborates that law at the same time. --- 2026-09-24, THE BASE, RE-MEASURED ON CLIENT 15.535.29 WITH PAIRED CONTROLS (the same scenario with and without the Tornado; each scenario is deterministic, so the position difference on the first acting tick is the pull and no walk model is needed): a Knight is pulled about 216 = tdiv(60 * 360, 100) whether it is walking, attacking a tower (215.5), stunned by Zap (216.1), frozen (215.4), mid-knockback (215.2, the pull ADDED to the ladder step), under Rage (215.9 -- its own step 77 that frame, so the buffed arm predicts 280) or slowed by an Ice Wizard (215.7 -- step 41, buffed arm 147). THE PULL IGNORES EVERY SPEED BUFF. The Giant above never separated the two arms: effective_speed is the stored speed through buffs and the charge, the stored speed of a stomp card is ALREADY stomp-corrected at load (card.rs, S = floor(Speed * (Stop + Wait) / Stop), 52 for the Giant against its raw column 45), and an unbuffed, uncharged Giant gives both arms 52. An earlier reading here, and the engine's comments, took the base arm to mean the raw column 45 and counted the Giant against it; the code never read the column. Rage is the first victim whose two speeds differ, and it says base_speed. Also measured: the pull is not capped at 250 (a Hog Rider pulled 431.7 = tdiv(120 * 360, 100) - 0.3); flyers are pulled at full magnitude (Minions 323.9 against 324); own troops are never pulled.

BUFF_STACKING.confidence: MEDIUM (ours; correct for every combination the corpus ships)
BUFF_STACKING.provenance: character_buffs ships EnableStacking on Poison, Earthquake, RageModeRage and the Heal Spirit's buff, so the game can carry a row more than once. WHAT IT CANNOT MEAN is one copy per APPLICATION: a Poison area re-applies its 1000 ms buff every HitSpeed = 250 ms for a LifeDuration of 8000, so 32 copies would stack on a unit that stood in one cloud and the card would deal 32 times its published damage. Stacking therefore needs the buff's SOURCE (the area effect object, the projectile) as part of its identity, and the engine does not carry that: `one_slot_per_buff_row` keys a slot on the buff ROW alone, so a second cloud refreshes the first rather than adding to it. A NAMED GAP -- two Poisons on one unit deal one Poison's damage. Measured against this: with per-application slots a Knight standing in one Poison took 17 damage ticks over the cloud's 8 s instead of 8 (tests/status.rs).
BUFF_STACKING.promotion_rules: Two Poisons over one Knight, cast a second apart: the hp curve doubles its slope while both clouds stand under per_source_slot and does not under one_slot_per_buff_row.
BUFF_STACKING.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json, the only() rule); state.rs `apply_effects` keys a slot on the buff row. tests/status.rs pins the Poison's pulse count.

SAME_BUFF_REAPPLY.provenance: A stun landing on a stunned unit sets the remaining time to max(remaining, new) and never shortens a longer one (ZapFreeze ships no EnableStacking; crforge AppliedEffect.refresh uses max). Several stuns landing in one tick merge by max, which is order-independent.
SAME_BUFF_REAPPLY.promotion_rules: Zap a unit 1 s into an Ice Spirit freeze (1.1 s live): it moves at 1.1 s under refresh_max, at 1.5 s under replace.
SAME_BUFF_REAPPLY.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted

STUN_PAUSES_DEPLOY_TIMER.promotion_rules: Zap a Knight about 0.8 s into its 1 s deploy: it starts walking about 1.3 s (false) or 1.5 s (true) after placement.
