FULL_STOP_BUFF_IS_STUN.confidence: MEDIUM (ours; the two candidates agree on every gate the engine has)
FULL_STOP_BUFF_IS_STUN.provenance: THE ENGINE'S OWN UNIFICATION. Every stun the data ships is a BUFF: a Zap, a Freeze spell, an Ice Spirit's projectile and an Electro Wizard's hit each hang a character_buffs row whose SpeedMultiplier, HitSpeedMultiplier and SpawnSpeedMultiplier are all -100, and under movement.BUFF_SPEED_COMPOSITION / combat.HIT_SPEED_BUFF / spawner.STUN_PAUSES_SPAWNER a composed 0 is what stops the unit. The engine already had a hold path -- `stun_ms`, and with it status.STUN_ATTACK_TIMER_MODEL, status.STUN_RETARGET_ON_RESUME, the three status.STUN_PAUSES_*, spawner.STUN_PAUSES_SPAWNER and charge.RESET_ON_STUN -- so `stun_timer` drives that one timer from such a buff and every one of those keys keeps the meaning it was written with. `buff_only` would leave the timer at 0 and make each gate read the composition itself, which re-attaches every STUN_PAUSES_* key; not implemented.
FULL_STOP_BUFF_IS_STUN.promotion_rules: None available: the two arms are observationally identical here. They separate only if a buff is found whose composed speed is 0 and which the game does NOT treat as a stun (no shipped row is like that).
FULL_STOP_BUFF_IS_STUN.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted

BUFF_PULSE_AMOUNT.provenance: The columns are DamagePerSecond / HealPerSecond alongside HitFrequency in milliseconds (15.535 Poison 36 at 1000, Earthquake 32 at 1000, the Heal Spirit's buff 157 at 250), so one pulse is dps x HitFrequency / 1000 and one second of the buff deals dps whatever the frequency. Not measured. `per_pulse` would make every pulse the whole per-second figure, which multiplies the Heal Spirit by four against its published value.
BUFF_PULSE_AMOUNT.promotion_rules: Total a Poison's damage on a standing Knight over its 8 s and compare with the published card value; the Heal Spirit's 250 ms frequency separates the two arms by a factor of four.
BUFF_PULSE_AMOUNT.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted

BUFF_PULSE_TIMING.provenance: WHEN a damaging or healing buff's first pulse falls. `after_first_period`: the pulse clock starts at HitFrequency, so a 1000 ms Poison buff that its area re-applies every 250 ms still pulses once a second while the unit stands in it (the refresh keeps the buff alive, it does not re-arm the pulse). `on_application` fires on the application tick, which would make a Poison cloud deal its per-second damage four times a second. Excluded by the card's published total, not by a trace.
BUFF_PULSE_TIMING.promotion_rules: Count the damage ticks a Poison deals to a Knight standing in it for the full 8 s: 8 under after_first_period, 32 under on_application.
BUFF_PULSE_TIMING.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted

TARGET_BUFF_ON_SPLASH.provenance: A projectile's TargetBuff column is named for the target, but the projectile's own splash hits everything inside its radius. `whole_splash`: every victim the impact damages takes the buff too, which is how the Snowball (Radius 2500, TargetBuff IceWizardSlowDown 3000 ms) is described. `primary_target_only` would slow one unit of a group -- for a troop's projectile the locked target, for a spell impact (which has a centre and no target) the victim nearest that centre. Not measured. BOTH PATHS dispatch on it: `combat.rs apply_attack_buff` for a troop's TargetBuff / BuffOnDamage and `spell.rs impact` for a spell's area buff (which had cited this key in a comment and never read it, so primary_target_only was a no-op for every spell carrying a buff until the two were joined).
TARGET_BUFF_ON_SPLASH.promotion_rules: Snowball three Skeletons standing together and time all three: all three slowed under whole_splash.
TARGET_BUFF_ON_SPLASH.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted

$comment: Buildings that hide when not attacking (buildings.csv HidesWhenNotAttacking / HideTimeMs /
UpTimeMs; Tesla true / 800 / 800 in both the 2018 data and 15.535). The timers are card data
(data/derived/cards.json, read by card.rs `HideDef`); everything the columns do not settle is a
key below. State machine: entity.rs `HideState`, stepped once per tick in state.rs `hide_pass`
(Target phase, before any entity decides its target). Community (unmeasured) rules the engine
takes without a key: the building lifetime keeps running in every state (wiki Tesla: 'its
lifetime still counts down while hidden'); a HIDDEN building ignores stun and knockback; a
hidden building neither targets nor attacks; a deploying Tesla is Up (targetable, damageable)
until its deploy time ends, when STARTS_HIDDEN applies. HideBeforeFirstHit (blank on every
2018 row) is not read.

STARTS_HIDDEN.provenance: Wiki Tesla: 'When deployed, it will be hidden underground' -- the building is under ground the moment its deploy time ends and rises only for a target. The false arm stands it up at deploy end with a full HideTimeMs countdown, so with no enemy near it goes under HideTimeMs later.
STARTS_HIDDEN.promotion_rules: Deploy a Tesla with an enemy Knight already adjacent: its first shot comes UpTimeMs after the deploy ends (true) or immediately at deploy end (false). A capture of the scene carries the Tesla's first-hit tick.
STARTS_HIDDEN.engine: state.rs Calib::hide_starts_hidden, applied by BattleState::hide_on_deployed (phase_upkeep on the tick deploy_ms reaches 0; spawn_now / setup spawns for a zero deploy time)

RISE_TRIGGER.provenance: Wiki Tesla: 'it will rise when an enemy comes within its range'. Tesla ships SightRange = Range = 5500, so the two arms agree on the shipped card and only a card whose sight exceeds its range could separate them. Both use the engine's own edge-to-edge range test and target eligibility (target.rs `enemy_in_wake_range` over `can_target`: an air unit does not wake a ground-only building, a hidden enemy building wakes nothing).
RISE_TRIGGER.promotion_rules: A hiding building whose SightRange exceeds its Range (none in the 2018 thin slice): an enemy standing between the two radii wakes it under enemy_in_sight_range only.
RISE_TRIGGER.engine: state.rs Calib::hide_rise_trigger, read by target.rs enemy_in_wake_range from state.rs hide_pass

TARGETABLE_WHILE_RISING.confidence: HIGH that enemies can target a Tesla from the tick it leaves the ground: client 15.535.29 and two independent 16.402 corpus cases agree, each locking on one tick after the Tesla surfaces. What the Tesla does while it surfaces is a different and larger defect; see open.
TARGETABLE_WHILE_RISING.provenance: MEASURED 2026-09-24. On client 15.535.29 (the tesla-vs-knight scenario) the Tesla surfaces on 240 and the Knight locks on at 241, taking the path goal (20,23). Under false the engine refuses the surfacing Tesla and the Knight keeps its princess route until 256, then turns to the same goal cell; under true it turns on 240. The Knight goes from 70.7% within 250 to 100.0%, the same across seeds and under both movement.ATTACKING_UNIT_MOVEMENT values, and no measure gets worse. On the 16.402 corpus, 3 of the 9 distinct Teslas surface, and two of them arbitrate the same way: a Tesla surfaces on 674 and a Giant locks on at 675; another on 1980 and a Minion locks on at 1981. Tested through a calibration override before the value moved. Re-checked the same evening by an independent derivation from the recordings, which found and corrected this entry's earlier claim that no corpus Tesla surfaces. The false arm is the older reading, that a Tesla is still under ground for targeting until its UpTimeMs rise has played.
TARGETABLE_WHILE_RISING.promotion_rules: A Giant walking past a hidden Tesla just inside its sight: the Giant turns toward the Tesla UpTimeMs after the Tesla starts rising (false) or on the same tick (true). On a capture, compare the Giant's target-change tick with the Tesla's rise tick.
TARGETABLE_WHILE_RISING.engine: state.rs Calib::hide_targetable_while_rising, read by target.rs hidden_from_targeting (inside can_target)
TARGETABLE_WHILE_RISING.open: THE RISING PHASE ITSELF IS THE REAL DEFECT, and it needs its own key. In both clients the surfacing state is already ATTACKING: on the surface tick the Tesla has its target and a running attack cycle, and its first hit lands 7 ticks later (15.535.29: 240 -> 247; corpus 674 -> 681 and 1980 -> 1987). The engine's Tesla has no target and no attack for its UpTimeMs rise (240-255), is up at 256 and first hits at 263, 16 ticks late under BOTH values of this key, so the Knight's hit points are exact on 67.9% of ticks under both. After its target dies the clients' Tesla goes back under in 6 ticks (15.535.29: 354 -> 360; corpus 1351 -> 1357, 2051 -> 2057); the engine's at 370. The law these fit: no pre-attack rise, the Tesla attacks the tick it surfaces, and hides 6 ticks after it loses its target. A red test for it has three numbers from the 15.535.29 scenario: first hit 247, Knight lock-on 241, hidden at 360. ONE TICK OF ORDERING remains under this key: the engine's Knight locks on 240, the clients' 241 (within 20: 54.6% -> 54.2%). It survives the fixtures' tick correction (the Knight is issued at 104 on both), so it is an ordering inside the tick and not a labelling artefact.

HIDDEN_IMMUNE_TO_DAMAGE.provenance: Wiki Tesla: 'while hidden it cannot be targeted or damaged by anything, including spells'. Enforced at ONE choke point, combat.rs `resolve` when the damage buffer is applied: every hit on a Hidden building is dropped whatever wrote it (attack, projectile, spell, rolling Log, death damage) -- except the building-lifetime expiry hit, which carries Hit.ignores_hide and always lands (a Tesla whose 40 s are up dies under ground). The false arm lets every hit land (targeting stays blocked).
HIDDEN_IMMUNE_TO_DAMAGE.promotion_rules: Fireball a Tesla that is under ground with nothing near it: its hp is unchanged when it next rises (true) or reduced by the Fireball's damage (false).
HIDDEN_IMMUNE_TO_DAMAGE.engine: state.rs Calib::hide_hidden_immune, read by combat.rs resolve from state.rs phase_resolve

HIDE_DELAY_MEANING.provenance: HideTimeMs is the time an Up building spends WITHOUT A LIVE TARGET before it goes under (the countdown resets to HideTimeMs on every Target phase it has one). The alternative reading counts from the building's LAST SHOT (state.rs phase_attack resets the countdown on fire), under which a target kept by the keep-target hysteresis but out of attack range does not hold it up. Tick alignment (both arms): the countdown is decremented in the Target phase; a building with no target from the Target phase of tick T on is Hidden in tick T + ceil(HideTimeMs / TICK_MS) - 1. LIMITS OF THE time_since_last_shot ARM: it is only viable on a hider whose HitSpeed <= HideTimeMs. The 2018 Tesla the engine loads ships HitSpeed 800 == HideTimeMs 800, which is why the arm hides on a STRICT countdown (< 0: with <= 0 it went under before every second shot); the 15.535 Tesla (characters/tesla.toml: HitSpeed 1100, LoadTime 700, HideTimeMs 800, UpTimeMs 800) would go under between every pair of shots with its target still in range, so on current data this arm cannot be the live rule as written -- a measurable restatement would be 'time since the last shot, not counting while a target is in attack range', which is not implemented. A THIRD READING the registry does not implement: HideTimeMs as the DURATION of the going-under transition (a Descending state) with the idle delay elsewhere -- the 15.535 Ghost row (characters/ghost.toml: BuffWhenNotAttackingTime = 2000 beside HideTimeMs = 400, no HidesWhenNotAttacking) pairs the same HideTimeMs column with a separate idle-delay column, so the schema does not rule it out; under it a Tesla whose target dies would start descending at once (untargetable immediately or only after the transition is the open question) instead of staying Up/targetable for 800 ms. Implementing it needs a fourth HideState.
HIDE_DELAY_MEANING.promotion_rules: Kill a Tesla's only target in the middle of its hit cycle: under idle_time_without_target it goes under HideTimeMs after the kill whatever the cycle phase; under time_since_last_shot HideTimeMs after its last shot, i.e. earlier by the time since that shot. For the unimplemented transition reading, a capture of a Tesla whose target dies: does it become untargetable (a Fireball / a locked attacker's retarget) immediately or only ~800 ms later?
HIDE_DELAY_MEANING.engine: state.rs Calib::hide_delay_meaning, read by state.rs hide_pass (and phase_attack for the reset under time_since_last_shot)

HIDDEN_OCCLUDES_PATH.provenance: A hidden Tesla's footprint still blocks deploys and still occludes the path grid (units walk around the spot; wiki: troops 'walk around a hidden Tesla'). The engine's path grid never looks at the hide state, so `true` is the only arm it runs; `false` needs the pathfinder to consult the hide state and is REFUSED at load.
HIDDEN_OCCLUDES_PATH.promotion_rules: A Knight walking a straight lane over a hidden Tesla's footprint with nothing to wake it (out of its sight is impossible on the footprint, so: a Tesla that cannot target the walker, e.g. an air unit over a ground-only hider -- none in the thin slice). Practically: the recorded path nodes of a Giant routed past a hidden enemy Tesla.
HIDDEN_OCCLUDES_PATH.engine: state.rs Calib::from_json refuses false (the only() rule for a boolean key); the value is not stored because nothing branches on it

$comment: PERIODIC SPAWNERS AND DEATH SPAWN (characters.csv / buildings.csv Spawn* and DeathSpawn*
columns; 2018: Tombstone, GoblinHut, BarbarianHut, FirespiritHut, Witch, DarkWitch spawn;
Tombstone, Golem, LavaHound, BattleRam, DarkWitch death-spawn). The columns are card data
(data/derived/cards.json `spawner` / `death_spawn`, read by card.rs `SpawnerDef` /
`DeathSpawnDef`, checked against the 15.535 csv_logic: same names, same meanings); every
rule they do not settle is a key below. Column semantics taken as read, not keyed:
SpawnNumber = units per wave; SpawnInterval = ms between the units of one wave (blank =
all at once); SpawnPauseTime = ms between waves; SpawnStartTime = ms to the first wave
(from activation or from placement: START_TIME_ORIGIN); SpawnLimit = most units from one
spawner alive at once (blank = unlimited); SpawnRadius = how far from the spawner the
units appear; a SpawnCharacter with SpawnNumber AND SpawnPauseTime both blank is no
periodic spawner (the SkeletonContainer row); DeathSpawnCount units at DeathSpawnRadius;
DeathSpawnDeployTime overrides the unit's DeployTime. COLUMNS THE DATA SHIPS THAT ARE NOT
READ: SpawnAngleShift (DarkWitch 90 -- the Bats on her flanks;
BattleRam 180 -- the Barbarians behind; 2018 and 15.535 alike), DeathSpawnPushback
(Golem, LavaHound, DarkWitch true), DeathSpawnMinRadius (SkeletonContainer 100), and
SpawnCharacterLevelIndex (2 on every hut, Witch 5, DarkWitch 8, BattleRam 2 -- not carried
into cards.json; every shipped value equals the owner's RelativeLevel and every spawned
unit is Common, so the owner's unified level is exact today). Engine: state.rs
`spawner_pass`, which runs in the MOVE phase right after the deploy countdown
(spawner.EMISSION_TIMING = move_phase_immediate, measured: a Tombstone's first Skeleton is
on the board on the Tombstone's own deploy-end tick) and creates its units in that same
tick; the Spawn phase, after the queue drains, pushing PendingSpawns that materialised in
the NEXT tick, is the spawn_phase_next_tick arm. Death spawn is still `phase_reap`, queued the old way (it
fires from a death, not from a timer). Timers run only past the deploy time; a building
lifetime is unaffected (see the lifetime section: a building's hp DRAINS over that time). A
wave's simultaneous units and every death spawn are laid out by the engine formation grid
(the same code as a Goblin Barrel release, spells.PROJECTILE_SPAWN_FORMATION = engine_grid)
in the OWNER's frame, water-ejected like a release; the contact law (collision.CONTACT_LAW
= client16402: the separation mean capped at 150 native per tick, deploying units
included) slides them out of footprints over the following ticks as it does every unit
(the Move phase's own one-tick static pass runs under the trace-fitted arm only). Spawned units
carry the owner's team and the owner's unified level (card.rs `unit_level`; the 2018
SpawnCharacterLevelIndex is not carried into cards.json, see above) and NO deploy timer
(spawner.SPAWNED_DEPLOY_TIME = zero, measured); a DEATH spawn serves DeathSpawnDeployTime
when the row sets one and otherwise none (DEATH_SPAWN_DEPLOY_TIME_DEFAULT = zero, measured).

FIRST_WAVE.confidence: HIGH: 44 live Tombstone deploys and 2 BarbarianHut deploys, first wave on the deploy-end tick
FIRST_WAVE.provenance: SpawnStartTime is blank on every 2018 hut (Witch 1000, DarkWitch 1500). MEASURED on the live 16.402 replay corpus: a Tombstone's first Skeleton exists on the Tombstone's own deploy-end tick (delta 0 on 38 of 44 exact-tick deploys, +1 on 3, the rest capture-start artefacts) and a BarbarianHut's first Barbarian likewise (2 of 2) -- a blank start time is 0. The shipped arm reads a blank start time as 0; with spawner.EMISSION_TIMING = move_phase_immediate the timer is loaded at the deploy-end tick and decremented in that same tick's pass, so a 0 fires there. A set start time S fires ceil(S / TICK_MS) ticks after activation (START_TIME_ORIGIN). The other arm treats a blank start time as one full SpawnPauseTime -- that would put the first Skeleton 70 ticks late, and no deploy of the corpus shows that.
FIRST_WAVE.promotion_rules: Settled by the measurement above (the losing arm is 70 ticks off on every one of the 46 deploys).
FIRST_WAVE.engine: state.rs Calib::spawner_first_wave, read by BattleState::spawner_activate (the timer's initial value)

START_TIME_ORIGIN.confidence: HIGH: 3 live Witch and 2 DarkWitch deploys, first wave 19 ticks after the deploy-end tick
START_TIME_ORIGIN.provenance: Where a set SpawnStartTime is measured from. from_activation (shipped): the timer is loaded with the raw column when the deploy timer reaches 0 -- a 2018 Witch (DeployTime 1000, SpawnStartTime 1000) placed at tick P has its first Skeleton at P + 1 + 20 + 20 = P + 41. from_placement: the deploy window already consumed that much of it, the timer is loaded with max(0, SpawnStartTime - DeployTime) -- the same Witch at P + 22. THE DATA PATTERN THAT RAISES THE FORK: every 15.535 spawning troop ships SpawnStartTime == DeployTime (witch.toml 1000 / 1000, darkwitch.toml 1000 / 1000), which is what a placement-relative 'first wave exactly at deploy end' looks like; the 2018 DarkWitch (1500 / 1000) parts the arms by 500 ms either way. MEASURED on the live 16.402 corpus: a Witch (DeployTime 1000, SpawnStartTime 1000) has her first four Skeletons 19 ticks AFTER her deploy-end tick (3 of 3), and a DarkWitch her first two Bats likewise (2 of 2). from_activation predicts exactly that -- the timer is loaded with 1000 at the deploy-end tick and decremented by TICK_MS in that same tick's pass, so it reaches 0 nineteen ticks later; from_placement predicts the deploy-end tick itself and matches none of the five. SETTLED. FIRST_WAVE covers the blank column only.

PAUSE_ANCHOR.provenance: For a wave with SpawnInterval > 0 (2018 Witch: 3 Skeletons 300 ms apart, BarbarianHut 2 x 500 ms), where SpawnPauseTime is measured from: the wave's LAST unit (shipped; the timer is simply reloaded with the pause after the last emission) or its FIRST (the pause minus the wave's own length; if that is <= 0 the next wave starts at once). Indistinguishable on a single-unit wave (Tombstone, GoblinHut) and on a wave with no interval. MEASURED on the live 16.402 corpus, what the corpus does show: a wave whose SpawnInterval is blank is emitted WHOLE on one tick (the live Witch: 13 groups of 4 Skeletons on one tick, 140 ticks apart), which is what the engine does under both arms. The reload is the plain column: every shipped SpawnPauseTime and SpawnInterval is a multiple of TICK_MS, so a timer that carried its (non-positive) leftover into the reload would land on the same tick, and the carry is not implemented.
PAUSE_ANCHOR.promotion_rules: Needs a live card that ships a SpawnInterval: the 16.402 Witch does NOT (15.535 witch.toml: SpawnNumber 4, SpawnPauseTime 7000, no SpawnInterval line -- her whole wave is simultaneous and both arms predict the same gap, so the 140-vs-128-tick Witch prediction is void). A capture of a BarbarianHut if 16.402 still ships its 2 x 500 ms wave: the tick gap between two consecutive waves' first Barbarians is ceil(pause / 50) + ceil(500 / 50) (after_last) or ceil(pause / 50) (after_first); on a hut with no interval the key is unsettleable and irrelevant.
PAUSE_ANCHOR.engine: state.rs Calib::spawner_pause_anchor, read by BattleState::spawner_pass when a wave's last unit is emitted

TIMER_LEFTOVER.confidence: HIGH on the Tombstone, whose every contiguous emission it fits; the Barbarian Hut rests on one activation. Neutral for a spawner with a SpawnStartTime, whose timer reaches exactly 0.
TIMER_LEFTOVER.provenance: MEASURED on the 16.402 corpus, one seat per battle, the ticks of each spawner's periodic emissions against its activation tick A (its first tick out of the deploy). A Tombstone (SpawnInterval 500, SpawnNumber 2, SpawnPauseTime 3500, blank SpawnStartTime) emits at A, A+9, A+79, A+89, A+159: the first gap is 9 on 36 of 38 exact activations, and every later contiguous emission comes one tick before the engine's (102 of 102). A Barbarian Hut (SpawnInterval 500, SpawnNumber 3, SpawnPauseTime 14000) emits at A, A+9, A+19, A+299, A+309 (one activation). The engine emitted at A, A+10, A+80 and A, A+10, A+20, A+300: on the activation tick its timer goes from 0 to -50, the first unit comes out, and the reload REPLACES the timer with SpawnInterval, dropping the -50. Adding the reload to the overshoot (-50 + 500 = 450, nine ticks) fits every emission above exactly. A Witch (SpawnStartTime 1000) fires with her timer at exactly 0, so the rule does not move her; the gaps of her corpus waves are a separate question. CORPUS PRE-SCORE, alone, on RoyaleSim 157da9f: within 250 +512, Tombstone +209. THE FOUR TOGETHER (formation.STAGGER_WAIT, spawner.TIMER_LEFTOVER, spawner.DEATH_SPAWN_AT_EMISSION_POINT, spawner.DEATH_SPAWN_RADIUS_DEFAULT = zero), stacked as overrides on RoyaleSim 157da9f over the 16.402 corpus fixtures: 128,094 of 156,718 playable no-tower unit-ticks within 250 (81.74%), against the base's 126,669 of 156,500 (80.94%): +1,425. The both-alive denominator moves with the treatment, so the counts, not the percentages, are the comparison. Per card: Goblins +829, GoblinGang +914, Tombstone +595; Knight -617, all of it in battle 124946, whose cascade also carries every other single-key loss. Flipped together on 2026-09-25.
TIMER_LEFTOVER.meaning: client16402_carried: when a spawner's timer reaches 0 or below and it emits, the reload (SpawnInterval, or the pause after a wave's last unit) is ADDED to the timer's value, so the overshoot carries into the next wait. dropped: today's engine, the reload replaces the timer's value.
TIMER_LEFTOVER.open: Whether other timers the engine reloads the same way (attack cooldowns, charge, hide) carry their overshoot too: not measured here.
TIMER_LEFTOVER.promotion_rules: SETTLED 2026-09-25 (see provenance). dropped, the earlier engine, is the old arm. tests/spawner.rs `wave_ticks` follows the arm: after a blank-start activation the first nonzero gap is ceil((gap - TICK_MS) / TICK_MS).
TIMER_LEFTOVER.engine: state.rs spawner_pass (the reload after an emission)

SPAWN_POINT.confidence: HIGH for the ring's angle: it is the spawner's facing angle rounded to a whole degree and read through the sine table, so the Night Witch's first Bats land on the client's points where the unrounded angle put them 26 native off (client 15.535.29, the Night Witch scenario). The earlier halves stand: a blank-SpawnRadius spawner emits forward at the two circles' tangent (849 of the Tombstone's 879 client 16.402 emissions within 250 of it), and a card that sets SpawnRadius emits on a ring of that radius.
SPAWN_POINT.measured_2026_09_26: MEASURED on client 15.535.29, the per-frame records of the 15.535.29 scenario runs (775 runs read; every Night Witch emission of two Bats on one frame, 7 in all): the two creation points are the Night Witch's position after her move on the emission tick plus trunc0(1500 * t / 1024) per component, with t the round(sin x 1024) table at a + 90 and a + 270 degrees, where a is the direction of her facing after the move ROUNDED to a whole degree: 7 of 7 exact. The degree whose table direction agrees with the facing most (the measured arm's choice) gives 6 of 7: for the facing (255, 22), at 4.93 degrees, the table's rounding picks 4 and the client uses 5, which puts both Bats 26 native around the ring. Her facing before the move misses 2 of 7, and her position before the move misses 4 of 7.

SPAWN_POINT.promotion_rules: The corpus already refutes both shipped candidates, so the next move is an engine change and not a capture. TWO THINGS ARE STILL OPEN AND ONE OF THEM IS GENUINELY HARD. (1) THE CONSTANT AGAINST THE FORMULA, undiscriminated. Both blank-SpawnRadius spawners the corpus holds sum to the same number -- Tombstone 1000 + 500 and BarbarianHut 1000 + 500 -- so 'emits at 1500' and 'emits at spawner radius + spawned unit radius' fit the data identically, and the second is the physically motivated one. Deciding it needs a blank-SpawnRadius spawner whose sum is NOT 1500, and every candidate is behind another loader job, which is why this is not a cheap lead: FirespiritHut (600 + a FireSpirit) and GoblinHut are refused for running an action graph this loader does not read, and the Firespirit Hut's graph is where its ActionSpawnToLocation emission lives, so the column is not missing but unread; RamRider and GoblinGiant are refused for a spawner with no SpawnPauseTime; SuperMiniPekka is refused for a spawned unit with no hitpoints, and its Pancakes have Speed 0. If the action-graph card work lands for its own reasons, this comes free with it. GoblinGiant does NOT decide it: its SpawnRadius is 900, so it is a ring card. (2) THE EXACT POINT IS SETTLED, 2026-09-23, and this rule is DISCHARGED. It asked for "an instrument that reports an entity on the tick it comes to exist" and client 15.535.29 is one; it reads the tangent exactly. The band below was inferred from a walk-back that assumed a part-step and the step is a full one, so read it as the history of the question rather than as its answer. ORIGINALLY: A recording's first frame for a unit is a part-step past materialisation by construction (see provenance), so a designed capture returns the same band. It can only be settled by an argument from the walk-back, or by an instrument that reports an entity on the tick it comes to exist. (3) THE WITCH ARM IS UNDER-DETERMINED WITHIN ITSELF, separately from (1): her 4-fold ring is invariant under 90 degrees, so it cannot separate a fixed absolute frame from the OWNER's forward frame. The discriminating observation is a SpawnRadius spawner whose ring count does not divide 360 into multiples of 90 -- a 3-ring is invariant only modulo 120 and a 5-ring only modulo 72, so either separates them in a single wave. Worth looking for in the already-implemented DEATH SPAWN ring too (spawner.DEATH_SPAWN_LAYOUT = facing_ring, state.rs `death_spawn_points`): it commits to a facing frame with the same owner's-forward fallback, so a corpus death spawn at a ring count other than 4 tests the same frame question against a law the engine already ships, and would say whether the Witch is the exception or the rule.

SPAWN_POINT.open: THE DEFECT THIS ENTRY NOW POINTS AT IS NOT IN THIS KEY. The spawn POINT is right; the engine does not give a spawned unit its first step, because spawner_pass runs at the end of phase_move (state.rs, spawner.EMISSION_TIMING = move_phase_immediate) after the tick's deltas are applied. Fixing it needs phase_path16402 to run for the newly created entities, and it MUST be gated on deploy time: 27 of 33 single-troop deploys sit exactly at the deploy centre on their first observable frame, so an ungated first step moves all 27 and breaks every one. spawner.SPAWNED_DEPLOY_TIME = zero is the gate, measured. WHAT WILL REMAIN: the SECOND member of each wave sits at 0.864 of a step (77.8 of 89.8), 7 of 8 identical to the unit, with one outlier at 0.378 belonging to the one pair whose inter-spawn gap is 9 ticks rather than 10. A sub-tick-phase explanation was TESTED AND IS DEAD -- deploying the Tombstone on ticks 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7 moved every spawn frame and changed no displacement at all. The live hypothesis is that the first member blocks the second, which the existing unit-unit collision would produce for free; the test is to implement the step and read the seconds WITHOUT tuning anything. Do not close the remaining 12 native with a constant: a constant is right for Skeletons, wrong for Barbarians, and double-counts the moment the step lands.

STUN_PAUSES_SPAWNER.provenance: character_buffs.csv ZapFreeze ships SpawnSpeedMultiplier -100 beside SpeedMultiplier -100 and HitSpeedMultiplier -100 (2018 and 15.535 alike), i.e. the stun class stops the spawn timer as it stops movement and attacks. The engine skips the timer's decrement on every pass the spawner is stunned in (stun_ms > 0 at that pass), so a D-ms Zap delays the next wave by exactly the number of passes the stun covers -- ceil(D / TICK_MS) under status.BUFF_EXPIRY_TICK_ALIGNMENT = ceil_from_next_tick. The false arm lets the timer run through a stun.
STUN_PAUSES_SPAWNER.promotion_rules: A capture: Zap a Tombstone mid-pause and compare its next Skeleton's tick with the unstunned cadence (ceil(D / 50) ticks late under the shipped arm, on time under the other).

LIMIT_RULE.provenance: No 2018 row sets SpawnLimit, so nothing shipped turns on it. The implemented arm counts the spawner's own live units plus its units still in the spawn queue (entity.rs `spawned_by`, a pure count over start-of-phase state) and, when the count is at the limit, SKIPS the unit and keeps the timer cadence. The other arm would hold the timer until room frees; it is not implemented and is refused at load.

$comment: A LIFETIME BUILDING'S HITPOINTS (characters.csv / buildings.csv LifeTime, carried into
data/derived/cards.json as `lifetime_ms` and read by card.rs `CardDef::lifetime_ms`).
The engine honours LifeTime on BUILDINGS only; the loader refuses a troop that ships one
(card.rs, `units.{unit} is a troop with a LifeTime`). Engine: state.rs `phase_status`.
The column is the building's whole life, not a timer that fires at the end: the game
bleeds the hitpoints away over it (HP_DECAY below), which is why a Tesla that nothing
ever touched is at half hp halfway through. status.STUN_PAUSES_BUILDING_LIFETIME says
whether a stun holds the clock; the hide state does not (a hidden Tesla drains: the live
corpus' Teslas lose hitpoints on frames they spend hidden).

HP_DECAY.confidence: HIGH: reproduced exactly on 92.2 % of 31113 live building frames, every residual a hit the building took; the exact-fraction alternative fits 46 %
HP_DECAY.provenance: MEASURED on the live 16.402 corpus. A building with a LifeTime does not keep its hitpoints and die at the end -- its hp falls every tick from its deploy-end tick and it dies when the pool runs out. The law that fits: a per-tick rate derived ONCE from the building's max hitpoints and its LifeTime, truncated to hundredths of a hitpoint, `drain = ((maxHitpoints * 100000) / LifeTime_ms) / 20` (nested floor division makes the two truncating divisions the same integer as one: max_hp x TICK_MS / LifeTime_ms in hundredths), then accumulated tick by tick with every whole hitpoint the accumulator crosses taken off the hp field; hp <= 0 is clamped to 0 and the building dies through the normal death path, so a drained Tombstone death-spawns exactly as a killed one does. With it, hp = maxHitpoints - (k * drain) / 100 for k ticks since the deploy-end tick reproduces 92.2 % of 31113 building frames over 79 buildings exactly (BombTower 1356 hp / drain 226: 100 % of 2132 frames; GoblinCage 780 / 195: 98.5 %; Tesla 1182 / 236: 95.9 %; Tombstone 91.7 %; InfernoTower 1748 / 291: 91.3 %; Cannon 824 / 137: 84.6 %), and every residual is a building that was hit -- of the 79, 54 are exact on every frame of their life. It also predicts the death tick: 501 for a Tesla (LifeTime 25000 = 500 ticks, the drain is one tick slower than the column), 600 for a BombTower, 602 for a Cannon or a level-11 Tombstone, 400 for a GoblinCage -- all confirmed on the last frame the recording shows. The drain starts at the DEPLOY-END tick, not at landing (a Tesla's hp is at max on every frame of its deploy window). The EXACT-FRACTION alternative (maxHitpoints x k / LifeTime_ticks, recomputed every tick) matches only 46 % of the frames and drifts one hitpoint high; truncating the rate first and accumulating it is what makes the law fit. expiry_hit, what the engine did before, keeps hp at max for the whole life and matches no frame past the deploy end of any building in the corpus.
HP_DECAY.meaning: linear_drain (shipped): every tick past the deploy end the building's hundredths accumulator gains ((max_hp * 100000) / LifeTime_ms) / 20 and each whole hitpoint it crosses is dealt as a hit that ignores the hide state, so damage and the drain share one hp pool and a death by drain goes through the normal death path. expiry_hit (the earlier engine, kept runnable): hp is untouched and a hit for everything the building has left lands when LifeTime is up.
HP_DECAY.promotion_rules: Settled for every building the corpus shows. Open: whether the drain rate is recomputed when a buff changes max hp, and which pool the drain takes from on a shielded building (no shipped LifeTime card carries a shield, so neither is testable on the data).
HP_DECAY.engine: state.rs Calib::lifetime_hp_decay, read by BattleState::phase_status (`lifetime_drain_per_tick`, the accumulator BattleState::lifetime_acc); tests/lifetime.rs

CHARGE_RANGE_UNIT.units: the unit of the raw ChargeRange column, as the four DISPLACEMENT accumulators read it; NOT READ under the shipped ACCUMULATOR = client16402_progress_permille
CHARGE_RANGE_UNIT.provenance: MEASURED ON THE 16.402 CORPUS (capture 20260918-122757.b1, ticks 1258..1300): the Prince walks at S 60 from tick 1258 and at 119..120 per tick from tick 1300, i.e. the doubled speed starts on its 43rd walking tick. With ChargeRange 250 that is a run-up of 42 x 60 = 2520 native units, 2.5 tiles: TEN TIMES the column in millitiles. 'centitiles' names that distance (250 centitiles = 2.5 tiles) and predicts the 42 ticks; 'millitiles' (0.25 tiles, 5 ticks) is refuted by the same capture. Under the shipped ACCUMULATOR the column is not converted to a distance at all -- the requested step is divided by it, `progress += tdiv(L x 1000, ChargeRange)` with `L = min(S, dist, 250)` in native units, charged at `progress >= 10000` -- which puts the threshold at the same 2500 native for the Prince (240 permille per walking tick, 10080 after the 42nd) and 3000 native = 3.0 tiles for the Ram (200 per tick, charged after the 50th). THE VALUE STAYS 'centitiles' because it is what the four displacement accumulators (walk_delta_length, walk_delta_toward_target, net_move_length, time_moving -- kept runnable as recording foils) need to hit the 2.5-tile run-up; the shipped accumulator does not read this key (state.rs charge_need returns 10000 permille for it). 2018 ChargeRange: Prince 250, DarkPrince 250, BattleRam 300; 15.535 (dark_prince.toml) and the 16.402 client: DarkPrince 300, Prince 250, BattleRam 300 -- a 16.402 Dark Prince capture must be read against 300 (50 ticks), not 250.
CHARGE_RANGE_UNIT.promotion_rules: Measured: 42 moving ticks at S 60 before the first S 120 tick on a clean lane (capture 20260918-122757.b1, walking from tick 1258). A further clean-lane Prince capture is a confirmation; a 16.402 Dark Prince switches at ~50 own moving ticks (ChargeRange 300 there).
CHARGE_RANGE_UNIT.engine: state.rs Calib::charge_range_unit, read by BattleState::charge_need for the four displacement accumulators only; a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted

ACCUMULATOR.provenance: What the run-up counts. client16402_progress_permille, the shipped 16.402 reading: per walking tick `progress += tdiv(L x 1000, ChargeRange)` where `L = min(S, dist_to_aim, 250)` is the REQUESTED step of the walk in native units (the step move16402::move_towards asks for), not the displacement: a body-blocked or pushed Prince still gains the full 240 permille per tick; a tick that is not a walking tick (not in the walking state, or L <= 0) resets progress to 0 (= PROGRESS_ON_STOP reset); reaching 10000 permille sets `charged` and the speed doubles from the NEXT walking tick -- the 43rd for the Prince (S 60, ChargeRange 250: 42 x 240 = 10080), the 51st for the Ram (300: 50 x 200 = 10000). CONSISTENT WITH THE CORPUS (capture 20260918-122757.b1: walking from tick 1258, 119..120 per tick from tick 1300 = walking tick 43), but that capture is a clean straight lane, on which every arm below predicts the same tick; nothing recorded so far separates them, hence hypothesis. Engine: state.rs phase_path16402 records L for every unit (Scratch::walk_step); charge_pass adds tdiv(L x 1000, range_raw) and charge_need is 10000 for this arm; under the two other path models (no requested-step notion) L is the proposed walk's length in native units. THE FOUR FOILS, kept runnable for a recording to decide (all identical to the shipped arm on a free straight walk): walk_delta_length: the length of the walk the Path phase proposed this tick (locomotion only; a blocked unit still counts its intended step). walk_delta_toward_target: that walk projected onto the direction to its target (the default tower when it has none), floored at zero, so a detour around a building counts less. net_move_length: the length of the unit's actual displacement over the Move phase (walk, arena clamp, separation and pushes together; a body-blocked Prince charges later). time_moving: TICK_MS per tick with a non-zero proposed walk, against the ms an unbuffed unit of the card takes to cover the run-up -- identical to walk_delta_length on a free straight walk and different the moment the unit is blocked, pushed or walking a diagonal (per-axis truncation shortens a diagonal step below the nominal S). FOR A FREE-WALKING UNIT ON A STRAIGHT LANE ALL FIVE ARE IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION, and all three charge cards ship the same Speed, so no clean-lane recording can decide this key: the discriminator is a body-blocked, pushed, detouring or slowed/raged Prince. Every arm is a frame-free scalar (a length, a dot product over a length, a tick count), so the seat rotation cannot enter; an own-frame forward-progress reading is deliberately not offered.
ACCUMULATOR.promotion_rules: To measured: a capture of a body-blocked Prince (behind a friendly Giant) -- the switch to S 120 at 42 of ITS OWN walking ticks under client16402_progress_permille / walk_delta_length / time_moving, later under net_move_length; a detour separates walk_delta_toward_target; a Prince slowed or raged mid-run-up separates the requested-step reading from walk_delta_length (the requested step is the buffed S, the proposed walk too, but a diagonal or blocked buffed walk parts them). tests/charge.rs prints the switch tick under every arm on the body-blocked scene and pins the 43rd-walking-tick doubling under the shipped arm from the data.
ACCUMULATOR.engine: state.rs Calib::charge_accumulator, read by BattleState::charge_pass (the per-tick gain) and charge_need (the threshold's unit); phase_path16402 records the requested step
ACCUMULATOR.onsets: The onsets of capture 20260920-003751 (seats A and B, the four chargers placed alone at (3499 | 14500, 8500)): Prince (S 60, ChargeRange 250) state 1 at tick 191, first step 192 (58, then 59 / 60 per tick), 42 steps = 2483 native from the spawn point, and the first 120 step at tick 234 = the 43RD walking tick; Dark Prince (300) first step 292, first 120 step 342 = the 51st; Battle Ram (300) first step 956, first 119 step 1006 = the 51st, its heading change at ~977 costing nothing; Ram Rider (250) first step 1462, first 120 step 1504 = the 43rd. Exactly the permille law with >= 10000 and the doubling from the tick after the run-up completes -- nothing to fix. A first look's '41 ticks / ~2490 native' counted from t193 because seat B's capture dropped the t192 frame, which seat A's has. tests/charge.rs (0) and (5) pin the three loadable cards' onsets from the data and name the capture. These are clean straight walks, on which every candidate predicts the same tick (provenance): they confirm the law's numbers without separating the candidates.

MULTIPLIER_MEANING.provenance: What ChargeSpeedMultiplier 200 multiplies. movement_when_charged: the walking speed once the run-up is complete -- the visible Prince charge every player knows (S 60 -> 120), and the live 16.402 corpus shows the Prince at exactly S = 120 while charging (movement.BUFF_SPEED_RULE, not_this_key). movement_always: the speed from the first step, run-up included. accumulation_rate: the rate the run-up fills at (the threshold divided by 200 %), the speed never changing. The buff arithmetic is the measured movement.BUFF_SPEED_RULE applied to the native S (floor(60 * 200 / 100) = 120, then x SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK), so a buffed speed is exact in subtiles.
MULTIPLIER_MEANING.promotion_rules: A capture: S on the Prince's first moving ticks (60 under movement_when_charged and accumulation_rate, 120 under movement_always) and whether S ever changes (never under accumulation_rate). One capture.
MULTIPLIER_MEANING.engine: state.rs Calib::charge_multiplier_meaning, read by BattleState::effective_speed (both path models) and charge_need

PROGRESS_ON_STOP.provenance: What a tick on which the unit does not walk (attacking, stunned, deploying, held with no proposed walk) does to a PARTIAL run-up: reset zeroes it (the wiki's 'the Prince must charge again after stopping'); hold leaves it so the run-up resumes where it stopped. Touches charge_progress only -- a completed charge is never undone by standing still (the resets for that are RESET_ON_*).
PROGRESS_ON_STOP.promotion_rules: A captured Zap on a Prince mid-run-up with RESET_ON_STUN settled false, or a Prince that fights a Skeleton mid-run-up: after the interruption the switch to S 120 comes a FULL run-up later (reset) or the remainder later (hold).
PROGRESS_ON_STOP.engine: state.rs Calib::charge_progress_on_stop, read by BattleState::charge_pass on a tick with no gain

RESET_ON_ATTACK.provenance: The landed charged hit consumes the charge: the next hit is the ordinary Damage and the unit walks at S 60 again until it has covered another run-up (wiki Prince: 'the charge is reset when he hits a target'). Consumed by a COMPLETED windup (state.rs phase_attack, right after combat::fire), not by entering range and not by a cancelled swing. The false arm keeps the charge through every hit (every hit DamageSpecial, the speed never dropping).
RESET_ON_ATTACK.promotion_rules: A capture: the tower's hp delta on the Prince's second hit (Damage-scaled under true, DamageSpecial-scaled under false) and S after the first hit.

CHARGED_HIT_TIMING.confidence: HIGH that the charged hit lands with NO LoadTime windup (both seats, unambiguous: the tower is already hit on the victim's first state-2 frame, a full LoadTime earlier than the engine); MEDIUM on the exact tick relative to the step -- the two seats' captures part by one frame (see provenance)
CHARGED_HIT_TIMING.provenance: MEASURED on the Prince of capture 20260920-003751 (both seats): at tick 327 the charged Prince is at (3261, 22254), state 1, 3246 native from the princess tower's centre (reach Range 1600 + own CollisionRadius 600 + the tower's 1000 = 3200: OUT of range); its next step is 120 to (3261, 22374) (in reach), and on its FIRST state-2 frame it already shows attack progress 1400 (= HitSpeed, as right after a hit) and load timer 900 (= LoadTime) with the tower 3052 -> 2269 = -783 = DamageSpecial 306 x 256 % -- no LoadTime windup; the following hits come at HitSpeed (391 each = Damage 153 x 256 %; the load timer counts 900 -> 0 after each hit and the next hit comes at the HitSpeed boundary, not at the timer's zero). THE TICK: seat B shows the step at t328 (state 1, tower 3052) and the hit at t329 (state 2, tower 2269) -- the step in tick 328's move pass, the hit in tick 329's attack pass, which runs before the move pass (match.TICK_ORDER) and finds the target in reach; seat A shows both at t328. Seat A's t328 frame of the Dark Prince also carries the position seat B shows at t329, so seat A's frame is one tick late there and seat B's reading is taken: the charged hit lands in the first attack pass after the step into reach, with no windup. A same-tick hit (contact_same_tick) stays possible on seat A's reading.
CHARGED_HIT_TIMING.promotion_rules: A capture without frame skew (both seats agreeing on the transition frame) settles first_attack_pass_no_windup against contact_same_tick outright; the corpus's Prince charging into a walking Giant (charged hit at t1546, capture 20260920-003751) pins it on a moving target. contact_same_tick stays in the list as the refused candidate.
CHARGED_HIT_TIMING.engine: IMPLEMENTED (read by state.rs Calib::from_json -> charged_hit_timing): under first_attack_pass_no_windup combat.rs attack_step snaps a charged unit's progress to the next HitSpeed multiple on the attack pass that finds its target in range, so the DamageSpecial hit lands that tick (charge.RESET_ON_ATTACK then consumes the charge); after_load_time_windup is the runnable foil (no snap: the charged unit hits on the ordinary first-hit tick of combat.ATTACK_CYCLE -- under windup_load_time the LoadTime windup the engine ran before); contact_same_tick has no implementation and is refused at load. tests/reach.rs pins the arrival-tick hit on the sample's numbers; tests/charge.rs (2) the 783 / 391 amounts.

RESET_ON_STUN.provenance: A stun landing (Zap; the stun buffer applied in Resolve) clears the charge AND the run-up (wiki Zap: 'resets the charge of a Prince'). The false arm leaves both untouched: a charged Prince is still charged when the stun ends. Unsourced by any recording.
RESET_ON_STUN.promotion_rules: A capture: a Zap on a Prince already at S 120 -- S after the stun is 60 (true) or 120 (false); and the tower's first-hit delta after the stun.
RESET_ON_STUN.engine: state.rs Calib::charge_reset_on_stun, read by BattleState::apply_effects (the stun loop)

RESET_ON_KNOCKBACK.confidence: MEDIUM under knockback.DISPLACEMENT_LAW = client16402 (the ladder's states measured; the tick of the clear not yet captured); LOW under fixed_distance (its landing-tick clear is the old guess)
RESET_ON_KNOCKBACK.provenance: THE RULE under client16402: the run-up is not cleared by the landing itself -- a victim is in state 1 for the whole ladder and the clearing happens on the ladder's zero-speed and back-step ticks; the clearing is the charge tail's own, run inside every pushback tick on the ladder's requested step min(speed, dist, 250): step > 0 on a unit in state 1 with the run-up below 10000 -> progress += tdiv(step x 1000, ChargeRange), reaching 10000 fires the charge; a charged unit stays charged. Otherwise -- the ladder's ZERO-speed tick and its BACK-STEP tick (step 0 / -25), or a unit not in state 1 (states 5 and 8 exempt) -- progress = 0 and the charge is cleared, WHATEVER the progress was. Every projectile ladder ends with those two ticks, so the run-up and the charge are gone when the ladder ends -- the end state the old landing-tick clear gave, reached at the zero tick instead, with the run-up ADVANCING on the positive-speed ticks in between (a Prince at 9600 permille Logged at 175: 10200 and the charge on the first ladder tick, 0 and no charge on the zero tick). MEASURED: the victim's state is 1 through the ladder (the Giant of capture 20260918-122757.b1, ticks 1216..1223; the Bomber and the Knight of capture 20260920-081819-B, attacking when hit and state 1 from the first ladder tick); no capture yet shows a charging or charged unit inside a ladder, so the tick of the clear is a hypothesis. All three charge cards ship IgnorePushback, so under the shipped data a Fireball never pushes a Prince and only The Log (PushbackAll) does -- a PREDICTION of the data, not a modelling choice. The false arm skips the tail on ladder ticks: the run-up and the charge are held across the ladder.
RESET_ON_KNOCKBACK.promotion_rules: To measured: a Log on a CHARGED Prince -- S after the ladder 60 (true) or 120 (false) -- and, for the tick of the clear, a Log on a Prince mid-run-up whose progress the capture shows advancing on the positive ladder ticks and zeroed on the zero tick. A Fireball on a charging Prince (capture 20260920-080208, t1016) shows no displacement and no reset either way: it pins IgnorePushback, not this key.
RESET_ON_KNOCKBACK.engine: state.rs Calib::charge_reset_on_knockback: under DISPLACEMENT_LAW = client16402 read by BattleState::charge_pass on every ladder tick (phase_path16402 and step_pushback_ladders record the ladder's requested step in Scratch::walk_step and the tick in Scratch::pushed); under fixed_distance read by apply_effects (the landing-tick clear). tests/charge.rs (9) measures after the ladder; tests/knockback16402.rs pins the mid-ladder add and the zero-tick clear.

RESET_ON_RETARGET.provenance: Whether switching from one LIVE target to a DIFFERENT live target (state.rs phase_target; acquiring a first target or replacing a dead one is not a switch) clears the charge and the run-up. Shipped false: no source describes a Prince losing its charge to a passing unit, and true would make every Skeleton that crosses its sight reset it. The true arm is kept runnable for the recording.
RESET_ON_RETARGET.promotion_rules: A capture: a Prince at S 120 walking for the tower with a Skeleton dropped beside it -- S the tick after it retargets (120 under false, 60 under true).

SPECIAL_LEVEL_SCALING.provenance: How DamageSpecial scales with level. scale_special_base: a rarity-local level-1 stat like every other, through CardDb::scaled (rarities.csv PowerLevelMultiplier, truncating). twice_scaled_damage: the entity's scaled Damage times DamageSpecial / Damage (i.e. 2 x the scaled Damage on the shipped rows). The two agree at level 1 and part under truncation from local level 2 on: Prince at Epic local 2 (110 %) is scale(490, 110) = 539 against 2 x scale(245, 110) = 538. cards.json level_scaling.applies_to lists hitpoints and damage only and nothing reads it. Settleable from any published Prince stat sheet at two levels, cheaper than a recording.
SPECIAL_LEVEL_SCALING.promotion_rules: A published charge-damage ladder for the Prince at two levels whose truncations differ (local 2: 539 vs 538), or a captured charged hit at a level above 1.
SPECIAL_LEVEL_SCALING.engine: state.rs Calib::charge_special_level_scaling, read by combat.rs fire

$comment: THE PER-TICK LOCOMOTION LAW OF A GROUND TROOP, measured from the 15.535.29 traces on
2026-09-18. Order matters: re-derive the goal cell, replan if it moved, apply the
stomp pause, take the heading from the PRE-move position, step with per-axis
truncation, then consume at most one waypoint. Permuting it does not reproduce the
traces.
EVERY LAW HERE HAS A DOMAIN: CONTACT_DOMAIN. They hold for a unit that is not in
contact with another unit. Two of the three regimes that break them set no flag at
all, so an engine that fits card constants to crowded traces will absorb the
avoidance and separation terms into the wrong place.

HEADING_LAW.formula: d = node_centre - position (PRE-move); L = floor(sqrt(d.x^2 + d.y^2)); dir = (d.x * 256 / L, d.y * 256 / L) with integer division truncating toward zero
HEADING_LAW.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. 100 % on every isolated unit. The FLOORED length is what is load-bearing, not the sqrt routine: over 1258 walk ticks floor(sqrt) matches 1258, nearest-integer 1179, scale-then-sqrt 191, ceil 173. The PRE-move position as the origin scores 106-307 ticks per card against 85-264 for post-move.
HEADING_LAW.do_not: |dir| legitimately ranges 254.678..256.236 because each axis truncates independently -- DO NOT renormalise or clamp to 256. Heading is STATELESS: a pure function of position and current node, recomputed from scratch. No inertia, no angular smoothing, no turn-rate limit; it snaps 71.57 degrees in one tick on a spawn tick and nothing in the corpus exceeds that. RotateAngleSpeed exists as a card column but only turret-like cards set it (cannon_cart, zapmachine, minizapmachine, dartbarrell) -- none is a troop.

POSITION_ROUNDING.formula: position.x += trunc(S * dir.x / 256); position.y += trunc(S * dir.y / 256)
POSITION_ROUNDING.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. The sub-unit remainder is DISCARDED every tick: integrating this law alone from the first moving tick reproduces the final position exactly over 106-308 ticks with zero drift. Floor matches 0 of about 1000 discriminating ticks (dir.x < 0 on every moving tick of every walk unit, so floor and truncation differ on every one); round matches 17-43 per card; ceil 201/240.
POSITION_ROUNDING.engine_contract: Rust i32/i32 already truncates toward zero and is correct. Do NOT use f32 and do NOT use div_euclid. The pre-2026 models keep path::advance's 1/65536 fractional carry -- that carry is WRONG for this model and is not used by it.

STOMP_SPEED_RULE.formula: S = Speed if StopMovementAfterMS is unset, else floor(Speed * (StopMovementAfterMS + WaitMS) / StopMovementAfterMS)
STOMP_SPEED_RULE.rounding: THE ROUNDING IS FLOOR, MEASURED, which is what raises this key from MEDIUM to HIGH. MEASURED on the LIVE 16.402 client (the live corpus, 13 captures; the movement analysis, Ice Golem arm). The Giant and the Golem could never separate it -- 45 * 740/640 = 52 and 45 * 1200/1000 = 54 are whole numbers, so floor, round and truncate all agree and only ceil was excluded. THE ICE GOLEM SEPARATES IT: icegolemite.toml ships Speed 45, StopMovementAfterMS 470, WaitMS 80, and 45 * 550/470 = 52.6596. Over 2373 ISOLATED free-walk moving ticks, S = 52 scores 2231, S = 53 scores 29, S = 51 scores 104 and S = 54 scores 0. Floor. royalesim already computed floor -- card.rs `move_speed` is integer division on non-negative operands -- so this promotion adds evidence and changes no behaviour.
STOMP_SPEED_RULE.provenance: MEASURED as a value, PARTLY UNVERIFIED as a formula. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. The free per-unit fit gives Giant 52 and Golem 54 while their Speed column is 45 for both; 640/100 and 1000/200 are their shipped StopMovementAfterMS/WaitMS. It is a TWO-POINT fit: Speed + floor(Speed*Wait/Stop) agrees on every shipped stomp card. The offline corpus cannot identify the rounding mode -- floor, round and truncate all give Giant 52 / Golem 54, and only ceil is excluded -- but the live Ice Golem can, because its value is not a whole number: it reads 52 rather than 53, so the rounding is FLOOR. The formula itself is still a two-point fit on the SHAPE; what is settled is the rounding.
STOMP_SPEED_RULE.do_not: Do NOT apply WalkingSpeedTweakPercentage to movement -- it is animation only (the Golem carries both a 15 % tweak and a stop/wait, and 45 * 1.15 = 51.75 != 54). S is the UNBUFFED base.
STOMP_SPEED_RULE.cards: Shipped stomp cards: Giant 640/100, RoyalGiant 640/100, Golem 1000/200, IceGolemite 470/80, GoblinGiant (2026 only). Extracted into data/derived/cards.json as stop_movement_after_ms / wait_ms.
STOMP_SPEED_RULE.buffed_speed: MOVED to movement.BUFF_SPEED_RULE, which is now its own measured key -- the live corpus separated its rounding too. What stood here: 'CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (this key used to say a buffed speed was unmeasured because no trace has one; one does). data/oracle-native/rage/Knight_rage_seed2.jsonl.gz drops a Rage at tick 140. Fitting the free integer S of movement.POSITION_ROUNDING over the Knight's isolated ticks (behavior_state == 1, avoidance_offset == 0) gives S = 60 on t121..155, S = 78 on t156..217 and S = 60 again on t218..340: the buffed regime is the SAME law with a larger integer S, held for 62 ticks, and 78 = 60 x 1.3 exactly. WHAT IS STILL UNMEASURED IS THE ROUNDING, for the same reason as the stomp formula above: 60 x 1.3 is a whole number, so floor, round, truncate and ceil all give 78.'

BUFF_SPEED_RULE.formula: S_buffed = floor(S * SpeedMultiplier / 100), where S is the speed the unit ALREADY walks at (i.e. the STOMP_SPEED_RULE output for a stomp card, not the raw Speed column) and SpeedMultiplier is a property of the BUFF
BUFF_SPEED_RULE.provenance: MEASURED. LIVE CLIENT, CR 16.402 -- recorded from the real game and converted to the offline trace format. Traces: the live corpus, 13 captures, 200096 unit-ticks / 97205 moving ticks. Analysis: the movement pass over the live corpus (Rage, Ice Golem and step arms). WHERE THE MULTIPLIER LIVES: spells_other.csv Rage -> SummonCharacter RageBottle; characters/ragebottle.toml [BUILDING.RageBottle] DeathAreaEffect = 'Rage'; [AEO.Rage] Radius 3000, LifeDuration 4500 ms, BuffTime 1000 ms, CapBuffTimeToAreaEffectTime = true, OnlyOwnTroops = true, Buff = 'Rage'; [BUFF.Rage] SpeedMultiplier = 130. There is no SpeedMultiplier column in area_effect_objects.csv at all -- it is on the BUFF, not the area effect. THE ROUNDING IS FLOOR: the Knight (60 -> 78) and the Skeletons (90 -> 117) are exact products and prove nothing; the RAGED ICE GOLEM does -- its stomped base is 52, 52 * 1.3 = 67.6, and it walks at exactly 67, where round and ceil both give 68. The raged Knight holds S = 78 for t3508..t3563 (56 ticks = 2800 ms) and returns to 60 at t3565, in BOTH clients' captures of the same battle.
BUFF_SPEED_RULE.engine: RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED. royalesim applies no SpeedMultiplier anywhere today, so nothing reads this key yet; path2026.rs `step_delta` takes whatever integer speed it is handed and card.rs `move_speed` documents the rule. When a buff is implemented it must multiply the STOMPED speed and floor.
BUFF_SPEED_RULE.open_composition_order: WHICH OPERAND THE STOMP APPLIES TO IS NOT SETTLED. floor(52 * 130/100) = 67 and floor(floor(45 * 130/100) * 550/470) = floor(58 * 1.17021) = 67 both fit the Ice Golem; only floor(45 * 1.3 * 550/470) = 68 is excluded. A stomp card whose two orderings disagree would settle it.
BUFF_SPEED_RULE.not_this_key: The FREEZE is NOT measured here and must not be quoted from this key. The one Ice Spirit hit in the corpus (capture 20260918-134739, side-1 Knight at (3500, 23499), spirit at t1016) drives the step to exactly zero rather than to a scaled speed, which is consistent with SpeedMultiplier = -100 -- but the Knight retargets the spirit (behavior_state 1 -> 2, path cleared), is pushed 160 native units over 4 ticks, then holds still for 46 ticks = 2300 ms against an 1100 ms BuffTime, and a unit in state 2 does not walk anyway. Nothing in the corpus measures a PARTIAL slow at all. The Prince's ChargeSpeedMultiplier = 200 (ChargeRange 250) is the other buffed speed in the live corpus, at S = 120.
BUFF_SPEED_RULE.promotion_rules: Raise to HIGH with a second non-integral product on a different card, or with any partial slow. Re-open the composition order with a raged stomp card whose two orderings disagree.

ATTACKING_UNIT_MOVEMENT.confidence: HIGH. On the 16.402 corpus, like for like (the same 67 battles, the same aggregation), 78.72% of no-tower unit-ticks are within 250 under this value against 73.48% under frozen (190,810 of 242,388 against 176,978 of 240,868: +13,832 on the numerator, the denominator +0.6%), and where an attacking unit is displaced its step equals the separation push to the native unit (SpearGoblin (-81,-41), Skeleton (15,48), Knight (7,-15), Goblin (-66,0), all exact). The measured contact law agrees on attackers: on 8,920 attacking ticks in contact, it moves the unit on the ticks the unit moved (97.6-100% per card). Four named losses remain; see open.
ATTACKING_UNIT_MOVEMENT.meaning: frozen: a unit whose attack phase holds it (combat.ATTACK_CYCLE = progress_credit means every non-Idle phase) skips the whole move pass, so it does not walk, does not steer, and is not separated. separation_only: it does not walk, steer or advance the stomp clock, and the offset decay and separation scan run as they already do for a unit that is merely in range of its target. Both arms are implemented; the route is cleared under either, as on any transition to attacking (SPEC 5.3).
ATTACKING_UNIT_MOVEMENT.provenance: MEASURED 2026-09-24 on the 16.402 corpus, both values, like for like: the same 67 battles, the engine at RoyaleSim 32a2997 with movement.DEPLOYING_HEADING = kept, playable no-tower unit-ticks within 250: frozen 176,978 / 240,868 = 73.48%, separation_only 190,810 / 242,388 = 78.72%. The harness's default run reproduces the separation_only figure exactly. An earlier pair quoted here (58.99% -> 61.60%, with per-card gains) was taken on a population that can no longer be reproduced and is withdrawn. The frozen value this replaces took an attacking unit out of the move pass entirely, so nothing could push it out of a contact, and the corpus already said the game does. A CORRECTION RECORDED WITH IT: an intermediate analysis that day found attackers 'holding' in settled siege stacks (RascalGirls, Golemites, Guards, LavaPups) and looked for a gate that held them. There is none. The analysis had looked up each sub-unit's collision radius from its PARENT card (a RascalGirl given the Rascals' 750, a Golemite the Golem's), which invented the overlaps; with each unit's own radius those units are 0-49 native units clear of touching, not in contact, and under the measured contact law they stand still because nothing touches them.
ATTACKING_UNIT_MOVEMENT.promotion_rules: MEASURED AND NOT PROMOTED. The corpus refutes `frozen` as a TOTAL hold, and the naive alternative is worse on the corpus, so both statements stand and neither is the law. Run under both arms on the 73-fixture replay corpus (67 played, 40 as prefixes, same engine, same seeds, `--attacking-movement`): no-tower unit-ticks within 250 native go 56.5 per cent under `frozen` to 50.5 under `separation_only`, and the alive/missing/extra share DOUBLES, 10.8 per cent to 22.4. The population grows too, 270972 no-tower unit-ticks to 303842, which is the mechanism showing itself: separating an attacking unit pushes it out of range, so it stops attacking and walks back, battles run longer and units that should die survive. WHAT THAT MEANS: the push is real (the corpus has it) and it does NOT cost the attack in the game, so the missing piece is what keeps a pushed unit attacking. The next candidate to implement is a push that does not re-open the replan gate -- keep the target and the attack phase across the displacement -- rather than another measurement. DO NOT promote on the strength of the refutation alone: a refuted value with no better candidate is still the best available, and this corpus run is what says so. Tried, and it does not help, so nobody spends the hour again: leaving the ROUTE intact across the hold, on the argument that a fresh replan after every push is what diverges, gives 50.6 per cent against 50.5 with the clear. The replan is not the cost.

The two 15.535.29 figures are re-measured on fixtures whose deploy ticks were corrected the same evening; on the mislabelled ones they read 46.1 -> 35.7 and 98.4 -> 67.0, so both losses survive the correction. Under this value the engine separates units that the recordings show are not touching, and every one is created by a formation or a split. HALF SETTLED 2026-09-24: the engine's contact step, handed the RECORDED positions of every attacking tick in 75 traces, gives the recorded position on 100.0% of them for every card (RascalGirl moved on 3 of 926 ticks, recorded 3; LavaPups 39/39; Golemite 23/23). So the step is right on the game's positions, and the losses come from its inputs in a battle: where the engine created the units, or the bodies the battle loop hands the step. Two differences in those bodies are named: they are indexed in slot order, while the neighbour query breaks ties by update order, and a slot reused by a newer unit puts it ahead of older ones (swapping two neighbours' order moves a walking unit 114 native units); and a held unit (stunned, frozen or knocked back) is left out of its neighbours' separation. Each becomes its own key with the present behaviour as the old arm. Every spawn takes its own card's collision radius, so a parent-card radius is ruled out there.

STOMP_PAUSE_SCHEDULE.ms_clock: THE CLOCK, NOT THE TICK INDEX. ms_clock (shipped): the unit keeps a MILLISECOND clock that advances by tdiv(compose(Speed, 100), 2) on every tick it actually walks -- 50 unbuffed, 65 under Rage (the same composition as movement.BUFF_SPEED_COMPOSITION, applied to 100) -- and the tick is paused iff the post-increment clock is strictly above StopMovementAfterMS and still short of StopMovementAfterMS + WaitMS; when it reaches the period the remainder is carried forward. UNBUFFED the advance is 50 and the clock equals ((k + 1) x 50) mod period exactly, so ms_clock reproduces the measured tick-index schedule below tick for tick, and the two candidates part ONLY under a buff -- 65 ms a tick under Rage, where the residue drifts 15 ms a tick and a pause group can run four ticks long. MEASURED on the live 16.402 raged Golem of capture 20260919-143305-B: 168 of 169 walking ticks reproduced under ms_clock, where the tick-index law keeps the unbuffed 13-tick runs and drifts off the recording within one period. The clock does not advance on a tick the unit does not walk (speed 0: attacking, deploying, frozen), which is what `move_ticks` already did.
STOMP_PAUSE_SCHEDULE.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted. Under ms_clock the per-entity state is entity.rs `stomp_clock` (milliseconds); under the older arm it is `move_ticks` (the index k). Both are kept and both are hashed, so the two arms are switchable on one tree.
STOMP_PAUSE_SCHEDULE.formula: with k the unit's moving-tick index (k = 0 on its first moving tick, NEVER reset), skip the position update iff ((k + 1) * TICK_MS) % (StopMovementAfterMS + WaitMS) > StopMovementAfterMS

Strict > beats >= (304/308, 294/306); (k+1) beats k (268/308, 282/306); every phase offset was brute-forced and only 0 fits. A naive 'move 640 ms then wait 100 ms' countdown gives 13 moving ticks in the Giant's first block and the traces show 12.
STOMP_PAUSE_SCHEDULE.scope: The pause gates the unit's OWN LOCOMOTION, not the position write: external displacement still applies during a freeze -- a jostled Giant moves on 2 of 323 scheduled pause ticks.
STOMP_PAUSE_SCHEDULE.k_counts_every_locomotion_tick: `k` ADVANCES ON EVERY LOCOMOTION TICK FROM THE FIRST MOVING TICK, PAUSES INCLUDED. the spec's phrase 'moving-tick index' is ambiguous and the live 16.402 corpus forces this reading: if `k` advanced only on ticks that actually MOVED it would stick at the first pause and the unit would never move again. Under this reading the Ice Golem's pauses are an exact period-11 progression in absolute tick number (Stop 470 + Wait 80 = 550 ms = 11 ticks, runs of 10 moving ticks) and the Giant's are period 740 ms with 13-tick runs. Traces: the live corpus; the movement analysis. VERIFIED IN THE ENGINE, by reading it rather than by assuming it: state.rs `phase_path_2026` increments `kticks[i]` BEFORE the `stomp_paused` test and `continue`s afterwards, so a pause tick still advances the counter. The increment's position is pinned by a comment there.
