CONTACT_DOMAIN.provenance: MEASURED, and this is a statement about what is NOT known. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: passes over the offline traces -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. Three regimes break every law in this section and TWO OF THEM SET NO FLAG AT ALL: avoidance (behavior_state 1, avoidance_offset != 0, heading deflected, |step| within +-2.3 % of S); crowd separation (behavior_state 1, NO flag, |step| about S plus a 15-28 unit lateral residual perpendicular to the heading); combat pushback (behavior_state 2, NO flag, displacement 0.06-2.5 x S, can oppose the heading). 174 flagless failures corpus-wide: 137 at state 1, 36 at state 2, 1 at state 4.
CONTACT_DOMAIN.not_directly_observable: The push is not separately observable in the corpus; it must be inferred from the residual between the predicted and the observed step. Keep it separate from the locomotion law (STOMP_PAUSE_SCHEDULE) so that a pushed unit still moves during a stomp pause. Confirmed again on the live corpus: 1 of 200096 unit-ticks shows anything else.
CONTACT_DOMAIN.defining_isolated: 'FREE WALK' MEANS ISOLATED BY DISTANCE, NOT `avoidance_offset == 0`. This is the single easiest way to get a wrong number out of this corpus, and any regression gate written against the flags will look broken on live data for the wrong reason. Offline the traces were single units on an empty board, so the two definitions were the same thing; live they are not, because the corpus records no push of its own AND the separation impulse leaves no flag either. MEASURED on the LIVE 16.402 corpus (the live corpus; the movement analysis, step and push arms): filtering on the fields alone gives step-law exactness 0.7273; adding an isolation radius of 2000 native to the nearest OTHER MOBILE UNIT gives 0.9807; adding Rage and the Prince charge gives 0.99903. Exactness by distance to the nearest other mobile unit -- 0-499: 0.433, 500-999: 0.281, 1000-1499: 0.793, 1500-1999: 0.970, 2000-2499: 0.987, 6000-6499: 0.994. USE d > 2000 native. About 27 % of all live moving ticks are crowded, so no crowded tick can be reproduced bit-exactly until the separation magnitude is fitted.
CONTACT_DOMAIN.what_the_live_pass_refined: Two of the three regimes are better understood, and neither is implemented. AVOIDANCE: on about 11 % of moving ticks (22158 of them) the step is a quantised ROTATION of the pure path heading rather than the heading itself; |step|/S has median 1.0006, so the length is unchanged and only the direction turns. The rotation is monotone in its magnitude and independent of the distance to the node (71.45 deg at d ~ 1082 and 71.60 deg at d ~ 1493 at the largest magnitude seen), so it is a rotation, not a lateral shift of the aim point -- but it is NOT linear (0.256 deg/unit at the smallest magnitude rising to 0.375 deg/unit at the largest; asin(a/256), asin(a*sqrt(2)/256), tan and 1/1024-of-a-turn were all tried and all miss somewhere), and what SETS it is still unknown -- it fires against static occluders too (one Knight of the 2026-09-18 corpus is at the largest magnitude at t3413 with the nearest mobile unit 8315 native away, walking past its own princess tower). SEPARATION: the residual that actually breaks the step law sets none of the three fields; over 24887 off-law ticks with a neighbour inside 1600 native, observed - predicted points AWAY from the nearest neighbour within 7.5 deg on 57.0 % and within 22.5 deg on 65.5 %, and at 180 deg on only 1.3 %, and it fires at a separation peaking exactly at 1.0 x (own CollisionRadius + neighbour CollisionRadius) -- bins 0.9: 4225, 1.0: 11442, 1.1: 4633. The MAGNITUDE is still unfitted (10-unit bins 0: 2893, 10: 3878, 20: 3372, 30: 2782, 40: 2169, 50: 1870, 60: 1668) and no Mass / PushMassFactor term has been tried.
CONTACT_DOMAIN.avoidance_offset: UNVERIFIED, DO NOT GUESS. It is set to +-190 in one tick and then performs a +-10-per-tick walk bounded at +-190 -- 16 of 36 runs ramp back UP before coming down, and runs reach 67 ticks against the 19 a pure decay implies. Do NOT implement 'decremented by 10 per tick toward 0'. What sets it, what selects the sign, and what deflection it applies (the ratio of heading error to offset is 0.327-0.387, non-linear) are all unmeasured.

JUMP_WATER_HOP.provenance: MEASURED step for step on the five river hops of live capture 20260920-002736 (Hog Rider hop t220 landing t242, Prince t323 -> t345, Royal Hog 1 t514 -> t536, Royal Hog 2 t519 -> t545, Royal Hog 3 t521 -> t532; fixture tests/fixtures/oracle2026/client16402_jumps.json, tools/make_client16402_jump_fixture.py; gate tests/jump16402.rs) and implemented in crates/royalesim/src/jump16402.rs and state.rs phase_path16402. THE LAW. A JumpEnabled troop plans like a walker except that its cost field prices water at WATER_COST (PATHFINDING_COSTS); from the river centre (9500, 12500) the Hog's list runs through the water cells (24,30)..(26,32) to the bridge's far corner cell (27,33) -- the cost-7 diagonal, not the bridge detour -- and the hop fires on the pop before the first water node (the fixture's Hog Rider case); from the lane placements the line north is a bridge column and the flag changes nothing. The hop is the WALK's: on the tick a waypoint is reached and popped, if the card is JumpEnabled, at least two nodes remain and the new last node -- the next waypoint -- is a water cell, the list is replaced by ONE node, the first non-water node scanning from the node after it toward the goal, or the goal when every remaining node is water; the segment is refreshed from the POST-move position, the distance from that position to the node's centre is recorded, and the unit enters the LEAP (movement state 5 in the captures). Every leaping tick: no path request; no avoidance scan, but the offset decays; no separation scan, and every neighbour's scan skips the unit (NON-COLLIDABLE); speed = JumpSpeed raw (no buff, no charge multiplier; 0 under a movement hold); the ordinary step law toward the node's centre with the facing set; then the LANDING TEST n_rem = tdiv(dist(centre, pos'), JumpSpeed) on the post-move position: n_rem <= 1 -> the walk resumes and requests a fresh path from wherever the unit is (Royal Hog 3 lands ON water cell (9, 30) and walks off it). The reached flag is ignored during the leap; no node is popped. THE MEASUREMENT: the Hog leaps (113, 113) per tick along (181, 181)/256 from (11096, 14096) for 22 ticks and lands at (13582, 16582), 237 from the bridge node's centre (< 2 x 160); the tick before it was 397 away (>= 320) and still leaping; each of the five hops replays from its trigger frame, and the Hog Rider's and the Prince's battles replay end to end through the engine with every published node list. walk_priced_water (the jumper walks the priced water at its Speed, no leap) fails 3 of the 8 gates; a landing decided by the reached flag, as for a walk, fails 4. Over the replay corpus the `jump` family's unit-ticks within 250 native rose from 26.0 % to 52.9 % (15035 unit-ticks). The charge run-up is HELD across the leap (charge.PROGRESS_ON_STOP does not fire; state.rs charge_pass, Scratch::jumped); the Prince's battle replays under that rule. JumpHeight draws the visual arc only: no position, not modelled.
JUMP_WATER_HOP.cards: JumpEnabled rows: the 2018 data set has HogRider only (TRUE / JumpHeight 4000 / JumpSpeed 160 -> cards.json `jump` {height_raw, speed}, card.rs JumpDef); the 15.535 card data gives Prince, DarkPrince, the Battle Ram's Ram, RoyalHog (and VoodooHog, PrinceBuff, SuperHogRider, Prince_Chess) the identical block. MegaKnight (3000 / 250) and Assassin (JumpSpeed 500) carry the columns WITHOUT JumpEnabled: their attack jump is a movement state of its own, not modelled, and they get no block. So the engine's Prince / Dark Prince / Battle Ram walk to the bridge until cards.json is re-extracted from a post-2019 data set; tests/jump16402.rs reproduces the Prince's hop by giving the Prince the Hog's block, which is what the 15.535 data does.
JUMP_WATER_HOP.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json, calib_enum JumpWaterHop); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted. client16402: state.rs phase_path16402 -- the trigger after the reached pop, the leap in place of the whole per-unit update while entity.rs `jumping` (snapshot format 11), jump16402.rs landing_node / landed / cell_centre; the unit is non-collidable (move16402 Body::collidable) and its attack is held (phase_attack can_act). walk_priced_water: no trigger -- the jumper walks the cost-7 water at its Speed, the naive reading of the cost field that the five live hops refute, kept runnable as the foil. Under pathfinding.PATH_SEARCH = trace_fitted_astar neither applies (water impassable, no JumpEnabled test).
JUMP_WATER_HOP.open: (1) the attack side of a leap -- whether a target in range interrupts it, and whether a leaping unit is targetable / hittable (the engine keeps it targetable and holds its own swing); (2) a movement hold (Zap / Freeze) on a jumper: the engine cancels the leap where the unit stands and replans when the hold ends (no capture has a stunned or frozen jumper); (3) a pushback landing mid-leap: the ladder runs in place of the leap and drops the path on its back-step tick, after which the leap aims like a walker with no nodes -- unexercised; (4) the engine publishes the landing's fresh path one Path phase after the capture's same-tick publish; positions agree on every tick because the first walk step falls on the same tick either way.
JUMP_WATER_HOP.promotion_rules: SETTLED on five live hops. Re-open only against a new client build; a capture of a Prince / Dark Prince leaping WHILE charged (the raw JumpSpeed, no multiplier, and the held run-up), a hop from a position whose priced-water route beats the bridge (the goal cell on the far bank within reach of a unit standing on the near bank, e.g. a jumper attacking a troop standing at the water's edge), and a Zap / Freeze landing on a leaping unit (open item 2) extend the evidence.
JUMP_WATER_HOP.units: native millitiles; JumpSpeed is native units per tick, the Speed column's unit
JUMP_WATER_HOP.plant: tests/jump16402.rs (8): jumper_pays_blocked (a jumper priced like a walker) red on 5, jump_never_hops (the cost-7 walk, no leap) red on 3, jump_never_lands (the reached flag decides, as for a walk) red on 4; goal_ignores_flying_target (the global passed unconditionally) red on the flying-target case and green on every oracle2026.rs gate

DYING_UNIT_VISIBILITY.provenance: MEASURED on the live 16.402 captures: a unit that dies during tick t (gone in frame t) is still counted by the separation / avoidance scans of the movers BEFORE it in creation order and no longer by the movers AFTER it -- 99 : 5 versus 35 : 0 decidable cases; a building that dies during tick t is counted by every mover (3 / 3). INFERRED, the mechanism not observable in the frames: the death takes effect at the victim's own place in the creation-ordered move pass, and a building has no place in that pass.
DYING_UNIT_VISIBILITY.meaning: creation_order_before_victim: in state.rs phase_path16402 a per-tick DOOMED mask is derived before the pass from the damage buffer as it stands when the move pass begins (this tick's Attack-phase hits, the Status-phase lifetime expiries and the previous Reap's death damage: the hits that in the measured order have landed before the move pass) -- a troop with no shield whose hp the buffered sum takes to 0 or below, hide immunity respected; when the pass reaches a doomed troop in creation order its own update is skipped (it neither walks nor is pushed on its death tick: the 'processed at its own place' reading, unobservable in the frames) and it is removed from every later mover's scans; movers before it saw it at its start-of-tick position. Buildings are never masked. whole_tick: no mask -- every mover sees the dying unit for the whole pass, the engine's earlier behaviour, kept runnable as the foil. The mask is a read-only derivation: no entity is mutated inside the pass (the hp write stays in Resolve, the despawn in Reap).
DYING_UNIT_VISIBILITY.promotion_rules: Measured on 134 decidable live cases with the mechanism inferred. A capture with several troops dying in one tick inside a crowd (Skeleton Army under a Fireball) extends the evidence and tests whether the victim's own step runs on its death tick.
DYING_UNIT_VISIBILITY.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json, calib_enum DyingUnitVisibility); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted. state.rs BattleState::doomed_mask and phase_path16402 (PATH_SEARCH = client16402 only: the frame-planned arms have no sequential pass, so nothing there orders on it); tests/tick_order.rs `a_unit_dying_this_tick_is_seen_by_earlier_movers_and_not_by_later_ones` constructs three overlapping Skeletons around a Knight's landing hit under both candidates.
DYING_UNIT_VISIBILITY.why_it_matters: The 655 unexplained live ticks (0.27 %) are Skeleton crowds with several dying neighbours in the same tick; the mask decides which of them still push on their death tick.

SPAWN_PATHFIND_STATES.confidence: MEDIUM on the SPEED, the GOAL and the missing LANE BONUS, which the corpus separates (the lane bonus on one path); LOW on the occlusions, which nothing recorded separates
SPAWN_PATHFIND_STATES.provenance: RECORDED ahead of a card that exercises it, so the next pass has the rule to test. client16402_explicit_goal_no_lane_no_occlusion: a spawn-pathfinding unit (the Miner's and the Goblin Drill's underground walk to the point where it comes up, the Wallbreakers' run-in) walks in a movement state of its own (6 in the captures' state column; no capture holds a state 7) toward an explicit goal position rather than a scanned goal cell, at SpawnPathfindSpeed. THE SPEED IS MEASURED: capture 20260920-083112, both seats, holds 175 state-6 entity-frames, and on every tick-adjacent pair of them the step is the card's SpawnPathfindSpeed -- the Goblin Drill 300 on 75 of 143 straight pairs and 297-299 on the diagonals, the Miner 650 on 6 of 10 and 646-647 on the rest -- against the card Speeds of 60 and 90, so a unit walking at its card speed is out by 5x and 7x. THE GOAL AND THE LANE BONUS ARE NOW MEASURED TOO (measured_2026_09_22); THE OCCLUSIONS ARE NOT, because no recorded spawn path comes near a building box, hence hypothesis for the value as a whole. The reached threshold is taken from SpawnPathfindSpeed rather than the fixed 1000, measured on the same frames (pathfinding.LOGIC_SPAWN_PATHFIND_REACHED_RADIUS_FROM_SPEED). Also recorded, not modelled: the dash (DashDistance cards; it reuses the leap's movement state), the attack jump (MegaKnight, Assassin: JumpSpeed with sub-steps of 250 and a water-clamped landing), and a rider copying its mount's position.
SPAWN_PATHFIND_STATES.measured_2026_09_22: The replay fixtures now publish each unit's path (data/derived/replay, truth.path_cells, goal first), so the state-6 paths of 20260920-083112-A and -B can be scored: 5 distinct units (3 Goblin Drills, 2 Miners), each seen from both seats with the same lists. THE GOAL: the path's goal cell is the cell holding the point where the unit comes up (the Drill's building, the Miner's first position after state 6) on 5 of 5, and the tap's own cell on 1 of 5 (the game moves a tap it will not accept). For the Drill of tick 2974 that point, (3000, 23000), is a cell corner, and the goal (6, 46) is not the one of its four cells nearest the unit ((6, 45) is), so a goal chosen by the ordinary nearest-cell scan around the point would have missed it. THE LANE BONUS: one path separates the arms, that Drill's 39 cells from its king to (6, 46). With every dry cell at 8 and water at 50 it is cost-optimal (3424) and the 16.402 search returns all 39 cells from the unit's own cell (18, 7); with road cells at 5 it costs 2908 against an optimum of 2380, and no start next to it returns it. (The search was run as a line-for-line Python port of path16402.rs, which returns 615 of 616 live and 128 of 128 offline paths of crates/royalesim/tests/fixtures/oracle2026/client16402_first_paths.json exactly under the walker's costs, the engine gate's own score. With every dry cell at 8 it returns only 123 of those 616: ordinary walking has the lane bonus, spawn pathfinding does not.) The three shorter paths (4, 4 and 7 cells) fit every arm. THE WATER: the same path crosses the river on the bridge (column 8). Water at 7 makes it more expensive than a crossing through the water (3424 against 3368), and water at 8 keeps it cost-optimal but is not the route the search returns, so a spawn-pathfinding unit pays the walker's 50. THE OCCLUSIONS: not separated. No spawn path comes near a building box except its own king's, which the unit starts inside and must leave either way; stamping every building of both sides at 50 returns all four paths too. Recorded by the client instrument that records ground-truth traces from the real game.
SPAWN_PATHFIND_STATES.cards: Which cards need it (data/derived/mechanic_register.json, tools/mechanic_register.py): spawn pathfinding (SpawnPathfindSpeed / SpawnPathfindEffect / SpawnPathfindMorph, family spawner) -- Miner and GoblinDrill (the underground walk to the tap point, state 6 / 7), Wallbreakers (the run-in), and the register's family `dash` -- Bandit (Assassin), MegaKnight's jump, Bats, DarkWitch, GoldenKnight, LittlePrince, BossBandit, SuperHogRider Terry -- for states 3 / 5. None of them is in the engine's cards.json thin slice today: no ENGINE card carries an explicit goal, so no engine unit ever walks in state 6 and the cost field's state test is never reached. The corpus does hold them: 175 state-6 frames, all in capture 20260920-083112 (Goblin Drill 162, Miner 13).
SPAWN_PATHFIND_STATES.engine: RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED. Not read by Calib::from_json -- like movement.BUFF_SPEED_RULE, a rule the engine records ahead of a card that exercises it; when Miner / GoblinDrill / Wallbreakers enter the thin slice the key becomes a Calib field, the cost closure in state.rs phase_path16402 gains the state test and path16402::choose_goal_cell is bypassed by the explicit goal. WHAT THE ENGINE WILL THEN DO: price every dry cell at DEFAULT (8) with no lane bonus and water at BLOCKED (50), and run to the cell holding the explicit goal point, all three measured (measured_2026_09_22); skip the building boxes and the avoidance and separation scans, which remain choices awaiting the capture named in promotion_rules and not observations. Until then the value names the rule and `not_modelled` is what the engine does.
SPAWN_PATHFIND_STATES.promotion_rules: The speed, goal and lane clauses are measured (capture 20260920-083112; measured_2026_09_22). To measured for the value as a whole: a spawn path that has to pass a building box other than its own king's, for example a Goblin Drill or a Miner sent to a point with a building standing on the straight line to it. A path straight through the box (every building ignored) against a detour around it (boxes stamped) settles the last clause.
SPAWN_PATHFIND_STATES.units: native millitiles; SpawnPathfindSpeed is native units per tick

BUFF_SPEED_COMPOSITION.confidence: MEDIUM (the single-buff case is measured; no corpus frame carries two speed buffs on one unit)
BUFF_SPEED_COMPOSITION.formula: S' = tdiv(max(0, min(100, 100 - maxneg)) * tdiv(maxpos * S, 100), 100), with maxpos = max(100, the positive SpeedMultipliers on the unit), maxneg = max(0, the negations of the negative ones), a zero column skipped
BUFF_SPEED_COMPOSITION.provenance: HOW SEVERAL SPEED BUFFS COMBINE, and where the charge multiplies. strongest_up_and_down (shipped): over the unit's buffs, maxpos = the largest positive SpeedMultiplier (at least 100) and maxneg = the largest negation of a negative one (at least 0), a zero column skipped; then S' = tdiv(max(0, min(100, 100 - maxneg)) * tdiv(maxpos * S, 100), 100), and the ChargeSpeedMultiplier multiplies THAT result. Only the strongest speed-up and the strongest slow count, two Rages are one Rage, and Freeze's -100 makes the whole product 0. movement.BUFF_SPEED_RULE recorded the SINGLE-buff case of this same law (floor(S x SpeedMultiplier / 100)), MEASURED on the live 16.402 raged Ice Golem (52 -> 67, where round and ceil both give 68); this key generalises it, and `single_multiplier_floor` is that arm kept runnable (the first buff's multiplier alone). Corpus effect of this key together with HIT_SPEED_BUFF and STOMP_PAUSE_SCHEDULE: Dark Prince 83.4 -> 100.0 % within 250 and 90.9 -> 100.0 % hp exact, Prince 70.7 -> 74.8 %, pushback family 69.4 -> 71.7 %, charge 61.8 -> 64.7 %.
BUFF_SPEED_COMPOSITION.promotion_rules: A unit carrying a Rage and a slow at once: 45 -> tdiv(130 x 45, 100) = 58 -> tdiv(85 x 58, 100) = 49 under strongest_up_and_down, against tdiv(45 x 115, 100) = 51 for an engine that adds the two percentages. No frame of the 75-capture corpus has both on one unit, so the corpus cannot yet separate them.
BUFF_SPEED_COMPOSITION.engine: read by crates/royalesim (state.rs Calib::from_json); a candidate without an engine implementation is refused at load, never silently substituted

$comment: THE SUMMON FORMATION: where a card's N summons stand around the tap and when each
leaves its deploy state (spells_characters.csv SummonNumber / SummonRadius / SummonWidth /
SummonDeployDelay / SummonCharacterSecond / SummonCharacterSecondCount /
SummonDeployDelaySecond; characters.csv SpawnRadius / SpawnAngleShift; globals.csv
LOGIC_LANE_ID_BASED_DEPLOY_SEQUENCE). The columns are card data (data/derived/cards.json
`summon_*` / `second_summon` / `spawn_radius_milli` / `spawn_angle_shift_deg`, read by
card.rs `FormationDef`); every rule they do not settle is a key below. The layout model is
crates/royalesim/src/formation.rs, fitted to and held to every clean multi-unit deploy of
the live 16.402 corpus (tests/fixtures/formations/measured.json, tools/make_formation_fixture.py,
tests/formations.rs) after the whole-battle replay harness put 33 of 48 first divergences on
the old square grid (the formation gap of the corpus report). Column semantics taken as
given, not keyed: SummonNumber = the primaries' count; a blank SummonRadius / SummonWidth /
delay is 0; SummonCharacterSecondCount members follow the primaries in creation order and
take the card's unified level (the same rule as a spawner's unit; SpawnCharacterLevelIndex
is not carried).

LAYOUT.provenance: MEASURED on the live 16.402 corpus through tools/replay_formations.py; tests/formations.rs pins every clean multi-unit deploy group from tests/fixtures/formations/measured.json (79 groups, 16 cards, both seats, both lanes, both ends of every column the corpus taps, the towers down per tick): 78 groups member by member, 197 members exact (within 3 native), one native unit off only where the placement log's tap tile and the formation's centre differ. THE MODEL (formation.rs `member_offset` / `nearest_lane` / `sin1024`, state.rs `formation_members`): the members are the SummonNumber primaries followed by the SummonCharacterSecondCount second summons. THE RADIUS: SummonRadius, or when 0 the primary character's CollisionRadius replaced by its SpawnRadius when that is set (Minions 500, SkeletonWarrior 800). THE LANE: the lane bits of the nearest lane-marked half-tile cell to the tap (first minimum in column-outer scan order); on the shipped map, left of the centre column is 1 and the rest 2. THE OFFSET: the ring count T is SummonNumber, or 2 x max(SummonNumber, SecondCount) with a second summon; T sets the base angle and the mirrored lane -- T = 1: the tap; T = 2: base SpawnAngleShift + 90, mirror on lane 1; T = 3: 180, lane 1; T = 4: 45, lane 2; T = 5: 180, lane 2; T = 6: 0, lane 2; T = 7: member 0 on the tap and the rest a hexagon nobody mirrors; T >= 8: 0, lane 2 -- the mirror only under globals.csv LOGIC_LANE_ID_BASED_DEPLOY_SEQUENCE = TRUE (both vintages). With no SummonWidth and T >= 3 the radius becomes radius x 577 / trunc(1000 x sin(90 / SummonNumber) / 1024) (sin from a 91-entry round(sin x 1024) table, integer degrees: 700 -> 807 for three, 700 -> 1077 for four (sin 22, not 22.5), 700 -> 1311 for five, 600 -> 1341 for six, 1000 -> 1154 for the Gang's 3 + 3), then SpawnAngleShift is added to the base and a swarm of eight or more puts member k at radius x ((3k) mod 7) / 6 (the Skeleton Army's spiral). Member k's angles (no second summon): ay = 360k / T + base + 90, ax = ay + 90, x = trunc(sin(ax) x r / 1024), y = trunc(sin(ay) x r / 1024); with a second summon the primaries start half a step in and the seconds interleave 180 degrees on, the y sign flipped. SummonWidth makes a LINE: x = W k / (T - 1) - W / 2, y = (k mod 2) x r - r / 2, the mirror then 'lane 1' without the global (RoyalHogs 3500). Side 0 negates y and the mirror negates x. The point is then y-clamped for a ground unit (GROUND_Y_CLAMP) and clamped into [250, W - 250] x [250, H - 250] native. THE CORPUS: Skeletons (0, 807) / (+-699, -403) on both lanes and both sides, Goblins (+-761, +-761), Minions (0, 577) / (+-499, -288), Skeleton Warriors (0, 923) / (+-799, -461), Spear Goblins, Barbarians (0, 1311) / (+-1246, 404) / (+-770, -1060), Minion Horde (0, +-1341) / (+-1161, +-670), Bats with their SpawnAngleShift 45 (1404-ring), Wall Breakers (+-750, 0), Skeleton Dragons (+-1500, 0), Archers (+-500, 0), Goblin Gang's hexagon (+-999, +-577) / (0, +-1154), the Rascals' Boy at (0, 1731) with the Girls at (+-1223, -1223), the Royal Hogs' line and the Skeleton Army's spiral -- exact on every member the contact law had not yet moved. THE ENGINE computes in the OWNER's frame (the owner's-frame lane, side 0's y sign) and rotates the point for Red; the corpus' Red formations are the rotations of its Blue ones (a rotation swaps the lanes and the y sign together; formation.rs `member_offset`). NOT MODELLED: a card whose units come from SummonCharactersList carries an explicit SummonCharactersOffsetsX/Y table with CharactersOffsetsXMirrored (the Three Musketeers, one corpus group at (0, 1000) / (+-1000, -1000)); such a card stays on its `count` alone (card.rs `convert`) and tests/formations.rs asserts its ring does NOT match the corpus.
LAYOUT.meaning: client16402: the ring / line / spiral above (formation.rs), every member on a native point. engine_grid: the earlier engine, a centred square grid of one collision diameter around the tap in the owner's frame (state.rs formation_grid, the second summon on the same grid), kept runnable as the refuted arm: 500-1500 native off on every swarm, 3.6 % / 15.5 % of the Skeletons' / Goblins' unit-ticks within 250 native on the corpus against 39.2 % / 36.5 % under the ring.
LAYOUT.promotion_rules: Stays measured; the open part is the offsets-table layout of a SummonCharactersList card: a Three Musketeers corpus group on each seat and lane, with every tower standing, decides it once the loader accepts the card.
LAYOUT.engine: state.rs Calib::from_json (pick), BattleState::formation_members; formation.rs; tests/formations.rs (plant formation_grid_legacy)

DEPLOY_STAGGER.provenance: MEASURED on the live 16.402 corpus (tools/replay_formations.py; tests/formations.rs over tests/fixtures/formations/measured.json): member k leaves its deploy state at spawn + 19 + 2k ticks on every 100 ms card (Minion Horde 215..225 for a spawn at 195, Goblin Gang 571..581, Barbarians 1351..1359, Bats, Wall Breakers, Royal Hogs), at spawn + 19 + 4k on the Goblins (SummonDeployDelay 200), all at spawn + 19 on the Skeletons and the Skeleton Army (blank), and the Rascals' Girls at 21 / 23 behind the Boy's 19 (SummonDeployDelaySecond 100 with the first blank) -- k x SummonDeployDelay on top of the unit's DeployTime, exactly, on every group (a transition seen one frame late where the capture skipped a frame, never early). THE RULE (formation.rs `stagger_ms`, state.rs `formation_members`): member k >= 1 of the primaries waits k x SummonDeployDelay; the j-th second-summon member (j + 1) x SummonDeployDelaySecond when the first column is blank; a summoned BUILDING's members all take the flat SummonDeployDelay (a hypothesis: no such card is in the slice); no wait without a DeployTime. THE ENGINE adds the wait to the member's deploy timer (PendingSpawn.deploy_ms = DeployTime + wait): the member stands in its deploy state for the whole of it -- non-walking and non-attacking; whether it can be targeted or pushed while it waits is formation.STAGGER_WAIT.
DEPLOY_STAGGER.meaning: client16402: the waits above. none: every member deploys on the same tick (the earlier engine).
DEPLOY_STAGGER.promotion_rules: Stays measured for the waits; the flat building delay and whether a waiting member can be hit differently from a deploying one take a designed capture of a summoned building with a SummonDeployDelay and a spell landing on a staggered group before its last member is out.
DEPLOY_STAGGER.engine: state.rs Calib::from_json (pick), BattleState::formation_members; formation.rs stagger_ms; tests/formations.rs

STAGGER_WAIT.confidence: HIGH on both halves for the corpus' staggered units (Goblins, Goblin Gang, Minions, Minion Horde, Spear Goblins, Bats, Royal Hogs, Archers, Guards, Rascals); OPEN on spells, knockback and pulls, which no corpus event puts on a waiting member (see open), and which keep their earlier reach.
STAGGER_WAIT.provenance: MEASURED on the 16.402 corpus, one seat per battle. A summon member waiting out its formation.DEPLOY_STAGGER wait is in a state of its own, distinct from deploying. (1) IT IS NEVER TARGETED: 0 of 972,681 truth target rows point at a waiting member, against 2,315 at deploying ones, and in all 27 acquisitions where a waiting enemy was the closer eligible candidate, the attacker took a farther one. (2) IT NEVER MOVES: 1083 of 1083 consecutive-frame pairs inside the wait are still, against 1505 of 17530 pairs inside the deploy that move; in the traced case a Goblin is pushed on the very frame its wait ends while its neighbour, still waiting, stays put. (3) THE WAIT IS EXACTLY THE STAGGER: on contiguous frames a member is seen waiting for its stagger less one tick (Goblins 3, 7 and 11 frames at SummonDeployDelay 200 ms; Bats and Minions 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 at 100 ms), and 156 of 162 such spans are followed by exactly 20 frames of deploying, the unit's own DeployTime (4 at 19, 2 cut short by the capture). So a member waits while its deploy timer exceeds its own DeployTime. CORPUS PRE-SCORE, alone, on RoyaleSim dd956b4: within 250 +581, both-alive -258, hp exact -343; Goblins +674, GoblinGang +914; battle 124946 -774, a downstream cascade after two trigger points the arm gets exactly right. THE FOUR TOGETHER (formation.STAGGER_WAIT, spawner.TIMER_LEFTOVER, spawner.DEATH_SPAWN_AT_EMISSION_POINT, spawner.DEATH_SPAWN_RADIUS_DEFAULT = zero), stacked as overrides on RoyaleSim 157da9f over the 16.402 corpus fixtures: 128,094 of 156,718 playable no-tower unit-ticks within 250 (81.74%), against the base's 126,669 of 156,500 (80.94%): +1,425. The both-alive denominator moves with the treatment, so the counts, not the percentages, are the comparison. Per card: Goblins +829, GoblinGang +914, Tombstone +595; Knight -617, all of it in battle 124946, whose cascade also carries every other single-key loss. Flipped together on 2026-09-25.
STAGGER_WAIT.meaning: client16402_untargetable_immovable: while a member's deploy timer exceeds its own DeployTime, no attacker can target it and the move pass leaves it where it is (no walk, no separation push); it still stands in the way, so units that overlap it are pushed off it as today. When the wait ends it is an ordinary deploying unit. deploying: today's engine, the wait counted as part of the deploy, so a waiting member is targeted and pushed like any deploying unit.
STAGGER_WAIT.open: Whether a waiting member can be hit by a spell or knocked back or pulled: no corpus event puts one under a spell, so those paths keep today's behaviour under both arms. Whether a waiting member pushes the units it overlaps any differently from a deploying one: 7 corpus rows in 5 battles show a walker overlapped by a member that has just appeared moved by the whole overlap in one tick, purely away and with no walk step, where the engine gives the walk plus a push capped at 150; too few to ship. Whether a waiting member wakes a hidden building: unmeasured, and the engine's one definition of targetable decides it. A staggered summoned building (none in the corpus) is untargetable while it waits under the measured arm, by the same column: unmeasured.
STAGGER_WAIT.promotion_rules: SETTLED 2026-09-25 (see provenance). deploying, the earlier engine, is the old arm.
STAGGER_WAIT.engine: entity.rs stagger_ms (the wait, set from PendingSpawn.stagger_ms in formation_members and counted down beside deploy_ms in deploy_countdown); target.rs can_target (the one definition of targetable); state.rs phase_path16402 (the 16.402 move pass skips a waiting member after the pushback branch and applies a pull alone, as the held branch does); hashed only under the measured arm. The pre-2026 path models do not read it.

GROUND_DEPLOY_POINT.confidence: HIGH on both offsets for a GROUND summon and on their absence for a FLYING one; MEDIUM on which side of each axis KEYS them, because the corpus taps only three ground columns and the two readings of each key are not separable on the shipped map
GROUND_DEPLOY_POINT.provenance: MEASURED on the live 16.402 corpus. A summon's ring is symmetric about the point the game lays it on, so that point is recoverable from the members themselves: take the ring a card shows on a Blue right-half tap tile as canonical, then for every other clean tap-tile group solve for the single shift that carries it onto the truth. Over the corpus' clean ground groups that shift is never zero and over the clean air ones it always is. THE X OFFSET: a ground ring laid on the arena's LEFT half sits one native unit lower in absolute x -- 57 tap-tile groups at -1 on the left against 0 on the right, over Skeletons, Goblins, Spear Goblins, Barbarians, Goblin Gang, Skeleton Army and Skeleton Warriors, on BOTH seats. The Red Skeletons of capture 20260919-182539-A t927 tapped on (3500, 30500) stand their centre member on x 3499, while the Blue Skeletons of t532 tapped on (14500, 1500) stand theirs on 14500. It is the ABSOLUTE half and not the owner's: the Red Goblins of capture 20260918-122757.b1 t1676, tapped at x 10500, take no x offset although 10500 is their own-left. THE Y OFFSET: a ground ring owned by side 1 sits one native unit lower in absolute y, on either half -- the Skeletons' own-frame offsets read 808 / -402 for side 1 against 807 / -403 for side 0, and the Goblins' 762 against 761. It is the OWNER and not the arena's half: capture 20260918-122757.b1 t1676 is a side-1 deploy in the BOTTOM half and its recovered point is (10500, 11499) against a tile centre of 11500. That is the corpus' only group of its kind, which is why the confidence splits. FLYING TAKES NEITHER: the Minions of capture 20260920-071056-A tapped on (14500, 30500) -- side 1, and the rotation of a Blue (3500, 1500) tap -- carry offsets (+-499, 288) and (0, -579), the exact negation of side 0's (+-499, -288) and (0, 579), so their point is the tap itself in both axes. Air and ground run the same ring, the same lane classifier and the same seat rotation, so none of those can be what produces the offsets. BOTH ARE ON THE SPAWN POINT ONLY. A member carries them for the whole of its deploy state and leaves them behind on its first walking frame: the Red Skeleton of capture 20260919-182539-A t927 holds (3499, 29692) to t943 and reads 3456, 3398 and 3377 on the next three recorded frames. That is why the bit-exact walk never saw them. THE ENGINE lays the ring around the offset point, so the column clamp's own bounds are untouched: a clamped member still sits on the bound (formation.GROUND_Y_CLAMP's absolute 31000 and 17499) and an unclamped one now lands where the corpus puts it. The Red Goblins of capture 20260918-164951-B t2262 come out (2738, 31000), (2738, 29738), (4260, 29738), (4260, 31000) -- all four exact, against the (2739, 31000), (2739, 29739), (4261, 29739), (4261, 31000) the engine gave before.
GROUND_DEPLOY_POINT.meaning: client16402_one_unit: the two offsets above, on a GROUND member only. none: the ring is laid on the tap itself for every member, which is what a flying summon measures and what the engine did before -- one native unit off on every Red ground member and on every ground member of a left-half tap, its clamped members excepted. tests/common symmetric_config selects `none`, because the y offset is a seat asymmetry and the x offset is an absolute-frame one, and a rotation gate must not have either answering for the systems it measures.
GROUND_DEPLOY_POINT.promotion_rules: To HIGH on the KEYS as well as the offsets, each wanting a designed capture with every tower standing: (1) the X key -- the corpus taps only columns 3, 9 and 14 for a ground summon, and on the shipped map the arena's left half and the LANE_LEFT bit change at the same column, so 'the absolute left half' and 'the lane bit' are not separable here; a column whose lane bit and half disagree, or a map where they do, decides it. (2) The Y key rests on ONE group (20260918-122757.b1 t1676) for 'the owner' over 'the arena's top half'; a side-0 ground deploy in the top half, which needs an enemy princess tower down, decides it and the corpus holds none. (3) Whether the x test is on the DEPLOY POINT or on each member: every corpus ring is small enough to sit wholly on one side of the centre column, so a wide ring straddling it -- a Goblin Gang or a Skeleton Army tapped on the centre column -- would separate them; the engine tests the deploy point. (4) Whether a card with both ground and flying members takes the offset per member: no such card is in the slice, and the engine applies it per member.

GROUND_Y_CLAMP.provenance: MEASURED on the live 16.402 corpus, over EVERY clean multi-unit GROUND deploy the recordings hold (148 groups; the cleanliness rule of tools/make_formation_fixture.py over data/derived/replay/*.replay.json). The clamp bites on 19 of the 148, 18 of them on side 1, and where it bites the corpus separates all three candidates. SIDE 1, THE BACK EDGE: 32 members of 16 groups over 9 distinct battles stand on absolute y 31000 EXACTLY -- every one of them a Goblins rear pair tapped on absolute row 30, on both lanes (captures 20260918-164951-B and 20260918-164953-A t2262, 20260919-182539-A/B, 20260919-184136-A/B and 20260920-081819-A/B on (3500, 30500); 20260920-071056-A/B on (14500, 30500); 20260918-122757.b1 t962, 20260918-130203.b2 t2175 and 20260918-133849-A/B t1263 for the same deploy read as a centroid). Side 0's formula rotated puts that pair at 31261 (31130 for the centroid-read taps) and the `none` arm leaves it there: 32 members for the shipped value, 0 against. SIDE 1, THE RIVER: one clean group -- capture 20260918-121158 t2439 -- stands two Goblins on absolute y 17499 EXACTLY, where side 0's rotated bound is 17500. So side 1's river bound is one native unit FURTHER FORWARD than the rotation, not behind it. 2 members for, 0 against; the group's members are one native unit apart under the two arms, which the member tolerance of tests/formations.rs cannot see, so that test pins these two exactly. THE HALF-ARENA DROP: one clean group -- capture 20260918-122757.b1 t1676, a Red Goblins deploy in a column whose far princess tower had fallen -- stands its forward pair on absolute y 10738, unclamped; the same range undropped would have held them on 11499. SIDE 0 IS PINNED BY NOTHING. The only side-0 group the clamp bites (capture 20260918-130203.b2 t1397) puts its forward Skeleton on 14597, 97 native past the formula's 14500: that says a clamp acts, not where it is. And side 0's lo cannot be observed at all while it is at or below 250 native, because the bounds clamp holds every member it would have moved. Side 0's range is therefore the formula's output -- [0, 14500] on a column with both enemy princess towers standing -- and not an observation. THE RULE (state.rs `ground_y_range`): the tap's tile column is scanned over the rows a deploy of that card may use, and the pair is DROPPED when hi - lo >= 16000 native, half the arena (once a princess tower has fallen the column reaches past the river); every GROUND member's y is then clamped into it (flying units skip; y <= lo -> lo, else min(y, hi)). THE PAIR IS PER SIDE: side 0 takes lo = min(row x 1000) and hi = max(row x 1000 + 500) over its own-frame rows, side 1 takes lo = min(row x 1000 + 500) - 1 and hi = max(row x 1000) over ABSOLUTE rows, turned into the owner's frame. With every tower standing that is own-frame [0, 14500] for side 0 and own-frame [1000, 14501] -- absolute [17499, 31000] -- for side 1: a FULL ROW (1000 native) apart at the back edge and one native unit apart at the river, side 1's the looser of the two there. THE MASK is arena.rs `territory_zone` per tile centre with the card's own territory rule (the river band and the alive enemy towers' NoDeploySize rects), NOT the tilemap's NO_DEPLOY corner strips: the Goblin Gang tapped on (3500, 1500) stands a Spear Goblin on y 346 inside one (captures 20260920-090825-A/B t552). The owner's-frame arm keeps the seat-symmetry gates meaningful.
GROUND_Y_CLAMP.meaning: client16402_deploy_column_range: the measured per-side pair above. The two seats are NOT rotations of each other. At the BACK EDGE the bounds are a FULL ROW apart -- side 1's lo is the highest deployable row's near edge, side 0's rotated is the arena edge -- which the [250, H - 250] bounds clamp turns into at most 750 native on where a member actually lands (the Red Goblins of capture 20260918-164951-B t2262 stand on 31000, not the 31261 the rotation gives: 261 native on that deploy). At the RIVER the bounds are ONE native unit apart, side 1's the looser, and capture 20260918-121158 t2439 stands two Goblins on side 1's 17499 rather than the rotation's 17500. tests/common symmetric_config selects the next arm for the seat-symmetry gates, as it does for the absolute-grid search. deploy_column_range_own_frame: side 0's formula in the owner's frame for both seats, the seat-symmetric arm -- one native unit short of the measurement at the river and up to 750 short of it on a Red back-row deploy. none: no clamp; a ground member past the bank is ejected to the nearest passable ground (arena.rs nearest_passable_ground) like a spell release -- it agrees with the own-frame arm, so the same 34 clamped side-1 members refute both. WHAT IS MEASURED IS THE TWO ABSOLUTE BOUNDS (31000 and 17499); turning them into an own-frame pair needs a seat step that the corpus shows is itself one native unit out for a GROUND member. Over the tap-tile groups, a side-1 ground member's own-frame offsets are ONE LARGER than a side-0 member's of the same card -- Skeletons 808 / -402 against 807 / -403, Goblins 762 against 761 -- so a Red ground member's absolute y is one below the rotation of its Blue twin's. A FLYING member shows no such difference (Minions 579 / -288 on both seats). Read the two measured absolute bounds back through that one unit and side 1's own-frame pair is [999, 14500] against side 0's [0, 14500]: the RIVER bound comes out seat-symmetric and only the back edge stays asymmetric. So the `- 1` this arm carries in side 1's lo is one way to carry a difference that is on every Red ground member, clamped or not, and the pair of them is a decomposition of the measurement rather than the measurement.
GROUND_Y_CLAMP.promotion_rules: Stays measured: 34 clamped members over 17 clean groups separate the shipped pair from both other candidates, 0 against. What MEDIUM still records, each wanting a designed capture with every tower standing: (1) SIDE 0's range is carried by the formula alone -- its hi wants a three-summon ground card tapped on side 0's bank row on each lane, and its lo is unobservable while it is at or below 250 native because the bounds clamp covers it, so the entry says so rather than claiming it; (2) side 1's back edge is 16 groups of ONE card (Goblins) on ONE row (absolute 30) -- a second card and a second row on each lane; (3) side 1's river bound rests on a single group's two members, and that group's tap is a centroid -- a tap-tile-sourced group on the other lane hardens it; (4) the half-arena drop rests on one group, a side-1 deploy whose column had opened -- the side-0 direction is untested; (5) the mask agreeing with deploy_zone cell for cell on a corner tap of every card class. AND ONE THING THIS KEY CANNOT SETTLE: the two ABSOLUTE bounds are what the corpus shows; their split into an own-frame formula plus a seat step is not, because the seat step is one native unit out for a ground member on its own (see `meaning`). A SECOND one-unit effect says the same thing from outside this key's reach: a GROUND member deployed on the arena's LEFT half stands one native unit lower in absolute X than the same ring on the right half, on BOTH seats (Skeletons, Goblins, Spear Goblins, Barbarians, Goblin Gang, Skeleton Army, Skeleton Warriors: 57 tap-tile groups at -1 on the left, 0 on the right; Minions, Minion Horde and Skeleton Dragons show 0 on both). Both effects are on the SPAWN POINT only -- a member's track leaves them behind on its first walking frame -- and this clamp touches only y, so it can be neither's cause and can only be masking the y one. Settling them is a change to how a ground summon's point is laid, not to this key, and the `- 1` here must not be removed on its own: the two only cancel together.
